papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Wide Neural Networks: Risk Bound, Data Efficiency and Imperfect Teacher
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a strategy of training a student network with guide of the soft output from a teacher network. It has been a successful method of model compression and knowledge transfer. However, currently knowledge distillation lacks a convincing theoretical understanding. On the other hand, recent finding on neural tangent kernel enables us to approximate a wide neural network with a linear model of the network's random features. In this paper, we theoretically analyze the knowledge distillation of a wide neural network. First we provide a transfer risk bound for the linearized model of the network. Then we propose a metric of the task's training difficulty, called data inefficiency. Based on this metric, we show that for a perfect teacher, a high ratio of teacher's soft labels can be beneficial. Finally, for the case of imperfect teacher, we find that hard labels can correct teacher's wrong prediction, which explains the practice of mixing hard and soft labels.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: What is known about Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques provide practical ways to transfer predictive capacity from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models. The field encompasses simple soft-target matching as well as richer forms of transfer such as intermediate representation alignment, attention- or feature-level matching, multi-stage and multi-teacher pipelines, self-distillation, and data- or privacy-aware variants. Empirical work shows distilled students can approach teacher performance while offering large gains in latency, memory, and deployability; theoretical and empirical analyses emphasize mechanisms including soft-target regularization, representational alignment, and optimization dynamics. Practical success depends on careful choices of what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to use data (including synthetic or public data), and how to address robustness, fairness, and distributional shifts.

papers_seen.author: Reid
papers_seen.title: Why Knowledge Distillation Remains Central to Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach to compressing large deep learning models into smaller, faster, and often more deployable ones. When combined with targeted strategies—such as pre-training compact architectures, layer-level alignment, selective sample choices, careful data augmentation, and privacy-aware protocols—distillation can preserve most of the teacher's performance while meeting latency, memory, and deployment constraints. I argue that KD should be treated as a core component of any compression pipeline because it unifies improvements across accuracy, generalization, efficiency, and privacy without requiring wholesale re-engineering of tasks or architectures.

papers_seen.author: Mills
papers_seen.title: Why Knowledge Distillation Should Be the Central Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, adaptable technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of their performance. When combined with careful pre-training of compact architectures, representation-level transfer, augmentation or synthesized data, and orthogonal compression methods (pruning, quantization), KD delivers strong trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy. However, realizing those gains in practice requires attention to optimization dynamics, data availability, privacy, and known failure modes (e.g., low-frequency token degradation), and so KD should be applied as part of an integrated, responsible compression pipeline.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Distilling portable Generative Adversarial Networks for Image Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been widely used in various image-to-image translation tasks, they can be hardly applied on mobile devices due to their heavy computation and storage cost. Traditional network compression methods focus on visually recognition tasks, but never deal with generation tasks. Inspired by knowledge distillation, a student generator of fewer parameters is trained by inheriting the low-level and high-level information from the original heavy teacher generator. To promote the capability of student generator, we include a student discriminator to measure the distances between real images, and images generated by student and teacher generators. An adversarial learning process is therefore established to optimize student generator and student discriminator. Qualitative and quantitative analysis by conducting experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method can learn portable generative models with strong performance.

papers_seen.author: Wong
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Principled Path to Efficient, Adaptable, and Responsible NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is not merely a compression trick but a general framework that enables smaller or specialized models to inherit useful behaviors from larger teachers while controlling generalization, efficiency, and social impact. When combined with layer-wise and representation-level matching, task-aware architecture search, thoughtful input augmentation, and deployment-aware protocols, KD supports high-performance, resource-frugal NLP systems that can be adapted to heterogeneous devices and sensitive application contexts.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Multi-Level Branched Regularization for Federated Learning
papers_seen.abstract: A critical challenge of federated learning is data heterogeneity and imbalance across clients, which leads to inconsistency between local networks and unstable convergence of global models. To alleviate the limitations, we propose a novel architectural regularization technique that constructs multiple auxiliary branches in each local model by grafting local and global subnetworks at several different levels and that learns the representations of the main pathway in the local model congruent to the auxiliary hybrid pathways via online knowledge distillation. The proposed technique is effective to robustify the global model even in the non-iid setting and is applicable to various federated learning frameworks conveniently without incurring extra communication costs. We perform comprehensive empirical studies and demonstrate remarkable performance gains in terms of accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods. The source code is available at our project page.

papers_seen.author: Maldonado
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge by Mimicking Features
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a popular method to train efficient networks ("student") with the help of high-capacity networks ("teacher"). Traditional methods use the teacher's soft logits as extra supervision to train the student network. In this paper, we argue that it is more advantageous to make the student mimic the teacher's features in the penultimate layer. Not only the student can directly learn more effective information from the teacher feature, feature mimicking can also be applied for teachers trained without a softmax layer. Experiments show that it can achieve higher accuracy than traditional KD. To further facilitate feature mimicking, we decompose a feature vector into the magnitude and the direction. We argue that the teacher should give more freedom to the student feature's magnitude, and let the student pay more attention on mimicking the feature direction. To meet this requirement, we propose a loss term based on locality-sensitive hashing (LSH). With the help of this new loss, our method indeed mimics feature directions more accurately, relaxes constraints on feature magnitudes, and achieves state-of-the-art distillation accuracy. We provide theoretical analyses of how LSH facilitates feature direction mimicking, and further extend feature mimicking to multi-label recognition and object detection.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression strategies enable smaller, faster models to inherit performance from larger teachers by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or ensemble knowledge. Techniques range from logit-based soft-target distillation to feature- and attention-level mimicry, multi-teacher and task-adaptive pipelines, and methods that relax the need for original training data or strong teachers. Across computer vision and natural language processing tasks, distilled students can approach teacher accuracy while drastically reducing parameters and latency; complementary strategies such as careful pre-training of compact models and architecture search further improve trade-offs between efficiency and effectiveness. Key challenges remain in preserving rare-token behavior, aligning heterogeneous teacher–student inputs, and ensuring privacy and robustness during compression.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Insights
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques enable deployment of large deep models by transferring knowledge to smaller, faster, or lower-precision models. Existing work spans pre-training compact models, teacher-to-student soft-target transfer, data-free and teacher-free approaches, self-distillation, architecture- and task-specific adaptations, and combinations with quantization or pruning. Empirical results show that distilled students can approach teacher performance across classification, ranking, speech, and generation tasks, while specialized strategies address limited task data, privacy constraints, and heterogeneous deployment settings. Open challenges include handling domain shift, designing teacher-student curricula, and developing universally effective objectives for diverse architectures and tasks.

papers_seen.author: Owens
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses capability from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. It encompasses methods that transfer final outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure, or training curricula, and it is applied across modalities (vision, language, scene synthesis, and optimization tasks). KD delivers practical gains in inference speed, memory footprint, and often generalization or robustness when paired with complementary techniques (data augmentation, architecture design, and adversarial training), but its success depends on choices about what is transferred, how data are used or synthesized, and how teacher and student capacities are aligned.

papers_seen.author: Zuniga
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Composable Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable and practical technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, and more deployable student models. KD is effective across modalities (vision, speech, language, graphs) and settings (task-specific compression, data-limited or data-free transfer), and its strengths are amplified when combined with complementary methods such as architecture-aware replacement, pruning, low-precision numerics, adaptive teacher design, and careful input-side practices. To realize robust and fair compressed models, practitioners should treat KD as one tool within a pipeline: design student-friendly teachers, account for data constraints, use augmentation and curriculum where helpful, and combine KD with orthogonal compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Nguyen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical and Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students. Across vision, speech, graph, and language tasks, KD enables substantial reductions in memory and inference cost while retaining much of the teacher's performance. However, KD is not a silver bullet: its effectiveness depends on choices of teacher/student architecture, what is distilled (logits, layers, attention, representations), the optimization and data used for distillation, and constraints such as privacy or fairness. Carefully combining KD with techniques like multi-teacher schedules, layer-mapping strategies, task-adaptive compression, and privacy-preserving perturbations yields the best trade-offs for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Mahoney
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context-Sensitive Path to Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, flexible technique for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models by transferring information from larger teacher models to compact student models. When combined with feature-level objectives, architectural transformations, teacher optimization, and data strategies, KD can recover much of a teacher's performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, its success depends on task and domain specifics, teacher quality, student capacity, and data availability; therefore, practitioners should treat KD as a toolbox to be adapted—not a single recipe—to obtain reliable compression in real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Hawkins
papers_seen.title: A Fast Knowledge Distillation Framework for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: While Knowledge Distillation (KD) has been recognized as a useful tool in many visual tasks, such as supervised classification and self-supervised representation learning, the main drawback of a vanilla KD framework is its mechanism, which consumes the majority of the computational overhead on forwarding through the giant teacher networks, making the entire learning procedure inefficient and costly. ReLabel, a recently proposed solution, suggests creating a label map for the entire image. During training, it receives the cropped region-level label by RoI aligning on a pre-generated entire label map, allowing for efficient supervision generation without having to pass through the teachers many times. However, as the KD teachers are from conventional multi-crop training, there are various mismatches between the global label-map and region-level label in this technique, resulting in performance deterioration. In this study, we present a Fast Knowledge Distillation (FKD) framework that replicates the distillation training phase and generates soft labels using the multi-crop KD approach, while training faster than ReLabel since no post-processes such as RoI align and softmax operations are used. When conducting multi-crop in the same image for data loading, our FKD is even more efficient than the traditional image classification framework. On ImageNet-1K, we obtain 79.8% with ResNet-50, outperforming ReLabel by ~1.0% while being faster. On the self-supervised learning task, we also show that FKD has an efficiency advantage. Our project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/FKD/index.html, source code and models are available at: https://github.com/szq0214/FKD.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical and Flexible Path to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large models into smaller, faster ones while retaining much of their performance. Beyond simple teacher-student logit matching, effective KD approaches exploit feature-level mimicking, task-aware layer selection, meta-learned teachers, online distillation for large-scale training, and task-adaptive model search. When applied thoughtfully — choosing the right supervision signal (logits vs. features), shaping teacher behavior to be student-friendly, and matching distillation to deployment constraints — KD can deliver strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across vision and language tasks, improve robustness, and enable practical deployment of pretrained models in resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Distilled Semantics for Comprehensive Scene Understanding from Videos
papers_seen.abstract: Whole understanding of the surroundings is paramount to autonomous systems. Recent works have shown that deep neural networks can learn geometry (depth) and motion (optical flow) from a monocular video without any explicit supervision from ground truth annotations, particularly hard to source for these two tasks. In this paper, we take an additional step toward holistic scene understanding with monocular cameras by learning depth and motion alongside with semantics, with supervision for the latter provided by a pre-trained network distilling proxy ground truth images. We address the three tasks jointly by a) a novel training protocol based on knowledge distillation and self-supervision and b) a compact network architecture which enables efficient scene understanding on both power hungry GPUs and low-power embedded platforms. We thoroughly assess the performance of our framework and show that it yields state-of-the-art results for monocular depth estimation, optical flow and motion segmentation.

papers_seen.author: Hurst
papers_seen.title: Ranking Distillation: Learning Compact Ranking Models With High Performance for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel way to train ranking models, such as recommender systems, that are both effective and efficient. Knowledge distillation (KD) was shown to be successful in image recognition to achieve both effectiveness and efficiency. We propose a KD technique for learning to rank problems, called \emph{ranking distillation (RD)}. Specifically, we train a smaller student model to learn to rank documents/items from both the training data and the supervision of a larger teacher model. The student model achieves a similar ranking performance to that of the large teacher model, but its smaller model size makes the online inference more efficient. RD is flexible because it is orthogonal to the choices of ranking models for the teacher and student. We address the challenges of RD for ranking problems. The experiments on public data sets and state-of-the-art recommendation models showed that RD achieves its design purposes: the student model learnt with RD has a model size less than half of the teacher model while achieving a ranking performance similar to the teacher model and much better than the student model learnt without RD.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Beyond Soft Labels: A Practical Position on Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a crucial technique for shrinking large deep models to meet real-world latency, memory and privacy constraints while retaining much of their performance. However, naive distillation that only matches teacher soft-labels is often insufficient. A more reliable strategy combines distillation of internal representations and features, task- or domain-adaptive compression, and architecture-aware search or adaptation. When applied with care — addressing optimization issues, data or privacy limits, and mismatch between teacher and student capacities — distillation enables compact, fast models that approach teacher performance across speech, NLP and vision tasks.

papers_seen.author: Mayo
papers_seen.title: Rethinking Soft Labels for Knowledge Distillation: A Bias-Variance Tradeoff Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective approach to leverage a well-trained network or an ensemble of them, named as the teacher, to guide the training of a student network. The outputs from the teacher network are used as soft labels for supervising the training of a new network. Recent studies \citep{muller2019does,yuan2020revisiting} revealed an intriguing property of the soft labels that making labels soft serves as a good regularization to the student network. From the perspective of statistical learning, regularization aims to reduce the variance, however how bias and variance change is not clear for training with soft labels. In this paper, we investigate the bias-variance tradeoff brought by distillation with soft labels. Specifically, we observe that during training the bias-variance tradeoff varies sample-wisely. Further, under the same distillation temperature setting, we observe that the distillation performance is negatively associated with the number of some specific samples, which are named as regularization samples since these samples lead to bias increasing and variance decreasing. Nevertheless, we empirically find that completely filtering out regularization samples also deteriorates distillation performance. Our discoveries inspired us to propose the novel weighted soft labels to help the network adaptively handle the sample-wise bias-variance tradeoff. Experiments on standard evaluation benchmarks validate the effectiveness of our method. Our code is available at \url{https://github.com/bellymonster/Weighted-Soft-Label-Distillation}.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Improved Accuracy in Spoken Question Answering
papers_seen.abstract: Spoken question answering (SQA) is a challenging task that requires the machine to fully understand the complex spoken documents. Automatic speech recognition (ASR) plays a significant role in the development of QA systems. However, the recent work shows that ASR systems generate highly noisy transcripts, which critically limit the capability of machine comprehension on the SQA task. To address the issue, we present a novel distillation framework. Specifically, we devise a training strategy to perform knowledge distillation (KD) from spoken documents and written counterparts. Our work makes a step towards distilling knowledge from the language model as a supervision signal to lead to better student accuracy by reducing the misalignment between automatic and manual transcriptions. Experiments demonstrate that our approach outperforms several state-of-the-art language models on the Spoken-SQuAD dataset.

papers_seen.author: Larson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from larger teacher models to smaller students to reduce inference cost, memory, and latency while preserving performance. Methods extend beyond matching soft output logits to include intermediate feature/representation matching, layer-wise alignment, adversarial or curriculum-driven sample selection, and data-free or privacy-aware synthesis. Distillation is widely applicable across modalities (vision, speech, language, multimodal) and use cases (on-device deployment, federated learning, low-precision inference), but success depends on careful choices about which signals to transfer, how to handle data availability or heterogeneity, and how to align teacher and student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Callahan
papers_seen.title: A Practical Position on Knowledge Distillation: Go Beyond Soft Labels
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a necessary tool for compressing large deep and NLP models into efficient students suitable for deployment. However, naive KD that only matches teacher soft-labels is often insufficient. Effective distillation combines richer knowledge targets (internal features, attention, and layerwise signals), data-aware augmentations, selective sample strategies, and privacy- or domain-aware procedures. The best practical pipelines treat KD as a toolbox: choose which knowledge to transfer based on student capacity and task needs, use augmentation or self-distillation to improve generalization when data are scarce, and apply selective or privacy-preserving queries where constraints require it.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Design Principles
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely applicable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. KD achieves favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across modalities when practitioners choose what form of teacher knowledge to transfer, how to map layers and representations, and how to handle limited or private data. However, KD is not plug-and-play: outcomes depend heavily on teacher quality, distilled signals, data availability, and task-specific constraints. Thoughtful combination of feature-level objectives, task-aware layer selection, data-synthesis or privacy-preserving queries, and targeted curricula yields robust compressed models ready for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Wong
papers_seen.title: Embracing the Dark Knowledge: Domain Generalization Using Regularized Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Though convolutional neural networks are widely used in different tasks, lack of generalization capability in the absence of sufficient and representative data is one of the challenges that hinder their practical application. In this paper, we propose a simple, effective, and plug-and-play training strategy named Knowledge Distillation for Domain Generalization (KDDG) which is built upon a knowledge distillation framework with the gradient filter as a novel regularization term. We find that both the ``richer dark knowledge" from the teacher network, as well as the gradient filter we proposed, can reduce the difficulty of learning the mapping which further improves the generalization ability of the model. We also conduct experiments extensively to show that our framework can significantly improve the generalization capability of deep neural networks in different tasks including image classification, segmentation, reinforcement learning by comparing our method with existing state-of-the-art domain generalization techniques. Last but not the least, we propose to adopt two metrics to analyze our proposed method in order to better understand how our proposed method benefits the generalization capability of deep neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Liu
papers_seen.title: Enabling Multimodal Generation on CLIP via Vision-Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The recent large-scale vision-language pre-training (VLP) of dual-stream architectures (e.g., CLIP) with a tremendous amount of image-text pair data, has shown its superiority on various multimodal alignment tasks. Despite its success, the resulting models are not capable of multimodal generative tasks due to the weak text encoder. To tackle this problem, we propose to augment the dual-stream VLP model with a textual pre-trained language model (PLM) via vision-language knowledge distillation (VLKD), enabling the capability for multimodal generation. VLKD is pretty data- and computation-efficient compared to the pre-training from scratch. Experimental results show that the resulting model has strong zero-shot performance on multimodal generation tasks, such as open-ended visual question answering and image captioning. For example, it achieves 44.5% zero-shot accuracy on the VQAv2 dataset, surpassing the previous state-of-the-art zero-shot model with $7\times$ fewer parameters. Furthermore, the original textual language understanding and generation ability of the PLM is maintained after VLKD, which makes our model versatile for both multimodal and unimodal tasks.

papers_seen.author: Powell
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from larger, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models so that students retain much of teacher performance while reducing computational cost. The literature characterizes KD methods at multiple granularities (final logits, intermediate features, attention or layer mappings, and module- or task-level transfer), documents practical recipes and failure modes, and explores extensions for data-free settings, robustness, and specialized tasks (e.g., machine translation, detection). Empirical and theoretical work shows KD is a flexible tool that benefits from careful choices in distilled signals, data/augmentation strategies, and teacher-student alignment; however, limitations remain around optimization, low-frequency phenomena, data availability, and architecture mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression seek to transfer performance and desirable properties from large, expensive models to smaller, efficient ones. The literature spans techniques that match outputs (soft labels), intermediate representations, or training dynamics; methods that operate with or without access to original data; and approaches that adapt compression to tasks, modalities, or deployment constraints. Empirical results show that discriminative matching of representations, careful layer mappings, adversarial data synthesis, and task-aware architecture search all improve the trade-offs between size, speed, and accuracy in both vision and language settings. Practical developments also emphasize teacher design, robustness transfer, and strategies for low-data or privacy-constrained scenarios.

papers_seen.author: West
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically proven toolkit for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across vision and NLP. KD preserves much of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and communication costs, and it integrates naturally with feature-level matching, data-free synthesis, online and federated protocols, and teacher-design strategies. However, its effectiveness depends on what is distilled (logits, features, attention), data availability and domain match, teacher–student capacity alignment, and objectives like robustness, privacy, and fairness. Real-world deployment requires matching distillation techniques to constraints and explicitly addressing robustness, bias, and data-privacy tradeoffs.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Extensions, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. Research over the past decade has expanded KD from simple teacher–student logit matching to a rich set of strategies that address data availability, privacy, distributed settings, architecture mismatches, and task-specific compression needs. Advances include data-free and zero-shot distillation, federated and privacy-aware distillation, representational and layer-mapping techniques for pre-trained language models, and practical combinations with quantization and architecture search to enable deployment on resource-constrained devices.

Experiments show that it can achieve higher accuracy than traditional KD. To further facilitate feature mimicking, we decompose a feature vector into the magnitude and the direction. We argue that the teacher should give more freedom to the student feature\'s magnitude, and let the student pay more attention on mimicking the feature direction. To meet this requirement, we propose a loss term based on locality-sensitive hashing (LSH). With the help of this new loss, our method indeed mimics feature directions more accurately, relaxes constraints on feature magnitudes, and achieves state-of-the-art distillation accuracy. We provide theoretical analyses of how LSH facilitates feature direction mimicking, and further extend feature mimicking to multi-label recognition and object detection.'}, {'author': 'Herrera', 'year': 2023, 'title': 'Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis', 'abstract': 'Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression strategies enable smaller, faster models to inherit performance from larger teachers by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or ensemble knowledge. papers_seen.author: Roman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Tool for Practical Model Compression in NLP and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-purpose strategy for compressing large deep models while preserving performance. KD can be adapted to constraints common in NLP deployment—limited compute, privacy restrictions, low-latency requirements, and robustness demands—by pairing standard teacher-student training with techniques such as feature-level matching, data augmentation, multi-teacher supervision, and teacher adaptation. Across domains (transformers for NLP, speech embeddings, graph models, generative models), KD consistently enables large reductions in model size or latency with modest accuracy loss, making it a primary method for productionization of deep models.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: What We Know
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical suite of techniques that transfers information from large teacher models to smaller students to enable efficient deployment. In practice KD spans matching teacher outputs (soft logits), aligning intermediate representations, specialized layer- and channel-level transfers, and workflows that combine distillation with pruning, quantization, or synthetic-data strategies. KD delivers substantial reductions in compute, memory, and latency while often improving student generalization, but its success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity, and how to handle data or domain shifts. Open issues include robustness under distributional heterogeneity, preserving rare-token or fine-grained behavior in sequence models, and distillation without original training data.

papers_seen.author: Mcclain
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multi-Modal Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an essential and versatile approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable models across NLP and vision domains. When adapted to task and deployment constraints—via multi-teacher schedules, feature-level objectives, data-free synthesis, online protocols, or privacy-aware ensembles—KD both preserves quality and addresses communication, privacy, and compute bottlenecks. However, KD is not a panacea: dataset heterogeneity and optimization mismatches can limit its effectiveness, so careful method selection and engineering are required for robust compression in real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Efficient Transformer-based Large Scale Language Representations using Hardware-friendly Block Structured Pruning
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained large-scale language models have increasingly demonstrated high accuracy on many natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, the limited weight storage and computational speed on hardware platforms have impeded the popularity of pre-trained models, especially in the era of edge computing. In this work, we propose an efficient transformer-based large-scale language representation using hardware-friendly block structure pruning. We incorporate the reweighted group Lasso into block-structured pruning for optimization. Besides the significantly reduced weight storage and computation, the proposed approach achieves high compression rates. Experimental results on different models (BERT, RoBERTa, and DistilBERT) on the General Language Understanding Evaluation (GLUE) benchmark tasks show that we achieve up to 5.0x with zero or minor accuracy degradation on certain task(s). Our proposed method is also orthogonal to existing compact pre-trained language models such as DistilBERT using knowledge distillation, since a further 1.79x average compression rate can be achieved on top of DistilBERT with zero or minor accuracy degradation. It is suitable to deploy the final compressed model on resource-constrained edge devices.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Apprentice: Using Knowledge Distillation Techniques To Improve Low-Precision Network Accuracy
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning networks have achieved state-of-the-art accuracies on computer vision workloads like image classification and object detection. The performant systems, however, typically involve big models with numerous parameters. Once trained, a challenging aspect for such top performing models is deployment on resource constrained inference systems - the models (often deep networks or wide networks or both) are compute and memory intensive. Low-precision numerics and model compression using knowledge distillation are popular techniques to lower both the compute requirements and memory footprint of these deployed models. In this paper, we study the combination of these two techniques and show that the performance of low-precision networks can be significantly improved by using knowledge distillation techniques. Our approach, Apprentice, achieves state-of-the-art accuracies using ternary precision and 4-bit precision for variants of ResNet architecture on ImageNet dataset. We present three schemes using which one can apply knowledge distillation techniques to various stages of the train-and-deploy pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Reid
papers_seen.title: Why Knowledge Distillation Remains Central to Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach to compressing large deep learning models into smaller, faster, and often more deployable ones. When combined with targeted strategies—such as pre-training compact architectures, layer-level alignment, selective sample choices, careful data augmentation, and privacy-aware protocols—distillation can preserve most of the teacher's performance while meeting latency, memory, and deployment constraints. I argue that KD should be treated as a core component of any compression pipeline because it unifies improvements across accuracy, generalization, efficiency, and privacy without requiring wholesale re-engineering of tasks or architectures.

papers_seen.author: Shaw
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical Tool for Model Compression in NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their performance. KD works across modalities and tasks, and its effectiveness depends on matching distillation techniques to data and deployment constraints. When combined with careful model and data design, KD enables practical deployment of advanced models under latency, memory, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Cohen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Strategy for Model Compression and Adaptation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach to produce compact models that retain much of the performance of larger models. Beyond simple compression, KD can transfer inductive biases, enable domain adaptation and vocabulary specialization, support privacy-preserving and federated scenarios, work without access to original data, and improve robustness and feature quality when carefully applied. When combined with targeted techniques — feature mimicking, weighted soft labels, projector layers, or adversarial robustness objectives — KD becomes a unifying toolkit to meet latency, capacity, and privacy constraints in real-world NLP and deep learning deployments.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, widely applicable strategy for producing compact, deployable models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. KD works across modalities and deployment constraints, and supports extensions for data-free, federated, and privacy-sensitive settings. However, realizing KD’s full potential requires careful choices about what signals to transfer (logits, features, relational signals), how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to mitigate transferred harms such as bias or degraded rare-token behavior. When combined with complementary methods (augmentation, layer-aware mapping, multi-teacher ensembles, or differential-privacy mechanisms), KD becomes a flexible core of effective compression pipelines for real-world NLP and deep-learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Hickman
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques aim to transfer the predictive power of large, expensive models into smaller, faster models while retaining performance. Approaches vary from matching teacher outputs (soft labels) to aligning intermediate representations, leveraging data augmentation or synthesized data when real data are limited, and jointly optimizing architecture and distillation losses for task-adaptive compression. Advances address student–teacher capacity gaps, multi-teacher transfer, and domain or data scarcity; remaining challenges include transferring internal structure efficiently, generalization under distribution shifts, and designing teacher models that are optimized for downstream distillation.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Feature-map-level Online Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Feature maps contain rich information about image intensity and spatial correlation. However, previous online knowledge distillation methods only utilize the class probabilities. Thus in this paper, we propose an online knowledge distillation method that transfers not only the knowledge of the class probabilities but also that of the feature map using the adversarial training framework. We train multiple networks simultaneously by employing discriminators to distinguish the feature map distributions of different networks. Each network has its corresponding discriminator which discriminates the feature map from its own as fake while classifying that of the other network as real. By training a network to fool the corresponding discriminator, it can learn the other network's feature map distribution. We show that our method performs better than the conventional direct alignment method such as L1 and is more suitable for online distillation. Also, we propose a novel cyclic learning scheme for training more than two networks together. We have applied our method to various network architectures on the classification task and discovered a significant improvement of performance especially in the case of training a pair of a small network and a large one.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Is Label Smoothing Truly Incompatible with Knowledge Distillation: An Empirical Study
papers_seen.abstract: This work aims to empirically clarify a recently discovered perspective that label smoothing is incompatible with knowledge distillation. We begin by introducing the motivation behind on how this incompatibility is raised, i.e., label smoothing erases relative information between teacher logits. We provide a novel connection on how label smoothing affects distributions of semantically similar and dissimilar classes. Then we propose a metric to quantitatively measure the degree of erased information in sample's representation. After that, we study its one-sidedness and imperfection of the incompatibility view through massive analyses, visualizations and comprehensive experiments on Image Classification, Binary Networks, and Neural Machine Translation. Finally, we broadly discuss several circumstances wherein label smoothing will indeed lose its effectiveness. Project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/LS_and_KD/index.html.

papers_seen.author: Gardner
papers_seen.title: Adversarially Robust Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is effective for producing small, high-performance neural networks for classification, but these small networks are vulnerable to adversarial attacks. This paper studies how adversarial robustness transfers from teacher to student during knowledge distillation. We find that a large amount of robustness may be inherited by the student even when distilled on only clean images. Second, we introduce Adversarially Robust Distillation (ARD) for distilling robustness onto student networks. In addition to producing small models with high test accuracy like conventional distillation, ARD also passes the superior robustness of large networks onto the student. In our experiments, we find that ARD student models decisively outperform adversarially trained networks of identical architecture in terms of robust accuracy, surpassing state-of-the-art methods on standard robustness benchmarks. Finally, we adapt recent fast adversarial training methods to ARD for accelerated robust distillation.

papers_seen.author: Brennan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring learned behavior beyond hard labels. Over the past decade KD has evolved from logit-matching to a broad toolkit that includes representation- and feature-level imitation, flexible layer mappings, task-aware architecture search, and strategies for data-limited or deployment-constrained settings. Combining these techniques with careful teacher selection, sample or objective weighting, and deployment-aware choices (e.g., low-precision or privacy-preserving protocols) yields compact models that often retain much of the teacher's utility while meeting latency and resource constraints.

papers_seen.author: Suarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Path to Compact Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, practical approach for turning large, high-performing deep models into smaller, faster models suitable for real-world deployment. Beyond pure compression, KD serves as a flexible training paradigm that can be combined with pre-training, privacy-preserving workflows, and architecture-aware mimicry to preserve task performance while meeting latency, memory, and device constraints. A pragmatic KD pipeline aligns the choice of distillation signal, teacher design, student pretraining, and data strategy to the deployment context.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Online Knowledge Distillation via Mutual Contrastive Learning for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: The teacher-free online Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to train an ensemble of multiple student models collaboratively and distill knowledge from each other. Although existing online KD methods achieve desirable performance, they often focus on class probabilities as the core knowledge type, ignoring the valuable feature representational information. We present a Mutual Contrastive Learning (MCL) framework for online KD. The core idea of MCL is to perform mutual interaction and transfer of contrastive distributions among a cohort of networks in an online manner. Our MCL can aggregate cross-network embedding information and maximize the lower bound to the mutual information between two networks. This enables each network to learn extra contrastive knowledge from others, leading to better feature representations, thus improving the performance of visual recognition tasks. Beyond the final layer, we extend MCL to intermediate layers and perform an adaptive layer-matching mechanism trained by meta-optimization. Experiments on image classification and transfer learning to visual recognition tasks show that layer-wise MCL can lead to consistent performance gains against state-of-the-art online KD approaches. The superiority demonstrates that layer-wise MCL can guide the network to generate better feature representations. Our code is publicly avaliable at https://github.com/winycg/L-MCL.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques reduce the size, memory, and inference cost of large neural networks by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models. Across tasks and modalities—classification, detection, generative modeling, retrieval, and NLP—research has developed logits-based, feature-based, and task-adapted distillation strategies, multi-teacher and ensemble approaches, privacy- and communication-conscious protocols for distributed settings, and teacher-optimization/meta-learning variants. These methods trade off fidelity to teacher behavior with student capacity, expose failure modes (e.g., transfer of low-frequency lexical mistakes or overfitting of student features), and introduce remedies such as selective sample distillation, feature projectors, adversarially-informed samples, and staged or multi-teacher curricula. While KD consistently improves compact models compared to training from scratch and enables deployment on resource-constrained platforms, open issues remain in robustness, task-specific alignment, and distillation under data heterogeneity.

papers_seen.author: Munoz
papers_seen.title: Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation in Deep Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation deals with the problem of training a smaller model (Student) from a high capacity source model (Teacher) so as to retain most of its performance. Existing approaches use either the training data or meta-data extracted from it in order to train the Student. However, accessing the dataset on which the Teacher has been trained may not always be feasible if the dataset is very large or it poses privacy or safety concerns (e.g., bio-metric or medical data). Hence, in this paper, we propose a novel data-free method to train the Student from the Teacher. Without even using any meta-data, we synthesize the Data Impressions from the complex Teacher model and utilize these as surrogates for the original training data samples to transfer its learning to Student via knowledge distillation. We, therefore, dub our method "Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation" and demonstrate that our framework results in competitive generalization performance as achieved by distillation using the actual training data samples on multiple benchmark datasets.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Compressing Visual-linguistic Model via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite exciting progress in pre-training for visual-linguistic (VL) representations, very few aspire to a small VL model. In this paper, we study knowledge distillation (KD) to effectively compress a transformer-based large VL model into a small VL model. The major challenge arises from the inconsistent regional visual tokens extracted from different detectors of Teacher and Student, resulting in the misalignment of hidden representations and attention distributions. To address the problem, we retrain and adapt the Teacher by using the same region proposals from Student's detector while the features are from Teacher's own object detector. With aligned network inputs, the adapted Teacher is capable of transferring the knowledge through the intermediate representations. Specifically, we use the mean square error loss to mimic the attention distribution inside the transformer block and present a token-wise noise contrastive loss to align the hidden state by contrasting with negative representations stored in a sample queue. To this end, we show that our proposed distillation significantly improves the performance of small VL models on image captioning and visual question answering tasks. It reaches 120.8 in CIDEr score on COCO captioning, an improvement of 5.1 over its non-distilled counterpart; and an accuracy of 69.8 on VQA 2.0, a 0.8 gain from the baseline. Our extensive experiments and ablations confirm the effectiveness of VL distillation in both pre-training and fine-tuning stages.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques reduce computation, memory and latency of large deep models by transferring information from high-capacity "teacher" models to smaller "student" models. A range of approaches have been developed: soft-target (logit) distillation, feature- and layer-wise matching, data-augmentation and data-free synthesis, multi-teacher and curriculum strategies, and teacher-aware or teacher-training modifications. These methods are applied across modalities (NLP, vision, multimodal) and settings (limited data, federated or resource-constrained deployments), and combine naturally with quantization and low-precision inference. Empirical and theoretical work shows gains arise both from conveying inter-class similarities (dark knowledge) and from the regularization effect of softened targets; more recent work focuses on selecting or synthesizing the most useful knowledge for a given student and task.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a heuristic for compressing large models into a broadly applicable set of techniques that enable smaller, faster, and in some cases fairer or more interpretable models. Its effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer (logits, features, structure), how to prepare training data, and how to reconcile teacher imperfections with student capacity. When these design choices are matched to the task and constraints, KD enables substantial compression with small performance loss and can address privacy and resource limitations.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Robust Cross-Modal Representation Learning with Progressive Self-Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The learning objective of vision-language approach of CLIP does not effectively account for the noisy many-to-many correspondences found in web-harvested image captioning datasets, which contributes to its compute and data inefficiency. To address this challenge, we introduce a novel training framework based on cross-modal contrastive learning that uses progressive self-distillation and soft image-text alignments to more efficiently learn robust representations from noisy data. Our model distills its own knowledge to dynamically generate soft-alignment targets for a subset of images and captions in every minibatch, which are then used to update its parameters. Extensive evaluation across 14 benchmark datasets shows that our method consistently outperforms its CLIP counterpart in multiple settings, including: (a) zero-shot classification, (b) linear probe transfer, and (c) image-text retrieval, without incurring added computational cost. Analysis using an ImageNet-based robustness test-bed reveals that our method offers better effective robustness to natural distribution shifts compared to both ImageNet-trained models and CLIP itself. Lastly, pretraining with datasets spanning two orders of magnitude in size shows that our improvements over CLIP tend to scale with number of training examples.

papers_seen.author: Higgins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Context-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable approach for compressing large models into smaller ones that meet deployment constraints. KD reduces storage, latency, and energy while preserving much of teacher performance, but its success depends on what knowledge is transferred, how teacher signals are generated and trusted, and how distillation is combined with other compression methods and fairness or robustness constraints. Effective deployment requires task-aware decisions about targets (logits vs. features), data (original, augmented, or synthetic), architectural alignment, and additional safeguards for bias and domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Cowan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical Tool for Compressing Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical method for transferring predictive behavior from large, expensive teacher models into smaller, faster student models so they meet real-world latency, memory, and deployment constraints. When combined with complementary techniques (pre-training compact students, layer-aware transfer, data synthesis or selective raw-data exposure), KD can preserve most of a teacher's performance while substantially reducing computational cost. However, distillation must be designed carefully: choices about what to transfer, how to supply or synthesize training data, and how to align teacher and student shape outcomes in accuracy, robustness, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Zamora
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, cheaper students by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. The family of KD methods includes soft-target (logit) matching, feature- and layer-wise alignment, relational and module-level transfer, data-free or zero-shot synthesis, and integration with architecture search or federated training. Practical deployments balance what is transferred with student capacity, data availability, privacy constraints, and device heterogeneity; empirical work shows KD often preserves much of teacher performance while enabling lower latency, smaller models, and domain specialization, but open challenges remain around robustness, domain shift, and principled selection of distilled signals.

papers_seen.author: Montoya
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of methods for transferring behavior from large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster student models so they can be deployed under real-world constraints. Approaches vary in what is transferred (soft outputs, internal features, attention maps, module behavior), whether distillation is offline, online, or federated, and how it is combined with architecture search, pruning, or privacy mechanisms. Empirically, KD routinely improves compact models over training from scratch and enables deployments across on-device, distributed, and data-scarce settings; however, practical success depends on aligning distillation signals to student capacity, handling imperfect or heterogeneous teachers, and addressing data and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer predictive behavior and internal structure from larger, often pre-trained teacher models into smaller, efficient student models in order to reduce latency, memory, and deployment cost while retaining task performance. Methods span matching soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, attention- or relation-based feature matching, curriculum strategies for progressively harder supervision, and task- or data-aware architecture search. Practical success depends on student capacity, availability and quality of data, whether the student itself is pre-trained, and choices about what to transfer; open challenges include preserving fairness and robustness, aligning heterogeneous architectures, and operating under privacy or data-limited conditions.

papers_seen.author: Koch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques aim to transfer useful knowledge from larger, expensive models to smaller, more efficient ones so that deployed systems retain high performance under resource constraints. Approaches span logit-level supervision, feature- and layer-level matching, progressive module replacement, and data-augmentation or data-free strategies. Applications include compressing large language models, accelerating inference on edge devices, enabling multi-task and federated learning, and improving robustness or generalization. Practical deployments often combine KD with quantization, architecture design, or task-aware selection of teacher signals to balance fidelity and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers information from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost while retaining much of the teacher's performance. KD methods operate at multiple granularities (soft-label/logit matching, intermediate-feature imitation, module- or layer-wise mapping) and appear across domains including NLP, vision, multimodal, federated, and graph settings. Practical pipelines combine KD with data strategies, teacher adaptation, and complementary compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search), but open challenges remain around data heterogeneity, teacher imperfections, and preserving properties such as low-frequency token fidelity, robustness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Survey of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and flexible approach to compress large models and transfer knowledge across models, modalities, and tasks. Practitioners use KD to produce smaller, faster student models that retain much of a teacher's performance, to regularize training via self-distillation, and to enable multi-task or resource-heterogeneous deployment. Despite strong empirical results across vision, speech, translation, and question answering, distillation exhibits failure modes—e.g., propagation of teacher errors or poor handling of low-frequency phenomena—that motivate variants such as multi-teacher schemes, feature-level objectives, projector layers, and teacher-student co-training. The literature combines empirical recipes and growing theoretical analysis to guide when and how to mix soft teacher signals and hard labels, design teacher architectures, and choose representation vs. logit distillation for best trade-offs between accuracy, efficiency, and robustness.
