papers_seen.author: Mason
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression strategies have become core methods for deploying large deep models in resource-constrained settings. Across vision, speech, and language tasks, practitioners compress models by transferring teacher behavior to smaller students, by architectural replacement, or by searching for task-specific compact architectures. Techniques differ in what is transferred (logits, intermediate representations, inter-class relations), how training data are used (original data, distilled targets, or synthetic data), and how robustness and task-specificity are preserved. Empirical work shows strong trade-offs between model size, runtime, and task performance; recent advances focus on task-adaptive compression, improved layer-mapping, data-free approaches, and preserving robustness under adversarial or distributional shifts. Important open challenges remain in handling domain shift, low-frequency phenomena, heterogeneous teacher ensembles, and reliable data-free distillation.

papers_seen.author: Mcmillan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression for NLP: Strengths, Limits, and a Recipe for Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is the most practical and widely adopted strategy for compressing large NLP models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully—matching soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, using task-aware layer mapping, and addressing data or privacy constraints—KD recovers most of a teacher’s performance while enabling large reductions in storage, latency, and power. However, effective deployment requires recognizing and mitigating limits such as capacity mismatch, distributional heterogeneity, and the risk of transferring teacher biases.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques transfer predictive behavior and internal structure from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce computation, memory, and latency while preserving performance. The literature documents a spectrum of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or channel maps, and relational signals), a variety of optimization and architectural practices (layer mapping, projectors, multi-stage training, and student-friendly teacher design), and deployment workflows for constrained settings (data-free, federated, and domain-adaptive distillation). Empirical and theoretical work highlights multiple mechanisms that make KD effective (regularization via soft targets, representation alignment, and optimization/inductive-bias transfer), while also identifying persistent challenges such as aligning heterogeneous architectures, preserving low-frequency behavior, and selecting what and when to transfer. Practical recommendations center on matching distillation signals to student capacity, using feature- or layer-aware objectives when internal alignment matters, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques for robust deployment.

papers_seen.author: Alvarado
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques compress large neural networks into smaller, faster models for practical deployment. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD succeeds through multiple mechanisms — not solely by copying a stronger teacher — enabling many practical variants (logit-based soft targets, feature- and layer-level matching, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-free and privacy-preserving protocols). Effective application depends on choosing what and how to transfer, handling data or device constraints, and combining distillation with other compression tools. Key limitations include optimization dynamics, distribution shift for synthetic data, and heterogeneity in federated or privacy-sensitive settings; current research points toward deeper study of representation transfer, optimization effects, and task-aware distillation pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: BAM! Born-Again Multi-Task Networks for Natural Language Understanding
papers_seen.abstract: It can be challenging to train multi-task neural networks that outperform or even match their single-task counterparts. To help address this, we propose using knowledge distillation where single-task models teach a multi-task model. We enhance this training with teacher annealing, a novel method that gradually transitions the model from distillation to supervised learning, helping the multi-task model surpass its single-task teachers. We evaluate our approach by multi-task fine-tuning BERT on the GLUE benchmark. Our method consistently improves over standard single-task and multi-task training.

papers_seen.author: Liu
papers_seen.title: Enabling Multimodal Generation on CLIP via Vision-Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The recent large-scale vision-language pre-training (VLP) of dual-stream architectures (e.g., CLIP) with a tremendous amount of image-text pair data, has shown its superiority on various multimodal alignment tasks. Despite its success, the resulting models are not capable of multimodal generative tasks due to the weak text encoder. To tackle this problem, we propose to augment the dual-stream VLP model with a textual pre-trained language model (PLM) via vision-language knowledge distillation (VLKD), enabling the capability for multimodal generation. VLKD is pretty data- and computation-efficient compared to the pre-training from scratch. Experimental results show that the resulting model has strong zero-shot performance on multimodal generation tasks, such as open-ended visual question answering and image captioning. For example, it achieves 44.5% zero-shot accuracy on the VQAv2 dataset, surpassing the previous state-of-the-art zero-shot model with $7\times$ fewer parameters. Furthermore, the original textual language understanding and generation ability of the PLM is maintained after VLKD, which makes our model versatile for both multimodal and unimodal tasks.

papers_seen.author: Rocha
papers_seen.title: Few Shot Network Compression via Cross Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Model compression has been widely adopted to obtain light-weighted deep neural networks. Most prevalent methods, however, require fine-tuning with sufficient training data to ensure accuracy, which could be challenged by privacy and security issues. As a compromise between privacy and performance, in this paper we investigate few shot network compression: given few samples per class, how can we effectively compress the network with negligible performance drop? The core challenge of few shot network compression lies in high estimation errors from the original network during inference, since the compressed network can easily over-fits on the few training instances. The estimation errors could propagate and accumulate layer-wisely and finally deteriorate the network output. To address the problem, we propose cross distillation, a novel layer-wise knowledge distillation approach. By interweaving hidden layers of teacher and student network, layer-wisely accumulated estimation errors can be effectively reduced.The proposed method offers a general framework compatible with prevalent network compression techniques such as pruning. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that cross distillation can significantly improve the student network's accuracy when only a few training instances are available.

papers_seen.author: Mills
papers_seen.title: Why Knowledge Distillation Should Be the Central Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, adaptable technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of their performance. When combined with careful pre-training of compact architectures, representation-level transfer, augmentation or synthesized data, and orthogonal compression methods (pruning, quantization), KD delivers strong trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy. However, realizing those gains in practice requires attention to optimization dynamics, data availability, privacy, and known failure modes (e.g., low-frequency token degradation), and so KD should be applied as part of an integrated, responsible compression pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Extensions, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. Research over the past decade has expanded KD from simple teacher–student logit matching to a rich set of strategies that address data availability, privacy, distributed settings, architecture mismatches, and task-specific compression needs. Advances include data-free and zero-shot distillation, federated and privacy-aware distillation, representational and layer-mapping techniques for pre-trained language models, and practical combinations with quantization and architecture search to enable deployment on resource-constrained devices.

papers_seen.author: Mueller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central, pragmatic approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD delivers strong empirical gains across domains by transferring soft outputs, intermediate representations, or task-specific behaviors from teachers to students. Its strengths are practical: it supports deployment on constrained hardware, enables multi-teacher and cross-model transfer, and integrates with other compression tools. At the same time, KD is not a plug-and-play solution: theoretical and empirical work shows limits under data heterogeneity, imperfect teachers, and mismatched architectures, so KD must be applied with task-aware choices (signal type, layer alignment, teacher selection, and curricula) and often combined with complementary methods to realize reliable, high-fidelity compression.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Path for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Power, Pitfalls, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and widely applicable approach to compress large neural models into smaller, faster, and often more deployable students while retaining much of the teacher's performance. KD enables dramatic inference speedups, parameter reduction, privacy-preserving transfer, and flexible deployment across device and domain constraints. However, distillation is not a panacea: it can introduce systematic errors (e.g., on low-frequency phenomena), struggle under data heterogeneity, and depends critically on teacher design and the distillation procedure. Combining KD with careful teacher selection or training, multi-teacher and ensemble strategies, data-free synthesis, architecture search for task-adaptive compression, and device-aware pruning yields a pragmatic toolkit for real-world compression and adaptation needs. The body of this paper lays out evidence for these claims and recommends concrete practices for deploying KD effectively in NLP and broader deep learning tasks.

papers_seen.author: Mckay
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques have become central to deploying high-performance deep models in resource-constrained settings. Research has produced diverse approaches that transfer information from larger "teacher" models to smaller "student" models via softened outputs, intermediate feature supervision, layer-wise alignment, module replacement, data augmentation, and data-free synthesis. These methods have been applied across modalities (vision, speech, language, multi-modal), combined with quantization and architecture search, and adapted for settings with limited or private data. Empirical and theoretical work highlights why distillation can improve generalization, how inductive biases or teacher strength influence transfer, and practical strategies to make students more robust and efficient. Challenges remain in aligning heterogeneous architectures, preserving task-relevant representations, and designing principled distillation objectives for varied downstream tasks.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques aim to transfer information from large, expensive teacher models into smaller, faster students while preserving performance. This synthesis summarizes methodological families (soft-label distillation, representation distillation, adversarial and decision-boundary approaches, data-free and domain-adaptive strategies), theoretical insights about when and why distillation helps, and practical considerations including robustness, privacy, and architecture-aware compression. It highlights representative results and trade-offs reported across recent work, and outlines open directions for improving optimization, preserving robustness, and adapting distillation to domain and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Graph-less Neural Networks: Teaching Old MLPs New Tricks via Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are popular for graph machine learning and have shown great results on wide node classification tasks. Yet, they are less popular for practical deployments in the industry owing to their scalability challenges incurred by data dependency. Namely, GNN inference depends on neighbor nodes multiple hops away from the target, and fetching them burdens latency-constrained applications. Existing inference acceleration methods like pruning and quantization can speed up GNNs by reducing Multiplication-and-ACcumulation (MAC) operations, but the improvements are limited given the data dependency is not resolved. Conversely, multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) have no graph dependency and infer much faster than GNNs, even though they are less accurate than GNNs for node classification in general. Motivated by these complementary strengths and weaknesses, we bring GNNs and MLPs together via knowledge distillation (KD). Our work shows that the performance of MLPs can be improved by large margins with GNN KD. We call the distilled MLPs Graph-less Neural Networks (GLNNs) as they have no inference graph dependency. We show that GLNNs with competitive accuracy infer faster than GNNs by 146X-273X and faster than other acceleration methods by 14X-27X. Under a production setting involving both transductive and inductive predictions across 7 datasets, GLNN accuracies improve over stand-alone MLPs by 12.36% on average and match GNNs on 6/7 datasets. Comprehensive analysis shows when and why GLNNs can achieve competitive accuracies to GNNs and suggests GLNN as a handy choice for latency-constrained applications.

papers_seen.author: Silva
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile, and central technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable ones while preserving most of their performance. KD works across modalities and tasks, integrates naturally with complementary compression strategies, and supports deployment under privacy- and resource-constrained settings. Realizing KD’s full potential requires attention to what signals are distilled (logits, features, relations), how data are managed or synthesized, and how teacher–student alignment and curricula are designed.

papers_seen.author: Shaffer
papers_seen.title: Selective Knowledge Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Neural Machine Translation (NMT) models achieve state-of-the-art performance on many translation benchmarks. As an active research field in NMT, knowledge distillation is widely applied to enhance the model's performance by transferring teacher model's knowledge on each training sample. However, previous work rarely discusses the different impacts and connections among these samples, which serve as the medium for transferring teacher knowledge. In this paper, we design a novel protocol that can effectively analyze the different impacts of samples by comparing various samples' partitions. Based on above protocol, we conduct extensive experiments and find that the teacher's knowledge is not the more, the better. Knowledge over specific samples may even hurt the whole performance of knowledge distillation. Finally, to address these issues, we propose two simple yet effective strategies, i.e., batch-level and global-level selections, to pick suitable samples for distillation. We evaluate our approaches on two large-scale machine translation tasks, WMT'14 English->German and WMT'19 Chinese->English. Experimental results show that our approaches yield up to +1.28 and +0.89 BLEU points improvements over the Transformer baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Higgins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Context-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable approach for compressing large models into smaller ones that meet deployment constraints. KD reduces storage, latency, and energy while preserving much of teacher performance, but its success depends on what knowledge is transferred, how teacher signals are generated and trusted, and how distillation is combined with other compression methods and fairness or robustness constraints. Effective deployment requires task-aware decisions about targets (logits vs. features), data (original, augmented, or synthetic), architectural alignment, and additional safeguards for bias and domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: AlphaNet: Improved Training of Supernets with Alpha-Divergence
papers_seen.abstract: Weight-sharing neural architecture search (NAS) is an effective technique for automating efficient neural architecture design. Weight-sharing NAS builds a supernet that assembles all the architectures as its sub-networks and jointly trains the supernet with the sub-networks. The success of weight-sharing NAS heavily relies on distilling the knowledge of the supernet to the sub-networks. However, we find that the widely used distillation divergence, i.e., KL divergence, may lead to student sub-networks that over-estimate or under-estimate the uncertainty of the teacher supernet, leading to inferior performance of the sub-networks. In this work, we propose to improve the supernet training with a more generalized alpha-divergence. By adaptively selecting the alpha-divergence, we simultaneously prevent the over-estimation or under-estimation of the uncertainty of the teacher model. We apply the proposed alpha-divergence based supernets training to both slimmable neural networks and weight-sharing NAS, and demonstrate significant improvements. Specifically, our discovered model family, AlphaNet, outperforms prior-art models on a wide range of FLOPs regimes, including BigNAS, Once-for-All networks, and AttentiveNAS. We achieve ImageNet top-1 accuracy of 80.0% with only 444M FLOPs. Our code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/facebookresearch/AlphaNet.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Design-Sensitive Path to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly useful family of techniques for transferring behavior from large teacher models to smaller students to reduce inference cost and enable deployment. KD has been instantiated as matching soft targets, aligning intermediate representations, progressive module replacement, and selective or multi-teacher schemes. While KD often yields strong empirical gains and enables domain- and task-specific compression, its success depends on optimization dynamics, the choice of distilled signal, data quality and selection, and teacher–student alignment. Careful method choices make KD a reliable, production-ready compression strategy, but it is not a universal shortcut: practitioners must tailor KD objectives and protocols to their constraints and goals.

papers_seen.author: Shaw
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical Tool for Model Compression in NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their performance. KD works across modalities and tasks, and its effectiveness depends on matching distillation techniques to data and deployment constraints. When combined with careful model and data design, KD enables practical deployment of advanced models under latency, memory, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation with Progressive Refinement of Targets
papers_seen.abstract: The generalization capability of deep neural networks has been substantially improved by applying a wide spectrum of regularization methods, e.g., restricting function space, injecting randomness during training, augmenting data, etc. In this work, we propose a simple yet effective regularization method named progressive self-knowledge distillation (PS-KD), which progressively distills a model's own knowledge to soften hard targets (i.e., one-hot vectors) during training. Hence, it can be interpreted within a framework of knowledge distillation as a student becomes a teacher itself. Specifically, targets are adjusted adaptively by combining the ground-truth and past predictions from the model itself. We show that PS-KD provides an effect of hard example mining by rescaling gradients according to difficulty in classifying examples. The proposed method is applicable to any supervised learning tasks with hard targets and can be easily combined with existing regularization methods to further enhance the generalization performance. Furthermore, it is confirmed that PS-KD achieves not only better accuracy, but also provides high quality of confidence estimates in terms of calibration as well as ordinal ranking. Extensive experimental results on three different tasks, image classification, object detection, and machine translation, demonstrate that our method consistently improves the performance of the state-of-the-art baselines. The code is available at https://github.com/lgcnsai/PS-KD-Pytorch.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, broadly applicable route to compressing large models into smaller, faster ones for deployment in resource- and privacy-constrained settings. When combined with complementary techniques (e.g., architecture-aware design, data augmentation, and privacy mechanisms), KD consistently yields strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across modalities. However, realizing those gains requires careful choices about what to transfer (logits, features, attention), how to select or synthesize data, and how to mitigate transferred harms (bias, privacy leakage). This paper argues that KD should be treated as a central, flexible tool for model compression while emphasizing practical design principles and known failure modes that practitioners must address.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applied strategy to transfer information from large or specialized teacher models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models. In practice KD has been used to compress pretrained language models, speed up inference in structured models, enable multimodal generation, improve low-precision networks, and scale training across data-parallel workers. Research spans theoretical analyses of why distillation works, empirical studies of failure modes (e.g., propagation of teacher errors), and practical training recipes (including online and self-distillation variants) that balance fidelity to the teacher with student capacity and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation in Practical Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a niche training trick into a broad, practically necessary toolkit for compressing large deep models for deployment in resource-constrained settings. KD variants enable compressing Transformer-based and convolutional architectures, transferring useful inductive biases, operating with limited or no access to original training data, and even addressing downstream concerns such as fairness. At the same time, KD has limitations in certain distributed or heterogeneous-data settings that require complementary methods or careful protocol design. A targeted combination of task-aware layer-wise methods, feature-level mimicking, adversarial/data-free generation, and attention to distributional heterogeneity yields the best practical results for NLP and other deep learning applications.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Task-Aware Path to Model Compression in NLP and Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a flexible and practical framework for compressing large models and transferring capabilities to smaller ones. When applied thoughtfully — using layer-aware alignment, attention-guided feature matching, dynamic multi-teacher strategies, and privacy- or deployment-aware protocols — distillation enables substantial speedups, reduced footprint, and cross-modal or cross-device applicability with small drops (or even gains) in task performance. Distillation is not a plug-and-play cure: optimization challenges, teacher-student mismatch, and task-specific redundancy mean methods must be adapted to the target architecture and data regime to realize consistent benefits.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: A Deep Hierarchical Approach to Lifelong Learning in Minecraft
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a lifelong learning system that has the ability to reuse and transfer knowledge from one task to another while efficiently retaining the previously learned knowledge-base. Knowledge is transferred by learning reusable skills to solve tasks in Minecraft, a popular video game which is an unsolved and high-dimensional lifelong learning problem. These reusable skills, which we refer to as Deep Skill Networks, are then incorporated into our novel Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning Network (H-DRLN) architecture using two techniques: (1) a deep skill array and (2) skill distillation, our novel variation of policy distillation (Rusu et. al. 2015) for learning skills. Skill distillation enables the HDRLN to efficiently retain knowledge and therefore scale in lifelong learning, by accumulating knowledge and encapsulating multiple reusable skills into a single distilled network. The H-DRLN exhibits superior performance and lower learning sample complexity compared to the regular Deep Q Network (Mnih et. al. 2015) in sub-domains of Minecraft.

papers_seen.author: Ramos
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. Across modalities and deployment regimes, KD can be adapted to match soft outputs, internal representations, or training dynamics, and it plays well with complementary techniques (architecture changes, pruning, data augmentation, and online/distributed protocols). However, realizing KD's benefits in practice requires careful choices about what signals to transfer, how to produce or curate training data, and how to mitigate transferred harms such as bias or degraded rare-token behavior. I argue KD should be treated as a central component in compression pipelines while being combined with representation-aware objectives, deployment-aware protocols, and safeguards for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Flexible Path to Compact and Robust NLP and Deep Learning Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical and versatile set of techniques for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster ones while retaining most of their performance. Distillation methods can be adapted to structural compression, domain adaptation, low-data or no-data scenarios, and different model families (transformers, convolutional nets, graph models). A pragmatic compression strategy combines well-chosen distillation objectives with complementary methods (pruning, architecture transformations, multi-teacher supervision, or data-generation) to meet deployment constraints without sacrificing reliability.

papers_seen.author: Maldonado
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge by Mimicking Features
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a popular method to train efficient networks ("student") with the help of high-capacity networks ("teacher"). Traditional methods use the teacher's soft logits as extra supervision to train the student network. In this paper, we argue that it is more advantageous to make the student mimic the teacher's features in the penultimate layer. Not only the student can directly learn more effective information from the teacher feature, feature mimicking can also be applied for teachers trained without a softmax layer. Experiments show that it can achieve higher accuracy than traditional KD. To further facilitate feature mimicking, we decompose a feature vector into the magnitude and the direction. We argue that the teacher should give more freedom to the student feature's magnitude, and let the student pay more attention on mimicking the feature direction. To meet this requirement, we propose a loss term based on locality-sensitive hashing (LSH). With the help of this new loss, our method indeed mimics feature directions more accurately, relaxes constraints on feature magnitudes, and achieves state-of-the-art distillation accuracy. We provide theoretical analyses of how LSH facilitates feature direction mimicking, and further extend feature mimicking to multi-label recognition and object detection.

papers_seen.author: Hawkins
papers_seen.title: A Fast Knowledge Distillation Framework for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: While Knowledge Distillation (KD) has been recognized as a useful tool in many visual tasks, such as supervised classification and self-supervised representation learning, the main drawback of a vanilla KD framework is its mechanism, which consumes the majority of the computational overhead on forwarding through the giant teacher networks, making the entire learning procedure inefficient and costly. ReLabel, a recently proposed solution, suggests creating a label map for the entire image. During training, it receives the cropped region-level label by RoI aligning on a pre-generated entire label map, allowing for efficient supervision generation without having to pass through the teachers many times. However, as the KD teachers are from conventional multi-crop training, there are various mismatches between the global label-map and region-level label in this technique, resulting in performance deterioration. In this study, we present a Fast Knowledge Distillation (FKD) framework that replicates the distillation training phase and generates soft labels using the multi-crop KD approach, while training faster than ReLabel since no post-processes such as RoI align and softmax operations are used. When conducting multi-crop in the same image for data loading, our FKD is even more efficient than the traditional image classification framework. On ImageNet-1K, we obtain 79.8% with ResNet-50, outperforming ReLabel by ~1.0% while being faster. On the self-supervised learning task, we also show that FKD has an efficiency advantage. Our project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/FKD/index.html, source code and models are available at: https://github.com/szq0214/FKD.

papers_seen.author: Yu
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable ones by transferring predictive behavior or internal structure. A range of techniques — from matching teacher soft outputs to aligning intermediate representations, synthesizing or augmenting data, and coordinating multi-teacher or online protocols — enable practical trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and resource constraints. Success depends on task-aware design choices, student capacity, data availability, and careful handling of robustness and social-impact concerns.

papers_seen.author: Rocha
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Trends
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques aim to transfer predictive power from large teacher models into smaller, faster, or more private student models while retaining most of the original performance. Work across vision and language has expanded KD beyond simple logit matching into data-centric methods (augmentation and mixup), layer- and representation-level transfers, task-adaptive architecture search, data-free and privacy-aware distillation, and unified pipelines that combine pruning or structural compression with distillation. The field blends empirical engineering (speed/size trade-offs) with emerging theoretical analyses that help explain when and why distillation helps.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, widely applicable strategy for producing compact, deployable models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. KD works across modalities and deployment constraints, and supports extensions for data-free, federated, and privacy-sensitive settings. However, realizing KD’s full potential requires careful choices about what signals to transfer (logits, features, relational signals), how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to mitigate transferred harms such as bias or degraded rare-token behavior. When combined with complementary methods (augmentation, layer-aware mapping, multi-teacher ensembles, or differential-privacy mechanisms), KD becomes a flexible core of effective compression pipelines for real-world NLP and deep-learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Heath
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and flexible approach for producing smaller, faster models from larger teachers across vision, language, speech, and multimodal settings. Methods range from matching teacher logits to aligning intermediate representations, ensembling or self-teaching, and combining distillation with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of a teacher's performance while enabling deployment under compute, memory, privacy, and latency constraints, but effectiveness depends on choices of distilled signals, data and augmentations, teacher–student alignment, and task-aware pipeline design.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Cross-modal Knowledge Distillation for Vision-to-Sensor Action Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: Human activity recognition (HAR) based on multi-modal approach has been recently shown to improve the accuracy performance of HAR. However, restricted computational resources associated with wearable devices, i.e., smartwatch, failed to directly support such advanced methods. To tackle this issue, this study introduces an end-to-end Vision-to-Sensor Knowledge Distillation (VSKD) framework. In this VSKD framework, only time-series data, i.e., accelerometer data, is needed from wearable devices during the testing phase. Therefore, this framework will not only reduce the computational demands on edge devices, but also produce a learning model that closely matches the performance of the computational expensive multi-modal approach. In order to retain the local temporal relationship and facilitate visual deep learning models, we first convert time-series data to two-dimensional images by applying the Gramian Angular Field ( GAF) based encoding method. We adopted ResNet18 and multi-scale TRN with BN-Inception as teacher and student network in this study, respectively. A novel loss function, named Distance and Angle-wised Semantic Knowledge loss (DASK), is proposed to mitigate the modality variations between the vision and the sensor domain. Extensive experimental results on UTD-MHAD, MMAct, and Berkeley-MHAD datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and competitiveness of the proposed VSKD model which can deployed on wearable sensors.

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression aim to transfer knowledge from large or ensemble teacher models to smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models while preserving predictive performance. Approaches span soft-label imitation, intermediate feature matching, architecture-aware compression, data-centric augmentations, online and distributed schemes, and teacher-design strategies. Applications include NLP (BERT compression and task-specific distillation), speech recognition, graph neural networks, and vision tasks. Empirical results across benchmarks show that carefully chosen distillation objectives, alignment mechanisms, and data strategies can yield compact models that approach teacher performance while enabling substantial speed and memory gains. Open challenges remain in automating architecture search for compression, preserving robustness and domain generalization, and scaling distillation to very large datasets and model families.

papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Trade-offs, and Practical Recipes
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. KD operates across levels—from soft output (logit) imitation to intermediate-feature and layer-wise alignment—and is often combined with architecture search, pruning, or data-synthesis to meet deployment constraints. Beyond pure compression, KD can act as a regularizer that improves generalization and robustness, but its effectiveness depends on student capacity, the choice of distillation signal, data availability or privacy constraints, and careful matching of teacher and student objectives.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers behavior from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce latency, memory, and computation while retaining much of the teacher's performance. Across vision, language, and graph domains, KD has been applied as logit matching, intermediate-feature alignment, adversarial transfer, and data- or task-aware synthesis. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD often acts both as a source of extra task signal and as a regularizer; practical systems combine KD with pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, and data strategies to meet deployment constraints. Important open issues include data heterogeneity, teacher–student capacity mismatch, privacy-preserving releases, and closing remaining gaps in robustness and domain generalization.

papers_seen.author: Mason
papers_seen.title: Learning Student Networks via Feature Embedding
papers_seen.abstract: Deep convolutional neural networks have been widely used in numerous applications, but their demanding storage and computational resource requirements prevent their applications on mobile devices. Knowledge distillation aims to optimize a portable student network by taking the knowledge from a well-trained heavy teacher network. Traditional teacher-student based methods used to rely on additional fully-connected layers to bridge intermediate layers of teacher and student networks, which brings in a large number of auxiliary parameters. In contrast, this paper aims to propagate information from teacher to student without introducing new variables which need to be optimized. We regard the teacher-student paradigm from a new perspective of feature embedding. By introducing the locality preserving loss, the student network is encouraged to generate the low-dimensional features which could inherit intrinsic properties of their corresponding high-dimensional features from teacher network. The resulting portable network thus can naturally maintain the performance as that of the teacher network. Theoretical analysis is provided to justify the lower computation complexity of the proposed method. Experiments on benchmark datasets and well-trained networks suggest that the proposed algorithm is superior to state-of-the-art teacher-student learning methods in terms of computational and storage complexity.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Insights
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques enable deployment of large deep models by transferring knowledge to smaller, faster, or lower-precision models. Existing work spans pre-training compact models, teacher-to-student soft-target transfer, data-free and teacher-free approaches, self-distillation, architecture- and task-specific adaptations, and combinations with quantization or pruning. Empirical results show that distilled students can approach teacher performance across classification, ranking, speech, and generation tasks, while specialized strategies address limited task data, privacy constraints, and heterogeneous deployment settings. Open challenges include handling domain shift, designing teacher-student curricula, and developing universally effective objectives for diverse architectures and tasks.

papers_seen.author: Munoz
papers_seen.title: Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation in Deep Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation deals with the problem of training a smaller model (Student) from a high capacity source model (Teacher) so as to retain most of its performance. Existing approaches use either the training data or meta-data extracted from it in order to train the Student. However, accessing the dataset on which the Teacher has been trained may not always be feasible if the dataset is very large or it poses privacy or safety concerns (e.g., bio-metric or medical data). Hence, in this paper, we propose a novel data-free method to train the Student from the Teacher. Without even using any meta-data, we synthesize the Data Impressions from the complex Teacher model and utilize these as surrogates for the original training data samples to transfer its learning to Student via knowledge distillation. We, therefore, dub our method "Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation" and demonstrate that our framework results in competitive generalization performance as achieved by distillation using the actual training data samples on multiple benchmark datasets.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Compressing GANs using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been used in several machine learning tasks such as domain transfer, super resolution, and synthetic data generation. State-of-the-art GANs often use tens of millions of parameters, making them expensive to deploy for applications in low SWAP (size, weight, and power) hardware, such as mobile devices, and for applications with real time capabilities. There has been no work found to reduce the number of parameters used in GANs. Therefore, we propose a method to compress GANs using knowledge distillation techniques, in which a smaller "student" GAN learns to mimic a larger "teacher" GAN. We show that the distillation methods used on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and Celeb-A datasets can compress teacher GANs at ratios of 1669:1, 58:1, and 87:1, respectively, while retaining the quality of the generated image. From our experiments, we observe a qualitative limit for GAN's compression. Moreover, we observe that, with a fixed parameter budget, compressed GANs outperform GANs trained using standard training methods. We conjecture that this is partially owing to the optimization landscape of over-parameterized GANs which allows efficient training using alternating gradient descent. Thus, training an over-parameterized GAN followed by our proposed compression scheme provides a high quality generative model with a small number of parameters.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Improved Feature Distillation via Projector Ensemble
papers_seen.abstract: In knowledge distillation, previous feature distillation methods mainly focus on the design of loss functions and the selection of the distilled layers, while the effect of the feature projector between the student and the teacher remains under-explored. In this paper, we first discuss a plausible mechanism of the projector with empirical evidence and then propose a new feature distillation method based on a projector ensemble for further performance improvement. We observe that the student network benefits from a projector even if the feature dimensions of the student and the teacher are the same. Training a student backbone without a projector can be considered as a multi-task learning process, namely achieving discriminative feature extraction for classification and feature matching between the student and the teacher for distillation at the same time. We hypothesize and empirically verify that without a projector, the student network tends to overfit the teacher's feature distributions despite having different architecture and weights initialization. This leads to degradation on the quality of the student's deep features that are eventually used in classification. Adding a projector, on the other hand, disentangles the two learning tasks and helps the student network to focus better on the main feature extraction task while still being able to utilize teacher features as a guidance through the projector. Motivated by the positive effect of the projector in feature distillation, we propose an ensemble of projectors to further improve the quality of student features. Experimental results on different datasets with a series of teacher-student pairs illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Distilled Semantics for Comprehensive Scene Understanding from Videos
papers_seen.abstract: Whole understanding of the surroundings is paramount to autonomous systems. Recent works have shown that deep neural networks can learn geometry (depth) and motion (optical flow) from a monocular video without any explicit supervision from ground truth annotations, particularly hard to source for these two tasks. In this paper, we take an additional step toward holistic scene understanding with monocular cameras by learning depth and motion alongside with semantics, with supervision for the latter provided by a pre-trained network distilling proxy ground truth images. We address the three tasks jointly by a) a novel training protocol based on knowledge distillation and self-supervision and b) a compact network architecture which enables efficient scene understanding on both power hungry GPUs and low-power embedded platforms. We thoroughly assess the performance of our framework and show that it yields state-of-the-art results for monocular depth estimation, optical flow and motion segmentation.

papers_seen.author: Carr
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Cornerstone for Compressing Deep Models in NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, versatile mechanism for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable ones in NLP and related modalities. When paired with targeted choices—what signals to transfer (logits versus features), how to align layers, teacher design, and data strategies—KD preserves much of the teacher’s capability while reducing compute, memory, and latency. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its success depends on optimization details, data availability, and careful engineering to handle distribution shift, rare behaviors, and student–teacher mismatches.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Path to Deployable Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical framework for producing compact, faster models that retain much of the capability of larger teachers. Beyond simple logit matching, modern KD leverages internal representation transfer, selective data strategies, and integration with pruning, architecture search, or federated protocols to meet latency, privacy, and device-heterogeneity constraints. When applied thoughtfully, KD enables efficient deployment across modalities while posing clear methodological trade-offs and open challenges that guide future research.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large models by transferring useful information from one or more teacher models to a smaller student model, enabling faster inference, lower memory use, and domain- or deployment-specific adaptation. Research has developed multiple distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals), teacher-management strategies (ensembles, multi-teacher weighting, teacher-training), data strategies (data-aware curricula, data-free synthesis), and complementary techniques (projector layers, adversarial objectives, curriculum schedules). Empirical work shows that careful selection of what to transfer and how to align teacher and student—balanced with attention to optimization dynamics and data constraints—produces compact models that preserve much of the teacher’s performance while meeting real-world latency, privacy, and robustness requirements.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Unified Visual Transformer Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Vision transformers (ViTs) have gained popularity recently. Even without customized image operators such as convolutions, ViTs can yield competitive performance when properly trained on massive data. However, the computational overhead of ViTs remains prohibitive, due to stacking multi-head self-attention modules and else. Compared to the vast literature and prevailing success in compressing convolutional neural networks, the study of Vision Transformer compression has also just emerged, and existing works focused on one or two aspects of compression. This paper proposes a unified ViT compression framework that seamlessly assembles three effective techniques: pruning, layer skipping, and knowledge distillation. We formulate a budget-constrained, end-to-end optimization framework, targeting jointly learning model weights, layer-wise pruning ratios/masks, and skip configurations, under a distillation loss. The optimization problem is then solved using the primal-dual algorithm. Experiments are conducted with several ViT variants, e.g. DeiT and T2T-ViT backbones on the ImageNet dataset, and our approach consistently outperforms recent competitors. For example, DeiT-Tiny can be trimmed down to 50\% of the original FLOPs almost without losing accuracy. Codes are available online:~\url{https://github.com/VITA-Group/UVC}.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation describes a method for training a student network to perform better by learning from a stronger teacher network. Translating a sentence with an Neural Machine Translation (NMT) engine is time expensive and having a smaller model speeds up this process. We demonstrate how to transfer the translation quality of an ensemble and an oracle BLEU teacher network into a single NMT system. Further, we present translation improvements from a teacher network that has the same architecture and dimensions of the student network. As the training of the student model is still expensive, we introduce a data filtering method based on the knowledge of the teacher model that not only speeds up the training, but also leads to better translation quality. Our techniques need no code change and can be easily reproduced with any NMT architecture to speed up the decoding process.

papers_seen.author: Mahoney
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context-Sensitive Path to Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, flexible technique for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models by transferring information from larger teacher models to compact student models. When combined with feature-level objectives, architectural transformations, teacher optimization, and data strategies, KD can recover much of a teacher's performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, its success depends on task and domain specifics, teacher quality, student capacity, and data availability; therefore, practitioners should treat KD as a toolbox to be adapted—not a single recipe—to obtain reliable compression in real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Show, Attend and Distill:Knowledge Distillation via Attention-based Feature Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation extracts general knowledge from a pre-trained teacher network and provides guidance to a target student network. Most studies manually tie intermediate features of the teacher and student, and transfer knowledge through pre-defined links. However, manual selection often constructs ineffective links that limit the improvement from the distillation. There has been an attempt to address the problem, but it is still challenging to identify effective links under practical scenarios. In this paper, we introduce an effective and efficient feature distillation method utilizing all the feature levels of the teacher without manually selecting the links. Specifically, our method utilizes an attention-based meta-network that learns relative similarities between features, and applies identified similarities to control distillation intensities of all possible pairs. As a result, our method determines competent links more efficiently than the previous approach and provides better performance on model compression and transfer learning tasks. Further qualitative analyses and ablative studies describe how our method contributes to better distillation. The implementation code is available at github.com/clovaai/attention-feature-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Moran
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of methods for transferring predictive capacity from larger teacher models into smaller, more efficient students so models can be deployed under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Research over the past decade has expanded simple logit-matching into a rich set of variants—feature and layer alignment, progressive module replacement, self-distillation, data-free synthesis, and privacy-aware ensembles—making KD a cornerstone of modern model-compression toolkits.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques provide practical routes to deploy large, high-performance neural models in resource- constrained or latency-sensitive settings. Methods vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, relational structure), how training data is used or synthesized, and whether compression is task-agnostic or task-adaptive. In natural language tasks, KD has enabled dramatic size and speed gains for large pretrained models (e.g., BERT) as well as the feasibility of simple architectures that retain most of the original performance. Despite empirical success, challenges remain: choosing what to transfer for maximal utility, constructing or selecting suitable training examples, handling heterogeneous or private data (federated or data-free settings), and designing teacher-student curricula or architectures that improve transfer. Emerging directions include task-adaptive compression, many-to-many layer alignment, multi-teacher and teacher-aware training, and principled approaches to data selection or generation during distillation.

papers_seen.author: Roman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Tool for Practical Model Compression in NLP and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-purpose strategy for compressing large deep models while preserving performance. KD can be adapted to constraints common in NLP deployment—limited compute, privacy restrictions, low-latency requirements, and robustness demands—by pairing standard teacher-student training with techniques such as feature-level matching, data augmentation, multi-teacher supervision, and teacher adaptation. Across domains (transformers for NLP, speech embeddings, graph models, generative models), KD consistently enables large reductions in model size or latency with modest accuracy loss, making it a primary method for productionization of deep models.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Distilling portable Generative Adversarial Networks for Image Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been widely used in various image-to-image translation tasks, they can be hardly applied on mobile devices due to their heavy computation and storage cost. Traditional network compression methods focus on visually recognition tasks, but never deal with generation tasks. Inspired by knowledge distillation, a student generator of fewer parameters is trained by inheriting the low-level and high-level information from the original heavy teacher generator. To promote the capability of student generator, we include a student discriminator to measure the distances between real images, and images generated by student and teacher generators. An adversarial learning process is therefore established to optimize student generator and student discriminator. Qualitative and quantitative analysis by conducting experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method can learn portable generative models with strong performance.

papers_seen.author: Osborne
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, more efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal knowledge. Across vision and language tasks, KD is used to reduce inference cost, enable deployment on resource-constrained devices, and retain performance through techniques that go beyond matching final outputs—including intermediate representation imitation, data-aware training, multi-teacher strategies, and teacher-free or data-free approaches. Empirical work demonstrates both consistent gains and important failure modes (e.g., loss of low-frequency lexical information or sensitivity to domain shift), motivating refinements such as internal representation distillation, curriculum or sample selection, data augmentation choices, and dynamic teacher weighting. Open challenges remain in understanding what components of teacher knowledge most benefit students, how to handle heterogeneity between teacher and student architectures, and how to distill effectively without access to original training data.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Survey of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students by transferring information from a teacher. Techniques extend beyond using teacher soft outputs (soft labels) to include internal representation matching, layer alignment, task-aware selection of teacher information, data-free synthesis, online mutual teaching, and architecture search guided by distillation. Practical work on NLP (especially BERT-family models), generative models, and domain- or modality-specific settings demonstrates that combining pre-training, architecture-aware search, and representation-level distillation often yields the best trade-offs between efficiency and downstream performance. Open challenges remain around imperfect teachers, optimization and capacity mismatch, data availability, and robustness/generalization under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Bowman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger, expensive models (teachers) to smaller, efficient models (students). KD has been applied across vision, language, generative modeling, and privacy-sensitive settings to reduce storage, latency, and energy while attempting to preserve accuracy and desirable properties. Practical approaches range from soft-label matching and feature imitation to many-to-many layer mappings and self-distillation; theoretical work links KD to regularization effects and label smoothing. Despite clear empirical successes in compressing large pretrained language models and vision networks, important challenges remain: students often fail to replicate teachers' internal representations, robustness and fairness do not automatically transfer, and privacy or heterogeneous-data settings impose additional constraints. Ongoing advances focus on richer targets (internal features, layer mappings), alternate training regimes (self- and teacher-free distillation), and task-aware strategies for robust and private compression.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers information from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost while retaining much of the teacher's performance. KD methods operate at multiple granularities (soft-label/logit matching, intermediate-feature imitation, module- or layer-wise mapping) and appear across domains including NLP, vision, multimodal, federated, and graph settings. Practical pipelines combine KD with data strategies, teacher adaptation, and complementary compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search), but open challenges remain around data heterogeneity, teacher imperfections, and preserving properties such as low-frequency token fidelity, robustness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Humphrey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Versatile Path to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) offers a pragmatic route to compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. Across modalities and tasks, KD can transfer predictive behavior, representations, or task-specific inductive biases; when combined with pre-training, architecture search, or careful data handling, it enables compact models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its effectiveness depends on the choice of what is distilled (logits vs. features), how teachers and students are chosen or trained, the availability and quality of data (including synthetic or unlabeled public data), and auxiliary techniques such as projectors, multi-teacher weighting, or meta-learning to adapt the teaching process. I argue that with these design choices attended to, KD is a broadly applicable and cost-effective strategy for model compression in deep learning and NLP.
