papers_seen.author: Davidson
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad family of techniques that transfer knowledge from larger, more expensive models (teachers) into smaller, efficient models (students) to improve inference speed, reduce memory, or enable deployment in resource-constrained settings. Across vision, language, graph, and generative modeling, KD has been instantiated as matching soft outputs, aligning internal representations, or supervising task-specific components. Practical work has shown KD can produce compact models with strong empirical performance, but success depends on many factors including student capacity, the choice of distilled signals, availability of data, training efficiency, and privacy constraints. Recent research has focused on richer teacher-to-student signals (intermediate layers, attention-based fusion), teacher adaptation strategies, data and augmentation strategies for better transfer, and integrating KD with pruning and other compression methods. Important open issues remain around optimization limits, data heterogeneity, and privacy-preserving distillation protocols.

papers_seen.author: Maddox
papers_seen.title: BERT-EMD: Many-to-Many Layer Mapping for BERT Compression with Earth Mover's Distance
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained language models (e.g., BERT) have achieved significant success in various natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, high storage and computational costs obstruct pre-trained language models to be effectively deployed on resource-constrained devices. In this paper, we propose a novel BERT distillation method based on many-to-many layer mapping, which allows each intermediate student layer to learn from any intermediate teacher layers. In this way, our model can learn from different teacher layers adaptively for various NLP tasks. %motivated by the intuition that different NLP tasks require different levels of linguistic knowledge contained in the intermediate layers of BERT. In addition, we leverage Earth Mover's Distance (EMD) to compute the minimum cumulative cost that must be paid to transform knowledge from teacher network to student network. EMD enables the effective matching for many-to-many layer mapping. %EMD can be applied to network layers with different sizes and effectively measures semantic distance between the teacher network and student network. Furthermore, we propose a cost attention mechanism to learn the layer weights used in EMD automatically, which is supposed to further improve the model's performance and accelerate convergence time. Extensive experiments on GLUE benchmark demonstrate that our model achieves competitive performance compared to strong competitors in terms of both accuracy and model compression.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Path to Efficient Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation provides a pragmatic and versatile set of techniques to compress large neural models into compact, faster students while retaining much of their performance. Across NLP and vision, modern distillation variants — including multi-teacher pipelines, self-distillation, teacher optimization, and task-aware layer alignment — address core challenges such as capacity gaps and task-specific redundancy. When combined with complementary compression strategies (pruning, low-precision arithmetic, architecture search), distillation enables deployment of high-performing models under tight resource or latency constraints.

papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Trade-offs, and Practical Recipes
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. KD operates across levels—from soft output (logit) imitation to intermediate-feature and layer-wise alignment—and is often combined with architecture search, pruning, or data-synthesis to meet deployment constraints. Beyond pure compression, KD can act as a regularizer that improves generalization and robustness, but its effectiveness depends on student capacity, the choice of distillation signal, data availability or privacy constraints, and careful matching of teacher and student objectives.

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression aim to transfer knowledge from large or ensemble teacher models to smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models while preserving predictive performance. Approaches span soft-label imitation, intermediate feature matching, architecture-aware compression, data-centric augmentations, online and distributed schemes, and teacher-design strategies. Applications include NLP (BERT compression and task-specific distillation), speech recognition, graph neural networks, and vision tasks. Empirical results across benchmarks show that carefully chosen distillation objectives, alignment mechanisms, and data strategies can yield compact models that approach teacher performance while enabling substantial speed and memory gains. Open challenges remain in automating architecture search for compression, preserving robustness and domain generalization, and scaling distillation to very large datasets and model families.

papers_seen.author: Wheeler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Cornerstone for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically proven approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation), task-aware design, and careful teacher selection or training, KD can yield compact models that retain much of the original performance. However, successful deployment requires attention to data heterogeneity, fairness, and robustness limitations.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Less is More: Task-aware Layer-wise Distillation for Language Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Layer-wise distillation is a powerful tool to compress large models (i.e. teacher models) into small ones (i.e., student models). The student distills knowledge from the teacher by mimicking the hidden representations of the teacher at every intermediate layer. However, layer-wise distillation is difficult. Since the student has a smaller model capacity than the teacher, it is often under-fitted. Furthermore, the hidden representations of the teacher contain redundant information that the student does not necessarily need for the target task's learning. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Task-aware layEr-wise Distillation (TED). TED designs task-aware filters to align the hidden representations of the student and the teacher at each layer. The filters select the knowledge that is useful for the target task from the hidden representations. As such, TED reduces the knowledge gap between the two models and helps the student to fit better on the target task. We evaluate TED in two scenarios: continual pre-training and fine-tuning. TED demonstrates significant and consistent improvements over existing distillation methods in both scenarios. Code is available at https://github.com/cliang1453/task-aware-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, broadly applicable route to compressing large models into smaller, faster ones for deployment in resource- and privacy-constrained settings. When combined with complementary techniques (e.g., architecture-aware design, data augmentation, and privacy mechanisms), KD consistently yields strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across modalities. However, realizing those gains requires careful choices about what to transfer (logits, features, attention), how to select or synthesize data, and how to mitigate transferred harms (bias, privacy leakage). This paper argues that KD should be treated as a central, flexible tool for model compression while emphasizing practical design principles and known failure modes that practitioners must address.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Apprentice: Using Knowledge Distillation Techniques To Improve Low-Precision Network Accuracy
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning networks have achieved state-of-the-art accuracies on computer vision workloads like image classification and object detection. The performant systems, however, typically involve big models with numerous parameters. Once trained, a challenging aspect for such top performing models is deployment on resource constrained inference systems - the models (often deep networks or wide networks or both) are compute and memory intensive. Low-precision numerics and model compression using knowledge distillation are popular techniques to lower both the compute requirements and memory footprint of these deployed models. In this paper, we study the combination of these two techniques and show that the performance of low-precision networks can be significantly improved by using knowledge distillation techniques. Our approach, Apprentice, achieves state-of-the-art accuracies using ternary precision and 4-bit precision for variants of ResNet architecture on ImageNet dataset. We present three schemes using which one can apply knowledge distillation techniques to various stages of the train-and-deploy pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Path to Compact, Deployable Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, flexible set of techniques for transferring behavior from large, expensive teacher models into smaller, faster students. In deep learning and NLP, KD enables practical deployment by reducing latency, memory, and power requirements while retaining much of teacher performance. Effective application requires: (1) combining KD with domain-aware pretraining of compact models, (2) adapting distillation to data-constrained or privacy-sensitive settings, and (3) integrating architectural and optimization improvements (e.g., feature projectors, mixed-precision) to close remaining gaps. When applied thoughtfully, KD is a key tool for making state-of-the-art models useful in real-world, resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Montoya
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of methods for transferring behavior from large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster student models so they can be deployed under real-world constraints. Approaches vary in what is transferred (soft outputs, internal features, attention maps, module behavior), whether distillation is offline, online, or federated, and how it is combined with architecture search, pruning, or privacy mechanisms. Empirically, KD routinely improves compact models over training from scratch and enables deployments across on-device, distributed, and data-scarce settings; however, practical success depends on aligning distillation signals to student capacity, handling imperfect or heterogeneous teachers, and addressing data and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Mayo
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques aim to transfer the predictive power of large, expensive models into smaller, faster models suitable for deployment, domain adaptation, or constrained hardware. Research has explored matching output distributions, aligning internal representations, module-replacement strategies, data-augmented or data-free distillation, robustness-aware objectives, and task-aware selection of transferable knowledge. Empirical work spans language models (including BERT), reading comprehension, retrieval/ranking, and vision tasks, demonstrating trade-offs between compression ratio, accuracy retention, robustness, and required access to teacher training data. Best practices emphasize careful choice of distillation signal (logits, attention, hidden activations), augmentation or synthesis of training examples when data are scarce, and filtering or adapting teacher knowledge to the student’s capacity and target task.

papers_seen.author: Jordan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models by transferring information from a high-capacity teacher to a smaller student, enabling deployment under computation, memory, and latency constraints. A range of techniques—matching soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, multi-stage pipelines, and data synthesis—have been developed to address diverse practical needs such as on-device inference, privacy-sensitive releases, federated settings, and domain shifts. Combining KD with orthogonal compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and adapting distillation signals to task and deployment constraints yields the best real-world outcomes, while open challenges remain around handling distribution shift, data scarcity, and student–teacher capacity mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Lawrence
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge From a Deep Pose Regressor Network
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a novel method to distill knowledge from a deep pose regressor network for efficient Visual Odometry (VO). Standard distillation relies on "dark knowledge" for successful knowledge transfer. As this knowledge is not available in pose regression and the teacher prediction is not always accurate, we propose to emphasize the knowledge transfer only when we trust the teacher. We achieve this by using teacher loss as a confidence score which places variable relative importance on the teacher prediction. We inject this confidence score to the main training task via Attentive Imitation Loss (AIL) and when learning the intermediate representation of the teacher through Attentive Hint Training (AHT) approach. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work which successfully distill the knowledge from a deep pose regression network. Our evaluation on the KITTI and Malaga dataset shows that we can keep the student prediction close to the teacher with up to 92.95% parameter reduction and 2.12x faster in computation time.

papers_seen.author: Montgomery
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical, Versatile Path to Model Compression and Responsible Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature and flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, and often more deployable models. Beyond raw compression, KD can be adapted to meet constraints of privacy, heterogeneous devices, low-precision hardware, and domain or modality shifts. When combined with complementary techniques such as pre-training, layer-level supervision, or ensemble teachers, distillation can retain much of the teacher’s effectiveness while enabling production usage that would otherwise be impractical. This essay argues that KD should be a primary tool in the model-compression toolbox for both research and engineering deployments, and that best results come from tailoring distillation objectives and pipelines to application needs.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques reduce computation, memory and latency of large deep models by transferring information from high-capacity "teacher" models to smaller "student" models. A range of approaches have been developed: soft-target (logit) distillation, feature- and layer-wise matching, data-augmentation and data-free synthesis, multi-teacher and curriculum strategies, and teacher-aware or teacher-training modifications. These methods are applied across modalities (NLP, vision, multimodal) and settings (limited data, federated or resource-constrained deployments), and combine naturally with quantization and low-precision inference. Empirical and theoretical work shows gains arise both from conveying inter-class similarities (dark knowledge) and from the regularization effect of softened targets; more recent work focuses on selecting or synthesizing the most useful knowledge for a given student and task.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Extensions, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. Research over the past decade has expanded KD from simple teacher–student logit matching to a rich set of strategies that address data availability, privacy, distributed settings, architecture mismatches, and task-specific compression needs. Advances include data-free and zero-shot distillation, federated and privacy-aware distillation, representational and layer-mapping techniques for pre-trained language models, and practical combinations with quantization and architecture search to enable deployment on resource-constrained devices.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Mechanisms, Variants, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, more deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. Across modalities and settings, KD methods range from matching teacher soft targets (logits) to aligning intermediate representations, combining multiple teachers, synthesizing training data when originals are unavailable, and integrating with other compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Practical distillation must balance student capacity, the form of transferred knowledge, data availability and privacy constraints, and optimization strategies to produce compact models that preserve accuracy, robustness, and deployment requirements.

papers_seen.author: Shaw
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical Tool for Model Compression in NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their performance. KD works across modalities and tasks, and its effectiveness depends on matching distillation techniques to data and deployment constraints. When combined with careful model and data design, KD enables practical deployment of advanced models under latency, memory, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Powell
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from larger, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models so that students retain much of teacher performance while reducing computational cost. The literature characterizes KD methods at multiple granularities (final logits, intermediate features, attention or layer mappings, and module- or task-level transfer), documents practical recipes and failure modes, and explores extensions for data-free settings, robustness, and specialized tasks (e.g., machine translation, detection). Empirical and theoretical work shows KD is a flexible tool that benefits from careful choices in distilled signals, data/augmentation strategies, and teacher-student alignment; however, limitations remain around optimization, low-frequency phenomena, data availability, and architecture mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Strategy for NLP Model Compression: Promise, Proofs, and Precautions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable approach for compressing large NLP and deep learning models into smaller, deployable students. When combined with complementary techniques—such as architecture-aware compression, data augmentation, and data-free synthesis—KD can deliver much of a teacher model’s performance while greatly reducing inference cost and memory. However, distillation is not without limits: it can propagate teacher biases, depends on careful choice of what and how to transfer, and requires task- and data-aware engineering to be robust in low-data or privacy-sensitive settings. A pragmatic pipeline therefore treats KD as the central tool but couples it with targeted strategies for representation alignment, sample selection, and evaluation under deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Mason
papers_seen.title: Learning Student Networks via Feature Embedding
papers_seen.abstract: Deep convolutional neural networks have been widely used in numerous applications, but their demanding storage and computational resource requirements prevent their applications on mobile devices. Knowledge distillation aims to optimize a portable student network by taking the knowledge from a well-trained heavy teacher network. Traditional teacher-student based methods used to rely on additional fully-connected layers to bridge intermediate layers of teacher and student networks, which brings in a large number of auxiliary parameters. In contrast, this paper aims to propagate information from teacher to student without introducing new variables which need to be optimized. We regard the teacher-student paradigm from a new perspective of feature embedding. By introducing the locality preserving loss, the student network is encouraged to generate the low-dimensional features which could inherit intrinsic properties of their corresponding high-dimensional features from teacher network. The resulting portable network thus can naturally maintain the performance as that of the teacher network. Theoretical analysis is provided to justify the lower computation complexity of the proposed method. Experiments on benchmark datasets and well-trained networks suggest that the proposed algorithm is superior to state-of-the-art teacher-student learning methods in terms of computational and storage complexity.

papers_seen.author: Carr
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Cornerstone for Compressing Deep Models in NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, versatile mechanism for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable ones in NLP and related modalities. When paired with targeted choices—what signals to transfer (logits versus features), how to align layers, teacher design, and data strategies—KD preserves much of the teacher’s capability while reducing compute, memory, and latency. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its success depends on optimization details, data availability, and careful engineering to handle distribution shift, rare behaviors, and student–teacher mismatches.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Improving the Interpretability of Deep Neural Networks with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep Neural Networks have achieved huge success at a wide spectrum of applications from language modeling, computer vision to speech recognition. However, nowadays, good performance alone is not sufficient to satisfy the needs of practical deployment where interpretability is demanded for cases involving ethics and mission critical applications. The complex models of Deep Neural Networks make it hard to understand and reason the predictions, which hinders its further progress. To tackle this problem, we apply the Knowledge Distillation technique to distill Deep Neural Networks into decision trees in order to attain good performance and interpretability simultaneously. We formulate the problem at hand as a multi-output regression problem and the experiments demonstrate that the student model achieves significantly better accuracy performance (about 1\% to 5\%) than vanilla decision trees at the same level of tree depth. The experiments are implemented on the TensorFlow platform to make it scalable to big datasets. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to distill Deep Neural Networks into vanilla decision trees on multi-class datasets.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical Core Tool with Clear Limits and Complementary Needs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely used approach to compressing large deep and language models into smaller, faster students suitable for deployment. KD reliably reduces inference cost and model size while often preserving much of teacher performance, but success depends on what is transferred, how the student is initialized and trained, and how data and robustness constraints are handled. Effective compression therefore treats KD as one component in a pipeline that includes pre-training of compact architectures, architecture-aware alignment or progressive replacement, and data strategies (including data-free or synthesized data) to meet privacy and domain needs.

papers_seen.author: Bowman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger, expensive models (teachers) to smaller, efficient models (students). KD has been applied across vision, language, generative modeling, and privacy-sensitive settings to reduce storage, latency, and energy while attempting to preserve accuracy and desirable properties. Practical approaches range from soft-label matching and feature imitation to many-to-many layer mappings and self-distillation; theoretical work links KD to regularization effects and label smoothing. Despite clear empirical successes in compressing large pretrained language models and vision networks, important challenges remain: students often fail to replicate teachers' internal representations, robustness and fairness do not automatically transfer, and privacy or heterogeneous-data settings impose additional constraints. Ongoing advances focus on richer targets (internal features, layer mappings), alternate training regimes (self- and teacher-free distillation), and task-aware strategies for robust and private compression.

papers_seen.author: Roman
papers_seen.title: Fair Feature Distillation for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: Fairness is becoming an increasingly crucial issue for computer vision, especially in the human-related decision systems. However, achieving algorithmic fairness, which makes a model produce indiscriminative outcomes against protected groups, is still an unresolved problem. In this paper, we devise a systematic approach which reduces algorithmic biases via feature distillation for visual recognition tasks, dubbed as MMD-based Fair Distillation (MFD). While the distillation technique has been widely used in general to improve the prediction accuracy, to the best of our knowledge, there has been no explicit work that also tries to improve fairness via distillation. Furthermore, We give a theoretical justification of our MFD on the effect of knowledge distillation and fairness. Throughout the extensive experiments, we show our MFD significantly mitigates the bias against specific minorities without any loss of the accuracy on both synthetic and real-world face datasets.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Design Principles
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely applicable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. KD achieves favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across modalities when practitioners choose what form of teacher knowledge to transfer, how to map layers and representations, and how to handle limited or private data. However, KD is not plug-and-play: outcomes depend heavily on teacher quality, distilled signals, data availability, and task-specific constraints. Thoughtful combination of feature-level objectives, task-aware layer selection, data-synthesis or privacy-preserving queries, and targeted curricula yields robust compressed models ready for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Suarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Path to Compact Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, practical approach for turning large, high-performing deep models into smaller, faster models suitable for real-world deployment. Beyond pure compression, KD serves as a flexible training paradigm that can be combined with pre-training, privacy-preserving workflows, and architecture-aware mimicry to preserve task performance while meeting latency, memory, and device constraints. A pragmatic KD pipeline aligns the choice of distillation signal, teacher design, student pretraining, and data strategy to the deployment context.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques provide practical routes to deploy large, high-performance neural models in resource- constrained or latency-sensitive settings. Methods vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, relational structure), how training data is used or synthesized, and whether compression is task-agnostic or task-adaptive. In natural language tasks, KD has enabled dramatic size and speed gains for large pretrained models (e.g., BERT) as well as the feasibility of simple architectures that retain most of the original performance. Despite empirical success, challenges remain: choosing what to transfer for maximal utility, constructing or selecting suitable training examples, handling heterogeneous or private data (federated or data-free settings), and designing teacher-student curricula or architectures that improve transfer. Emerging directions include task-adaptive compression, many-to-many layer alignment, multi-teacher and teacher-aware training, and principled approaches to data selection or generation during distillation.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Distilling the Knowledge of BERT for Sequence-to-Sequence ASR
papers_seen.abstract: Attention-based sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) models have achieved promising results in automatic speech recognition (ASR). However, as these models decode in a left-to-right way, they do not have access to context on the right. We leverage both left and right context by applying BERT as an external language model to seq2seq ASR through knowledge distillation. In our proposed method, BERT generates soft labels to guide the training of seq2seq ASR. Furthermore, we leverage context beyond the current utterance as input to BERT. Experimental evaluations show that our method significantly improves the ASR performance from the seq2seq baseline on the Corpus of Spontaneous Japanese (CSJ). Knowledge distillation from BERT outperforms that from a transformer LM that only looks at left context. We also show the effectiveness of leveraging context beyond the current utterance. Our method outperforms other LM application approaches such as n-best rescoring and shallow fusion, while it does not require extra inference cost.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques reduce the size, memory, and inference cost of large neural networks by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models. Across tasks and modalities—classification, detection, generative modeling, retrieval, and NLP—research has developed logits-based, feature-based, and task-adapted distillation strategies, multi-teacher and ensemble approaches, privacy- and communication-conscious protocols for distributed settings, and teacher-optimization/meta-learning variants. These methods trade off fidelity to teacher behavior with student capacity, expose failure modes (e.g., transfer of low-frequency lexical mistakes or overfitting of student features), and introduce remedies such as selective sample distillation, feature projectors, adversarially-informed samples, and staged or multi-teacher curricula. While KD consistently improves compact models compared to training from scratch and enables deployment on resource-constrained platforms, open issues remain in robustness, task-specific alignment, and distillation under data heterogeneity.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information from teacher models. Across vision, language, and cross-modal tasks, KD is used both as a stand-alone compression method and in combination with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical strategies include logit (soft-label) matching, feature-level imitation, multi-teacher schemes, and data- or label-synthesis when original training data are unavailable. Empirical work shows that distillation can recover most of a teacher's performance while enabling much smaller and faster models, but outcomes depend strongly on choices such as teacher quality, the form of distilled signals, augmentation and synthetic-data generation, and whether low-precision or domain-specific constraints apply.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity models into smaller, faster models by transferring learned behavior from a teacher to a student. Techniques range from matching soft outputs to mimicking internal representations, and they address goals including latency reduction, domain adaptation, privacy, and scalability. Recent work expands classical teacher-student pipelines with self-distillation, data-free approaches, ensemble-to-singleton transfer, and scalable online schemes, while theoretical analyses reframe distillation as a form of label smoothing and regularization. Practical deployments show that careful choice of distilled signal (logits, features, attention, or ensembles) and training protocols can yield compact models that approach or match teacher performance in many settings, but open issues remain around low-frequency token handling, domain shift, and privacy-aware data constraints.

papers_seen.author: Yu
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable ones by transferring predictive behavior or internal structure. A range of techniques — from matching teacher soft outputs to aligning intermediate representations, synthesizing or augmenting data, and coordinating multi-teacher or online protocols — enable practical trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and resource constraints. Success depends on task-aware design choices, student capacity, data availability, and careful handling of robustness and social-impact concerns.

papers_seen.author: Wolfe
papers_seen.title: Robust and Resource-Efficient Data-Free Knowledge Distillation by Generative Pseudo Replay
papers_seen.abstract: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation (KD) allows knowledge transfer from a trained neural network (teacher) to a more compact one (student) in the absence of original training data. Existing works use a validation set to monitor the accuracy of the student over real data and report the highest performance throughout the entire process. However, validation data may not be available at distillation time either, making it infeasible to record the student snapshot that achieved the peak accuracy. Therefore, a practical data-free KD method should be robust and ideally provide monotonically increasing student accuracy during distillation. This is challenging because the student experiences knowledge degradation due to the distribution shift of the synthetic data. A straightforward approach to overcome this issue is to store and rehearse the generated samples periodically, which increases the memory footprint and creates privacy concerns. We propose to model the distribution of the previously observed synthetic samples with a generative network. In particular, we design a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) with a training objective that is customized to learn the synthetic data representations optimally. The student is rehearsed by the generative pseudo replay technique, with samples produced by the VAE. Hence knowledge degradation can be prevented without storing any samples. Experiments on image classification benchmarks show that our method optimizes the expected value of the distilled model accuracy while eliminating the large memory overhead incurred by the sample-storing methods.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Graph-less Neural Networks: Teaching Old MLPs New Tricks via Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are popular for graph machine learning and have shown great results on wide node classification tasks. Yet, they are less popular for practical deployments in the industry owing to their scalability challenges incurred by data dependency. Namely, GNN inference depends on neighbor nodes multiple hops away from the target, and fetching them burdens latency-constrained applications. Existing inference acceleration methods like pruning and quantization can speed up GNNs by reducing Multiplication-and-ACcumulation (MAC) operations, but the improvements are limited given the data dependency is not resolved. Conversely, multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) have no graph dependency and infer much faster than GNNs, even though they are less accurate than GNNs for node classification in general. Motivated by these complementary strengths and weaknesses, we bring GNNs and MLPs together via knowledge distillation (KD). Our work shows that the performance of MLPs can be improved by large margins with GNN KD. We call the distilled MLPs Graph-less Neural Networks (GLNNs) as they have no inference graph dependency. We show that GLNNs with competitive accuracy infer faster than GNNs by 146X-273X and faster than other acceleration methods by 14X-27X. Under a production setting involving both transductive and inductive predictions across 7 datasets, GLNN accuracies improve over stand-alone MLPs by 12.36% on average and match GNNs on 6/7 datasets. Comprehensive analysis shows when and why GLNNs can achieve competitive accuracies to GNNs and suggests GLNN as a handy choice for latency-constrained applications.

papers_seen.author: Allen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practical Principles, and Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques transfer knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models so that compact systems approach teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. Work across vision and NLP shows that effective compression combines multiple strategies — soft-label matching, intermediate representation alignment, architecture-aware design, data- and privacy-aware workflows, and adversarial or ensemble consolidation — and that practical gains depend on addressing representation mismatch, optimization dynamics, and task or domain shifts. This synthesis summarizes prevailing methods, empirical patterns, and recurring trade-offs relevant for practitioners aiming to deploy efficient models in resource- or data-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Callahan
papers_seen.title: A Practical Position on Knowledge Distillation: Go Beyond Soft Labels
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a necessary tool for compressing large deep and NLP models into efficient students suitable for deployment. However, naive KD that only matches teacher soft-labels is often insufficient. Effective distillation combines richer knowledge targets (internal features, attention, and layerwise signals), data-aware augmentations, selective sample strategies, and privacy- or domain-aware procedures. The best practical pipelines treat KD as a toolbox: choose which knowledge to transfer based on student capacity and task needs, use augmentation or self-distillation to improve generalization when data are scarce, and apply selective or privacy-preserving queries where constraints require it.

papers_seen.author: Calderon
papers_seen.title: Learning Generalizable Models for Vehicle Routing Problems via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent neural methods for vehicle routing problems always train and test the deep models on the same instance distribution (i.e., uniform). To tackle the consequent cross-distribution generalization concerns, we bring the knowledge distillation to this field and propose an Adaptive Multi-Distribution Knowledge Distillation (AMDKD) scheme for learning more generalizable deep models. Particularly, our AMDKD leverages various knowledge from multiple teachers trained on exemplar distributions to yield a light-weight yet generalist student model. Meanwhile, we equip AMDKD with an adaptive strategy that allows the student to concentrate on difficult distributions, so as to absorb hard-to-master knowledge more effectively. Extensive experimental results show that, compared with the baseline neural methods, our AMDKD is able to achieve competitive results on both unseen in-distribution and out-of-distribution instances, which are either randomly synthesized or adopted from benchmark datasets (i.e., TSPLIB and CVRPLIB). Notably, our AMDKD is generic, and consumes less computational resources for inference.

papers_seen.author: Pierce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a General-Purpose Paradigm: Beyond Compression to Adaptation, Robustness, and Inclusive Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) began as a technique to compress large models into smaller, faster ones. Over the past decade it has matured into a flexible training paradigm that can shape student behavior via soft targets, intermediate feature alignment, and multi-teacher or self-teaching schemes. When designed with task, data, and deployment constraints in mind, KD can enable domain specialization, interpretability, privacy-friendly federated learning, and improved robustness while still supporting efficient inference.

papers_seen.author: Mckay
papers_seen.title: MixKD: Towards Efficient Distillation of Large-scale Language Models
papers_seen.abstract: Large-scale language models have recently demonstrated impressive empirical performance. Nevertheless, the improved results are attained at the price of bigger models, more power consumption, and slower inference, which hinder their applicability to low-resource (both memory and computation) platforms. Knowledge distillation (KD) has been demonstrated as an effective framework for compressing such big models. However, large-scale neural network systems are prone to memorize training instances, and thus tend to make inconsistent predictions when the data distribution is altered slightly. Moreover, the student model has few opportunities to request useful information from the teacher model when there is limited task-specific data available. To address these issues, we propose MixKD, a data-agnostic distillation framework that leverages mixup, a simple yet efficient data augmentation approach, to endow the resulting model with stronger generalization ability. Concretely, in addition to the original training examples, the student model is encouraged to mimic the teacher's behavior on the linear interpolation of example pairs as well. We prove from a theoretical perspective that under reasonable conditions MixKD gives rise to a smaller gap between the generalization error and the empirical error. To verify its effectiveness, we conduct experiments on the GLUE benchmark, where MixKD consistently leads to significant gains over the standard KD training, and outperforms several competitive baselines. Experiments under a limited-data setting and ablation studies further demonstrate the advantages of the proposed approach.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Preserving Privacy in Federated Learning with Ensemble Cross-Domain Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is a machine learning paradigm where local nodes collaboratively train a central model while the training data remains decentralized. Existing FL methods typically share model parameters or employ co-distillation to address the issue of unbalanced data distribution. However, they suffer from communication bottlenecks. More importantly, they risk privacy leakage. In this work, we develop a privacy preserving and communication efficient method in a FL framework with one-shot offline knowledge distillation using unlabeled, cross-domain public data. We propose a quantized and noisy ensemble of local predictions from completely trained local models for stronger privacy guarantees without sacrificing accuracy. Based on extensive experiments on image classification and text classification tasks, we show that our privacy-preserving method outperforms baseline FL algorithms with superior performance in both accuracy and communication efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Bowman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger, expensive models (teachers) to smaller, efficient models (students). KD has been applied across vision, language, generative modeling, and privacy-sensitive settings to reduce storage, latency, and energy while attempting to preserve accuracy and desirable properties. Practical approaches range from soft-label matching and feature imitation to many-to-many layer mappings and self-distillation; theoretical work links KD to regularization effects and label smoothing. Despite clear empirical successes in compressing large pretrained language models and vision networks, important challenges remain: students often fail to replicate teachers' internal representations, robustness and fairness do not automatically transfer, and privacy or heterogeneous-data settings impose additional constraints. Ongoing advances focus on richer targets (internal features, layer mappings), alternate training regimes (self- and teacher-free distillation), and task-aware strategies for robust and private compression.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques aim to transfer information from large, expensive teacher models into smaller, faster students while preserving performance. This synthesis summarizes methodological families (soft-label distillation, representation distillation, adversarial and decision-boundary approaches, data-free and domain-adaptive strategies), theoretical insights about when and why distillation helps, and practical considerations including robustness, privacy, and architecture-aware compression. It highlights representative results and trade-offs reported across recent work, and outlines open directions for improving optimization, preserving robustness, and adapting distillation to domain and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, widely applicable strategy for producing compact, deployable models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. KD works across modalities and deployment constraints, and supports extensions for data-free, federated, and privacy-sensitive settings. However, realizing KD’s full potential requires careful choices about what signals to transfer (logits, features, relational signals), how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to mitigate transferred harms such as bias or degraded rare-token behavior. When combined with complementary methods (augmentation, layer-aware mapping, multi-teacher ensembles, or differential-privacy mechanisms), KD becomes a flexible core of effective compression pipelines for real-world NLP and deep-learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Mayo
papers_seen.title: Rethinking Soft Labels for Knowledge Distillation: A Bias-Variance Tradeoff Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective approach to leverage a well-trained network or an ensemble of them, named as the teacher, to guide the training of a student network. The outputs from the teacher network are used as soft labels for supervising the training of a new network. Recent studies \citep{muller2019does,yuan2020revisiting} revealed an intriguing property of the soft labels that making labels soft serves as a good regularization to the student network. From the perspective of statistical learning, regularization aims to reduce the variance, however how bias and variance change is not clear for training with soft labels. In this paper, we investigate the bias-variance tradeoff brought by distillation with soft labels. Specifically, we observe that during training the bias-variance tradeoff varies sample-wisely. Further, under the same distillation temperature setting, we observe that the distillation performance is negatively associated with the number of some specific samples, which are named as regularization samples since these samples lead to bias increasing and variance decreasing. Nevertheless, we empirically find that completely filtering out regularization samples also deteriorates distillation performance. Our discoveries inspired us to propose the novel weighted soft labels to help the network adaptively handle the sample-wise bias-variance tradeoff. Experiments on standard evaluation benchmarks validate the effectiveness of our method. Our code is available at \url{https://github.com/bellymonster/Weighted-Soft-Label-Distillation}.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Trade-offs, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or ensemble knowledge. The approach spans simple logit/soft-label matching to feature- and layer-level objectives, multi-teacher pipelines, teacher-free variants, and combinations with architecture search, pruning and data-synthesis. Empirical and theoretical work shows distillation yields substantial efficiency gains with careful design, but also exposes limits from optimization, data heterogeneity, and capacity mismatch. Practical deployment therefore balances what to transfer, how to adapt the student architecture, and whether data or privacy constraints require specialized protocols.

papers_seen.author: Blair
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for transferring behavior from large, expensive teacher models into smaller, faster students so models can be deployed under compute, latency, memory, or privacy constraints. KD methods extend beyond simple logit matching to include intermediate representation matching, layer mapping, adversarial or decision-boundary focused sample selection, data-free generation of training examples, meta-learned teachers, and divergence-aware training objectives. Empirical work shows KD often preserves much of a teacher's performance when adapted to task and deployment constraints; theoretical and empirical analyses reveal optimization limits, distributional fragilities, and conditions under which distillation succeeds or fails. Combining KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and tailoring the distillation signal to student capacity and available data produces the most reliable compression outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models by transferring information from a high-capacity teacher to a smaller student so the student retains much of the teacher’s predictive power while using less compute, memory, or latency. The literature has expanded KD beyond matching teacher soft-labels to include intermediate-feature and layer-wise matching, online/self-distillation, data-free and privacy-aware methods, and combinations with architectural compression (pruning, quantization, and architecture search). Empirical results across vision, NLP, speech, graphs, and ranking show that distilled students often recover a large fraction of teacher performance, but practical success depends on choices like teacher design, student capacity, layer alignment, data availability, and training schedules. Remaining challenges include handling low-frequency or fine-grained behaviors, optimization and capacity mismatch, matching heterogeneous architectures, and distilling under privacy or data-scarce constraints.

papers_seen.author: Tran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Patterns
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring predictive behavior or intermediate representations. Across vision, speech, and natural language tasks, practitioners apply KD to reduce model size, latency, and resource cost while retaining much of the teacher's performance. Variants of KD extend beyond soft-label matching to feature- and layer-level alignment, multi-teacher and online schemes, cross-modal transfer, and data-limited or privacy-sensitive settings. Effective distillation typically combines careful choice of transfer target, student architecture and pre-training, and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization). Open challenges include principled data selection or synthesis for distillation, handling imperfect or heterogeneous teachers, preserving robustness and fairness, and scaling distillation to large distributed training scenarios.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Distilling portable Generative Adversarial Networks for Image Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been widely used in various image-to-image translation tasks, they can be hardly applied on mobile devices due to their heavy computation and storage cost. Traditional network compression methods focus on visually recognition tasks, but never deal with generation tasks. Inspired by knowledge distillation, a student generator of fewer parameters is trained by inheriting the low-level and high-level information from the original heavy teacher generator. To promote the capability of student generator, we include a student discriminator to measure the distances between real images, and images generated by student and teacher generators. An adversarial learning process is therefore established to optimize student generator and student discriminator. Qualitative and quantitative analysis by conducting experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method can learn portable generative models with strong performance.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge distillation from multi-modal to mono-modal segmentation networks
papers_seen.abstract: The joint use of multiple imaging modalities for medical image segmentation has been widely studied in recent years. The fusion of information from different modalities has demonstrated to improve the segmentation accuracy, with respect to mono-modal segmentations, in several applications. However, acquiring multiple modalities is usually not possible in a clinical setting due to a limited number of physicians and scanners, and to limit costs and scan time. Most of the time, only one modality is acquired. In this paper, we propose KD-Net, a framework to transfer knowledge from a trained multi-modal network (teacher) to a mono-modal one (student). The proposed method is an adaptation of the generalized distillation framework where the student network is trained on a subset (1 modality) of the teacher's inputs (n modalities). We illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in brain tumor segmentation with the BraTS 2018 dataset. Using different architectures, we show that the student network effectively learns from the teacher and always outperforms the baseline mono-modal network in terms of segmentation accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Wong
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Principled Path to Efficient, Adaptable, and Responsible NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is not merely a compression trick but a general framework that enables smaller or specialized models to inherit useful behaviors from larger teachers while controlling generalization, efficiency, and social impact. When combined with layer-wise and representation-level matching, task-aware architecture search, thoughtful input augmentation, and deployment-aware protocols, KD supports high-performance, resource-frugal NLP systems that can be adapted to heterogeneous devices and sensitive application contexts.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression strategies are widely used to produce smaller, faster models by transferring knowledge from larger or ensemble teachers to compact students. These techniques span supervised distillation, self-distillation, data-free and adversarial approaches, layer- and task-aware mappings, and distributed/online schemes. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance across modalities (classification, detection, generation, and language tasks) while enabling practical deployment; theoretical and practical challenges remain around data dependence, teacher imperfection, robustness, and optimal student–teacher alignment.

papers_seen.author: Shaffer
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become central to deploying large deep models in resource-constrained settings. Research spans a range of goals — shrinking model size and latency, preserving privacy, enabling distributed learning, and retaining task- or robustness-related properties — and a correspondingly diverse set of techniques including logit and feature matching, layer-wise and many-to-many mapping, adversarial generation of training examples, and architecture-aware pruning and replacement. Empirical work shows effective trade-offs across vision, multimodal, and language tasks, while recent methods also tackle practical constraints such as lack of original data, privacy requirements, and distributed communication budgets.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques transfer information from larger, ensemble, or otherwise expensive teacher models into smaller, cheaper student models so that deployed systems meet latency, memory, and power constraints while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. Over the past decade researchers have developed a family of approaches — soft-target matching, intermediate representation and relation matching, online and self-distillation, curriculum and data-aware strategies, and combinations with pruning/quantization or architecture search — that together form a practical toolkit for compressing models used in vision and language tasks. Empirical work shows KD can produce dramatic inference-speed and memory gains with modest accuracy loss when methods are chosen to match task, data, and deployment constraints; important open problems remain around optimization mismatches, robustness to distribution shift, and how best to distill under limited or sensitive data conditions.

papers_seen.author: Bass
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach to producing small, fast models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. When combined with complementary techniques (e.g., layer mapping, multi-stage curricula, data augmentation, and hardware-aware compression), KD enables deployable NLP and deep-learning systems across constrained environments while admitting clear failure modes that demand targeted remedies.

papers_seen.author: Harrell
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques have become central tools to deploy high-capacity deep models in latency-, memory-, privacy-, and compute-constrained settings. Across vision, language, graph, and multimodal domains, practitioners use teacher-student training, feature-level transfer, data-free distillation, and hybrid pipelines that combine pruning or architecture search with distillation. Work in this area balances fidelity to teacher models, robustness, and efficiency, and explores trade-offs such as reliance on original training data, communication overhead in federated settings, and the benefits of designing students or student-friendly teachers. The literature shows repeated success of KD when tailored to the task and constraints, while also revealing limitations under severe data heterogeneity or adversarial settings.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Insights
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques enable deployment of large deep models by transferring knowledge to smaller, faster, or lower-precision models. Existing work spans pre-training compact models, teacher-to-student soft-target transfer, data-free and teacher-free approaches, self-distillation, architecture- and task-specific adaptations, and combinations with quantization or pruning. Empirical results show that distilled students can approach teacher performance across classification, ranking, speech, and generation tasks, while specialized strategies address limited task data, privacy constraints, and heterogeneous deployment settings. Open challenges include handling domain shift, designing teacher-student curricula, and developing universally effective objectives for diverse architectures and tasks.
