papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Compression of Deep Learning Models for Text: A Survey
papers_seen.abstract: In recent years, the fields of natural language processing (NLP) and information retrieval (IR) have made tremendous progress thanksto deep learning models like Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTMs)networks, and Transformer [120] based models like Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) [24], GenerativePre-training Transformer (GPT-2) [94], Multi-task Deep Neural Network (MT-DNN) [73], Extra-Long Network (XLNet) [134], Text-to-text transfer transformer (T5) [95], T-NLG [98] and GShard [63]. But these models are humongous in size. On the other hand,real world applications demand small model size, low response times and low computational power wattage. In this survey, wediscuss six different types of methods (Pruning, Quantization, Knowledge Distillation, Parameter Sharing, Tensor Decomposition, andSub-quadratic Transformer based methods) for compression of such models to enable their deployment in real industry NLP projects.Given the critical need of building applications with efficient and small models, and the large amount of recently published work inthis area, we believe that this survey organizes the plethora of work done by the 'deep learning for NLP' community in the past fewyears and presents it as a coherent story.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: What is known about Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques provide practical ways to transfer predictive capacity from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models. The field encompasses simple soft-target matching as well as richer forms of transfer such as intermediate representation alignment, attention- or feature-level matching, multi-stage and multi-teacher pipelines, self-distillation, and data- or privacy-aware variants. Empirical work shows distilled students can approach teacher performance while offering large gains in latency, memory, and deployability; theoretical and empirical analyses emphasize mechanisms including soft-target regularization, representational alignment, and optimization dynamics. Practical success depends on careful choices of what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to use data (including synthetic or public data), and how to address robustness, fairness, and distributional shifts.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Design-Sensitive Path to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly useful family of techniques for transferring behavior from large teacher models to smaller students to reduce inference cost and enable deployment. KD has been instantiated as matching soft targets, aligning intermediate representations, progressive module replacement, and selective or multi-teacher schemes. While KD often yields strong empirical gains and enables domain- and task-specific compression, its success depends on optimization dynamics, the choice of distilled signal, data quality and selection, and teacher–student alignment. Careful method choices make KD a reliable, production-ready compression strategy, but it is not a universal shortcut: practitioners must tailor KD objectives and protocols to their constraints and goals.

papers_seen.author: Harrell
papers_seen.title: No One Left Behind: Inclusive Federated Learning over Heterogeneous Devices
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning (FL) is an important paradigm for training global models from decentralized data in a privacy-preserving way. Existing FL methods usually assume the global model can be trained on any participating client. However, in real applications, the devices of clients are usually heterogeneous, and have different computing power. Although big models like BERT have achieved huge success in AI, it is difficult to apply them to heterogeneous FL with weak clients. The straightforward solutions like removing the weak clients or using a small model to fit all clients will lead to some problems, such as under-representation of dropped clients and inferior accuracy due to data loss or limited model representation ability. In this work, we propose InclusiveFL, a client-inclusive federated learning method to handle this problem. The core idea of InclusiveFL is to assign models of different sizes to clients with different computing capabilities, bigger models for powerful clients and smaller ones for weak clients. We also propose an effective method to share the knowledge among multiple local models with different sizes. In this way, all the clients can participate in the model learning in FL, and the final model can be big and powerful enough. Besides, we propose a momentum knowledge distillation method to better transfer knowledge in big models on powerful clients to the small models on weak clients. Extensive experiments on many real-world benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in learning accurate models from clients with heterogeneous devices under the FL framework.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across vision, speech, and language tasks, KD has expanded from simple logit matching to a rich toolbox including feature- and layer-level imitation, self- and progressive-distillation, ensemble compression, data-free or zero-shot approaches, and federated protocols. Empirical work shows KD can yield compact models that retain much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost, but practical success depends on design choices about what to transfer, how to supply or synthesize data, and how to handle teacher–student mismatches and optimization challenges.

papers_seen.author: Alvarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Challenges, and Trends
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques aim to produce smaller, faster models that retain much of the predictive power of larger teachers. Across modalities (vision, language, speech, graphs, and generation), practitioners balance trade-offs among accuracy, efficiency, data availability, privacy, and fairness. Recent work extends classical logits-based distillation with feature- and layer-level objectives, projector modules, adversarial data generation for data-free settings, multi-teacher and meta-learned teachers, and privacy-aware perturbations. Empirical and theoretical analyses highlight both practical gains and persistent issues—optimization barriers that prevent perfect teacher matching, data-mismatch effects, and modality-specific alignment problems—guiding current best practices for deploying distilled models in resource- and privacy-constrained scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Practical NLP Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical, flexible pathway to deploy high-performing deep learning and NLP models under real-world constraints. By transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or inductive biases from large or multi-modal teachers to smaller students, distillation enables task- and domain-specific compression, faster inference, privacy-preserving distributed training, and architectural simplification. Effective distillation requires methods that match the target deployment needs—task-awareness, layer alignment, careful use of data augmentation and teacher ensembles, and scaling strategies for large datasets and distributed settings. When designed deliberately, distillation yields compressed models that retain much of the teacher's capability while meeting latency, size, and privacy requirements.

papers_seen.author: Barnes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practical Patterns, and Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Across vision and language, distillation strategies—matching logits, internal features, attention or relational structure, or using synthetic or public data—enable large reductions in model size and latency while preserving much of teacher performance. Practical deployments combine distillation with other compression tools, online or distributed training regimes, and privacy-aware variants, but face persistent challenges in aligning internal representations, retaining robustness and fairness, and operating under data or resource constraints.

papers_seen.author: Owens
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses capability from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. It encompasses methods that transfer final outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure, or training curricula, and it is applied across modalities (vision, language, scene synthesis, and optimization tasks). KD delivers practical gains in inference speed, memory footprint, and often generalization or robustness when paired with complementary techniques (data augmentation, architecture design, and adversarial training), but its success depends on choices about what is transferred, how data are used or synthesized, and how teacher and student capacities are aligned.

papers_seen.author: Farrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Versatile Tool for Model Compression and Adaptation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable strategy for producing compact models that retain much of the accuracy, inductive bias, and robustness of larger teachers. Beyond simple logit-matching, KD encompasses feature- and layer-level alignment, self-distillation, many-to-many layer mapping, and data-aware or data-free workflows that together enable deployment under latency, memory, privacy, and domain-shift constraints. When combined with careful objectives, curriculum strategies, and task-aware layer mapping, KD can serve both as a primary compression mechanism and as a general-purpose training paradigm for regularization and adaptation. However, realizing its full value requires attention to teacher quality, data heterogeneity, and the choice of distilled signals to preserve robustness and generalization.

papers_seen.author: Osborne
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, more efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal knowledge. Across vision and language tasks, KD is used to reduce inference cost, enable deployment on resource-constrained devices, and retain performance through techniques that go beyond matching final outputs—including intermediate representation imitation, data-aware training, multi-teacher strategies, and teacher-free or data-free approaches. Empirical work demonstrates both consistent gains and important failure modes (e.g., loss of low-frequency lexical information or sensitivity to domain shift), motivating refinements such as internal representation distillation, curriculum or sample selection, data augmentation choices, and dynamic teacher weighting. Open challenges remain in understanding what components of teacher knowledge most benefit students, how to handle heterogeneity between teacher and student architectures, and how to distill effectively without access to original training data.

papers_seen.author: Huff
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression methods transfer information from larger teacher models to smaller students to reduce computation, memory, and latency while retaining predictive performance. Methods vary from matching soft outputs to aligning intermediate representations, using teacher ensembles or meta-learned teachers, and operating under constraints such as missing data, privacy, or heterogeneous devices. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD improves student generalization relative to training from scratch in many settings but interacts with optimization, data availability, and teacher imperfection; practical deployments benefit from task-aware choices of distillation targets, architectural adapters, and data strategies.

papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Trade-offs, and Practical Recipes
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. KD operates across levels—from soft output (logit) imitation to intermediate-feature and layer-wise alignment—and is often combined with architecture search, pruning, or data-synthesis to meet deployment constraints. Beyond pure compression, KD can act as a regularizer that improves generalization and robustness, but its effectiveness depends on student capacity, the choice of distillation signal, data availability or privacy constraints, and careful matching of teacher and student objectives.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Distilling Object Detectors with Fine-grained Feature Imitation
papers_seen.abstract: State-of-the-art CNN based recognition models are often computationally prohibitive to deploy on low-end devices. A promising high level approach tackling this limitation is knowledge distillation, which let small student model mimic cumbersome teacher model's output to get improved generalization. However, related methods mainly focus on simple task of classification while do not consider complex tasks like object detection. We show applying the vanilla knowledge distillation to detection model gets minor gain. To address the challenge of distilling knowledge in detection model, we propose a fine-grained feature imitation method exploiting the cross-location discrepancy of feature response. Our intuition is that detectors care more about local near object regions. Thus the discrepancy of feature response on the near object anchor locations reveals important information of how teacher model tends to generalize. We design a novel mechanism to estimate those locations and let student model imitate the teacher on them to get enhanced performance. We first validate the idea on a developed lightweight toy detector which carries simplest notion of current state-of-the-art anchor based detection models on challenging KITTI dataset, our method generates up to 15% boost of mAP for the student model compared to the non-imitated counterpart. We then extensively evaluate the method with Faster R-CNN model under various scenarios with common object detection benchmark of Pascal VOC and COCO, imitation alleviates up to 74% performance drop of student model compared to teacher. Codes released at https://github.com/twangnh/Distilling-Object-Detectors

papers_seen.author: Mueller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central, pragmatic approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD delivers strong empirical gains across domains by transferring soft outputs, intermediate representations, or task-specific behaviors from teachers to students. Its strengths are practical: it supports deployment on constrained hardware, enables multi-teacher and cross-model transfer, and integrates with other compression tools. At the same time, KD is not a plug-and-play solution: theoretical and empirical work shows limits under data heterogeneity, imperfect teachers, and mismatched architectures, so KD must be applied with task-aware choices (signal type, layer alignment, teacher selection, and curricula) and often combined with complementary methods to realize reliable, high-fidelity compression.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Multi-Level Branched Regularization for Federated Learning
papers_seen.abstract: A critical challenge of federated learning is data heterogeneity and imbalance across clients, which leads to inconsistency between local networks and unstable convergence of global models. To alleviate the limitations, we propose a novel architectural regularization technique that constructs multiple auxiliary branches in each local model by grafting local and global subnetworks at several different levels and that learns the representations of the main pathway in the local model congruent to the auxiliary hybrid pathways via online knowledge distillation. The proposed technique is effective to robustify the global model even in the non-iid setting and is applicable to various federated learning frameworks conveniently without incurring extra communication costs. We perform comprehensive empirical studies and demonstrate remarkable performance gains in terms of accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods. The source code is available at our project page.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques provide practical routes to deploy large, high-performance neural models in resource- constrained or latency-sensitive settings. Methods vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, relational structure), how training data is used or synthesized, and whether compression is task-agnostic or task-adaptive. In natural language tasks, KD has enabled dramatic size and speed gains for large pretrained models (e.g., BERT) as well as the feasibility of simple architectures that retain most of the original performance. Despite empirical success, challenges remain: choosing what to transfer for maximal utility, constructing or selecting suitable training examples, handling heterogeneous or private data (federated or data-free settings), and designing teacher-student curricula or architectures that improve transfer. Emerging directions include task-adaptive compression, many-to-many layer alignment, multi-teacher and teacher-aware training, and principled approaches to data selection or generation during distillation.

papers_seen.author: Hodges
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical Pillar for Compressing Deep Models in NLP and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical, flexible toolkit for compressing large neural networks while retaining much of their performance. Across NLP and other domains, KD enables deployment on resource-limited devices, supports privacy-preserving and federated scenarios, and combines effectively with pre-training, data augmentation, and structured compression. I argue that KD should be a default component of any production-aware model compression pipeline, augmented by task- and data-aware techniques to preserve robustness and accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Rejuvenating Low-Frequency Words: Making the Most of Parallel Data in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is commonly used to construct synthetic data for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models. However, there exists a discrepancy on low-frequency words between the distilled and the original data, leading to more errors on predicting low-frequency words. To alleviate the problem, we directly expose the raw data into NAT by leveraging pretraining. By analyzing directed alignments, we found that KD makes low-frequency source words aligned with targets more deterministically but fails to align sufficient low-frequency words from target to source. Accordingly, we propose reverse KD to rejuvenate more alignments for low-frequency target words. To make the most of authentic and synthetic data, we combine these complementary approaches as a new training strategy for further boosting NAT performance. We conduct experiments on five translation benchmarks over two advanced architectures. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach can significantly and universally improve translation quality by reducing translation errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach achieves 28.2 and 33.9 BLEU points on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets, respectively. Our code, data, and trained models are available at \url{https://github.com/alphadl/RLFW-NAT}.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Practical Recommendations for NLP and Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable approach to compress large deep models into smaller, deployable ones. Across language models, speech encoders, and vision systems, distillation reduces model size and inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. However, success is not automatic: distillation interacts with dataset availability, model heterogeneity, optimization dynamics, robustness, and fairness. Careful choices of what to transfer (logits, features, layer-wise representations), how to handle missing data, and how to address heterogeneous or privacy-sensitive settings are essential for reliable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Federated Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Distributed learning frameworks often rely on exchanging model parameters across workers, instead of revealing their raw data. A prime example is federated learning that exchanges the gradients or weights of each neural network model. Under limited communication resources, however, such a method becomes extremely costly particularly for modern deep neural networks having a huge number of model parameters. In this regard, federated distillation (FD) is a compelling distributed learning solution that only exchanges the model outputs whose dimensions are commonly much smaller than the model sizes (e.g., 10 labels in the MNIST dataset). The goal of this chapter is to provide a deep understanding of FD while demonstrating its communication efficiency and applicability to a variety of tasks. To this end, towards demystifying the operational principle of FD, the first part of this chapter provides a novel asymptotic analysis for two foundational algorithms of FD, namely knowledge distillation (KD) and co-distillation (CD), by exploiting the theory of neural tangent kernel (NTK). Next, the second part elaborates on a baseline implementation of FD for a classification task, and illustrates its performance in terms of accuracy and communication efficiency compared to FL. Lastly, to demonstrate the applicability of FD to various distributed learning tasks and environments, the third part presents two selected applications, namely FD over asymmetric uplink-and-downlink wireless channels and FD for reinforcement learning.

papers_seen.author: Carr
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Cornerstone for Compressing Deep Models in NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, versatile mechanism for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable ones in NLP and related modalities. When paired with targeted choices—what signals to transfer (logits versus features), how to align layers, teacher design, and data strategies—KD preserves much of the teacher’s capability while reducing compute, memory, and latency. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its success depends on optimization details, data availability, and careful engineering to handle distribution shift, rare behaviors, and student–teacher mismatches.

papers_seen.author: Bush
papers_seen.title: Practical and Principled Knowledge Distillation for NLP: Task-aware, Teacher-aware, and System-level Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical pillar for compressing large deep and language models into deployable, efficient students. When applied thoughtfully—aligning distilled information to the downstream task, designing or adapting teachers with student constraints in mind, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques—KD can recover much of the teacher's capability while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a panacea: optimization difficulties, dataset mismatch, and distributional issues can limit gains unless addressed explicitly. A principled KD pipeline therefore includes task-aware selection of distilled signals, teacher-student co-design, and system-level techniques (pruning/quantization or data-free synthesis) to achieve robust, efficient models for production NLP settings.

papers_seen.author: Mckay
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques have become central to deploying high-performance deep models in resource-constrained settings. Research has produced diverse approaches that transfer information from larger "teacher" models to smaller "student" models via softened outputs, intermediate feature supervision, layer-wise alignment, module replacement, data augmentation, and data-free synthesis. These methods have been applied across modalities (vision, speech, language, multi-modal), combined with quantization and architecture search, and adapted for settings with limited or private data. Empirical and theoretical work highlights why distillation can improve generalization, how inductive biases or teacher strength influence transfer, and practical strategies to make students more robust and efficient. Challenges remain in aligning heterogeneous architectures, preserving task-relevant representations, and designing principled distillation objectives for varied downstream tasks.

papers_seen.author: Zuniga
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Composable Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable and practical technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, and more deployable student models. KD is effective across modalities (vision, speech, language, graphs) and settings (task-specific compression, data-limited or data-free transfer), and its strengths are amplified when combined with complementary methods such as architecture-aware replacement, pruning, low-precision numerics, adaptive teacher design, and careful input-side practices. To realize robust and fair compressed models, practitioners should treat KD as one tool within a pipeline: design student-friendly teachers, account for data constraints, use augmentation and curriculum where helpful, and combine KD with orthogonal compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: BERT-of-Theseus: Compressing BERT by Progressive Module Replacing
papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel model compression approach to effectively compress BERT by progressive module replacing. Our approach first divides the original BERT into several modules and builds their compact substitutes. Then, we randomly replace the original modules with their substitutes to train the compact modules to mimic the behavior of the original modules. We progressively increase the probability of replacement through the training. In this way, our approach brings a deeper level of interaction between the original and compact models. Compared to the previous knowledge distillation approaches for BERT compression, our approach does not introduce any additional loss function. Our approach outperforms existing knowledge distillation approaches on GLUE benchmark, showing a new perspective of model compression.

papers_seen.author: Wheeler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Cornerstone for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically proven approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation), task-aware design, and careful teacher selection or training, KD can yield compact models that retain much of the original performance. However, successful deployment requires attention to data heterogeneity, fairness, and robustness limitations.

papers_seen.author: Mckay
papers_seen.title: MixKD: Towards Efficient Distillation of Large-scale Language Models
papers_seen.abstract: Large-scale language models have recently demonstrated impressive empirical performance. Nevertheless, the improved results are attained at the price of bigger models, more power consumption, and slower inference, which hinder their applicability to low-resource (both memory and computation) platforms. Knowledge distillation (KD) has been demonstrated as an effective framework for compressing such big models. However, large-scale neural network systems are prone to memorize training instances, and thus tend to make inconsistent predictions when the data distribution is altered slightly. Moreover, the student model has few opportunities to request useful information from the teacher model when there is limited task-specific data available. To address these issues, we propose MixKD, a data-agnostic distillation framework that leverages mixup, a simple yet efficient data augmentation approach, to endow the resulting model with stronger generalization ability. Concretely, in addition to the original training examples, the student model is encouraged to mimic the teacher's behavior on the linear interpolation of example pairs as well. We prove from a theoretical perspective that under reasonable conditions MixKD gives rise to a smaller gap between the generalization error and the empirical error. To verify its effectiveness, we conduct experiments on the GLUE benchmark, where MixKD consistently leads to significant gains over the standard KD training, and outperforms several competitive baselines. Experiments under a limited-data setting and ablation studies further demonstrate the advantages of the proposed approach.

papers_seen.author: Liu
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Strategy for Compressing NLP Models: Benefits, Limits, and Practical Recipes
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable ones. In NLP, KD enables retaining much of the teacher model's linguistic capability while reducing storage and inference cost. Effective compression with KD requires more than mimicking final outputs: it benefits from aligning internal representations, task-aware layer mapping, and handling data or privacy constraints with synthetic or metadata-driven techniques. However, KD is not a panacea — distributional heterogeneity, privacy, and mismatches between teacher and student capacity pose real limits that must be mitigated by careful method design and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Shaffer
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become central to deploying large deep models in resource-constrained settings. Research spans a range of goals — shrinking model size and latency, preserving privacy, enabling distributed learning, and retaining task- or robustness-related properties — and a correspondingly diverse set of techniques including logit and feature matching, layer-wise and many-to-many mapping, adversarial generation of training examples, and architecture-aware pruning and replacement. Empirical work shows effective trade-offs across vision, multimodal, and language tasks, while recent methods also tackle practical constraints such as lack of original data, privacy requirements, and distributed communication budgets.

papers_seen.author: Moran
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of methods for transferring predictive capacity from larger teacher models into smaller, more efficient students so models can be deployed under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Research over the past decade has expanded simple logit-matching into a rich set of variants—feature and layer alignment, progressive module replacement, self-distillation, data-free synthesis, and privacy-aware ensembles—making KD a cornerstone of modern model-compression toolkits.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Understanding and Improving Lexical Choice in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is essential for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models by reducing the complexity of the raw data with an autoregressive teacher model. In this study, we empirically show that as a side effect of this training, the lexical choice errors on low-frequency words are propagated to the NAT model from the teacher model. To alleviate this problem, we propose to expose the raw data to NAT models to restore the useful information of low-frequency words, which are missed in the distilled data. To this end, we introduce an extra Kullback-Leibler divergence term derived by comparing the lexical choice of NAT model and that embedded in the raw data. Experimental results across language pairs and model architectures demonstrate the effectiveness and universality of the proposed approach. Extensive analyses confirm our claim that our approach improves performance by reducing the lexical choice errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach pushes the SOTA NAT performance on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets up to 27.8 and 33.8 BLEU points, respectively. The source code will be released.

papers_seen.author: Gardner
papers_seen.title: Practical and Responsible Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach to compressing large models into smaller, faster ones for deployment in resource-constrained settings. However, successful distillation requires attention to optimization dynamics, representation alignment, data availability and privacy, robustness, and social biases. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a suite of complementary techniques — including feature mimicking, input alignment, multi-teacher curricula, data-free synthesis, and adversarially-aware training — and outlines concrete best practices for applying KD in deep learning and NLP to maximize utility while minimizing harms.

papers_seen.author: Archer
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Core, Practical Tool for Compression — Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical method for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. It succeeds by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone (e.g., softened logits, intermediate representations, or relational signals), and by combining with complementary techniques (pruning, low-precision inference, architecture search, and data augmentation). KD enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while retaining much of teacher performance, but its effectiveness depends on careful choices about what to transfer, which examples to use, and how to adapt teachers and students to deployment constraints. Thoughtful design — including feature-level transfer, curriculum or selective-sample strategies, augmentation, and data-free synthesis when needed — makes KD a practical cornerstone of model compression for deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Novak
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression methods enable transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large, high-capacity teachers to smaller students so models can be deployed under computation, memory, latency, or privacy constraints. The literature shows a spectrum of approaches — from matching softened output distributions to feature- and layer-level imitation, attention-guided alignment, data-free or zero-shot synthesis of training examples, and distributed or privacy-aware protocols — and demonstrates successful applications across vision, speech, recommendation, and many NLP tasks. Practical effectiveness depends on choices of distillation signal, data availability and synthesis, teacher–student architecture alignment, and training curricula; open challenges include handling imperfect teachers, preserving rare or long-tail behaviors, and maintaining robustness under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Flexible Path to Compact and Robust NLP and Deep Learning Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical and versatile set of techniques for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster ones while retaining most of their performance. Distillation methods can be adapted to structural compression, domain adaptation, low-data or no-data scenarios, and different model families (transformers, convolutional nets, graph models). A pragmatic compression strategy combines well-chosen distillation objectives with complementary methods (pruning, architecture transformations, multi-teacher supervision, or data-generation) to meet deployment constraints without sacrificing reliability.

papers_seen.author: Davidson
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad family of techniques that transfer knowledge from larger, more expensive models (teachers) into smaller, efficient models (students) to improve inference speed, reduce memory, or enable deployment in resource-constrained settings. Across vision, language, graph, and generative modeling, KD has been instantiated as matching soft outputs, aligning internal representations, or supervising task-specific components. Practical work has shown KD can produce compact models with strong empirical performance, but success depends on many factors including student capacity, the choice of distilled signals, availability of data, training efficiency, and privacy constraints. Recent research has focused on richer teacher-to-student signals (intermediate layers, attention-based fusion), teacher adaptation strategies, data and augmentation strategies for better transfer, and integrating KD with pruning and other compression methods. Important open issues remain around optimization limits, data heterogeneity, and privacy-preserving distillation protocols.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques aim to transfer information from large, expensive teacher models into smaller, faster students while preserving performance. This synthesis summarizes methodological families (soft-label distillation, representation distillation, adversarial and decision-boundary approaches, data-free and domain-adaptive strategies), theoretical insights about when and why distillation helps, and practical considerations including robustness, privacy, and architecture-aware compression. It highlights representative results and trade-offs reported across recent work, and outlines open directions for improving optimization, preserving robustness, and adapting distillation to domain and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Mayo
papers_seen.title: Rethinking Soft Labels for Knowledge Distillation: A Bias-Variance Tradeoff Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective approach to leverage a well-trained network or an ensemble of them, named as the teacher, to guide the training of a student network. The outputs from the teacher network are used as soft labels for supervising the training of a new network. Recent studies \citep{muller2019does,yuan2020revisiting} revealed an intriguing property of the soft labels that making labels soft serves as a good regularization to the student network. From the perspective of statistical learning, regularization aims to reduce the variance, however how bias and variance change is not clear for training with soft labels. In this paper, we investigate the bias-variance tradeoff brought by distillation with soft labels. Specifically, we observe that during training the bias-variance tradeoff varies sample-wisely. Further, under the same distillation temperature setting, we observe that the distillation performance is negatively associated with the number of some specific samples, which are named as regularization samples since these samples lead to bias increasing and variance decreasing. Nevertheless, we empirically find that completely filtering out regularization samples also deteriorates distillation performance. Our discoveries inspired us to propose the novel weighted soft labels to help the network adaptively handle the sample-wise bias-variance tradeoff. Experiments on standard evaluation benchmarks validate the effectiveness of our method. Our code is available at \url{https://github.com/bellymonster/Weighted-Soft-Label-Distillation}.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Distilled Semantics for Comprehensive Scene Understanding from Videos
papers_seen.abstract: Whole understanding of the surroundings is paramount to autonomous systems. Recent works have shown that deep neural networks can learn geometry (depth) and motion (optical flow) from a monocular video without any explicit supervision from ground truth annotations, particularly hard to source for these two tasks. In this paper, we take an additional step toward holistic scene understanding with monocular cameras by learning depth and motion alongside with semantics, with supervision for the latter provided by a pre-trained network distilling proxy ground truth images. We address the three tasks jointly by a) a novel training protocol based on knowledge distillation and self-supervision and b) a compact network architecture which enables efficient scene understanding on both power hungry GPUs and low-power embedded platforms. We thoroughly assess the performance of our framework and show that it yields state-of-the-art results for monocular depth estimation, optical flow and motion segmentation.

papers_seen.author: Maldonado
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge by Mimicking Features
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a popular method to train efficient networks ("student") with the help of high-capacity networks ("teacher"). Traditional methods use the teacher's soft logits as extra supervision to train the student network. In this paper, we argue that it is more advantageous to make the student mimic the teacher's features in the penultimate layer. Not only the student can directly learn more effective information from the teacher feature, feature mimicking can also be applied for teachers trained without a softmax layer. Experiments show that it can achieve higher accuracy than traditional KD. To further facilitate feature mimicking, we decompose a feature vector into the magnitude and the direction. We argue that the teacher should give more freedom to the student feature's magnitude, and let the student pay more attention on mimicking the feature direction. To meet this requirement, we propose a loss term based on locality-sensitive hashing (LSH). With the help of this new loss, our method indeed mimics feature directions more accurately, relaxes constraints on feature magnitudes, and achieves state-of-the-art distillation accuracy. We provide theoretical analyses of how LSH facilitates feature direction mimicking, and further extend feature mimicking to multi-label recognition and object detection.

papers_seen.author: Gardner
papers_seen.title: Adversarially Robust Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is effective for producing small, high-performance neural networks for classification, but these small networks are vulnerable to adversarial attacks. This paper studies how adversarial robustness transfers from teacher to student during knowledge distillation. We find that a large amount of robustness may be inherited by the student even when distilled on only clean images. Second, we introduce Adversarially Robust Distillation (ARD) for distilling robustness onto student networks. In addition to producing small models with high test accuracy like conventional distillation, ARD also passes the superior robustness of large networks onto the student. In our experiments, we find that ARD student models decisively outperform adversarially trained networks of identical architecture in terms of robust accuracy, surpassing state-of-the-art methods on standard robustness benchmarks. Finally, we adapt recent fast adversarial training methods to ARD for accelerated robust distillation.

papers_seen.author: Mcclain
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multi-Modal Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an essential and versatile approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable models across NLP and vision domains. When adapted to task and deployment constraints—via multi-teacher schedules, feature-level objectives, data-free synthesis, online protocols, or privacy-aware ensembles—KD both preserves quality and addresses communication, privacy, and compute bottlenecks. However, KD is not a panacea: dataset heterogeneity and optimization mismatches can limit its effectiveness, so careful method selection and engineering are required for robust compression in real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Methods, Theory, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses and transfers knowledge from larger, often ensemble or teacher models into smaller student models to enable efficient deployment and improved generalization under resource constraints. Techniques range from matching final soft outputs to aligning intermediate representations, leveraging self-supervision, adversarial objectives, or curriculum and sample selection strategies. Distillation has been applied across classification, generation, retrieval, speech, and structured prediction, and it also offers avenues to transfer inductive biases, improve robustness, and preserve privacy. Empirical and theoretical work has clarified when distillation helps, what kind of "dark knowledge" is useful, and how regularization-like effects of soft targets can be harnessed even without a superior teacher.

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression aim to transfer knowledge from large or ensemble teacher models to smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models while preserving predictive performance. Approaches span soft-label imitation, intermediate feature matching, architecture-aware compression, data-centric augmentations, online and distributed schemes, and teacher-design strategies. Applications include NLP (BERT compression and task-specific distillation), speech recognition, graph neural networks, and vision tasks. Empirical results across benchmarks show that carefully chosen distillation objectives, alignment mechanisms, and data strategies can yield compact models that approach teacher performance while enabling substantial speed and memory gains. Open challenges remain in automating architecture search for compression, preserving robustness and domain generalization, and scaling distillation to very large datasets and model families.

papers_seen.author: Kim
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When paired with representation-aware objectives, careful pre-training of compact models, and safeguards for robustness and privacy, KD enables production-ready reductions in latency, memory, and energy while retaining much of a teacher's performance. I argue that KD should be treated as a central tool in model-compression pipelines, not as a single recipe but as a family of methods to be combined with task-aware design choices for reliable deployment.

papers_seen.author: Callahan
papers_seen.title: A Practical Position on Knowledge Distillation: Go Beyond Soft Labels
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a necessary tool for compressing large deep and NLP models into efficient students suitable for deployment. However, naive KD that only matches teacher soft-labels is often insufficient. Effective distillation combines richer knowledge targets (internal features, attention, and layerwise signals), data-aware augmentations, selective sample strategies, and privacy- or domain-aware procedures. The best practical pipelines treat KD as a toolbox: choose which knowledge to transfer based on student capacity and task needs, use augmentation or self-distillation to improve generalization when data are scarce, and apply selective or privacy-preserving queries where constraints require it.

papers_seen.author: Moreno
papers_seen.title: Reframing Knowledge Distillation: Beyond Compression to Regularization, Robustness, and Generalization
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is often presented primarily as a model compression technique. Emerging work shows KD is also a flexible training paradigm that provides regularization, transfers internal representations, improves robustness to adversaries and domain shifts, and can be applied without a stronger teacher. This essay argues KD should be treated as a general-purpose tool for shaping student learning — one that can and should be combined with teacher-free methods, internal-representation alignment, multi-teacher aggregation, careful data augmentation, and principled mixing of hard and soft targets to maximize performance in NLP and broader deep learning applications.

papers_seen.author: Harrell
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques have become central tools to deploy high-capacity deep models in latency-, memory-, privacy-, and compute-constrained settings. Across vision, language, graph, and multimodal domains, practitioners use teacher-student training, feature-level transfer, data-free distillation, and hybrid pipelines that combine pruning or architecture search with distillation. Work in this area balances fidelity to teacher models, robustness, and efficiency, and explores trade-offs such as reliance on original training data, communication overhead in federated settings, and the benefits of designing students or student-friendly teachers. The literature shows repeated success of KD when tailored to the task and constraints, while also revealing limitations under severe data heterogeneity or adversarial settings.

papers_seen.author: Allen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practical Principles, and Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques transfer knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models so that compact systems approach teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. Work across vision and NLP shows that effective compression combines multiple strategies — soft-label matching, intermediate representation alignment, architecture-aware design, data- and privacy-aware workflows, and adversarial or ensemble consolidation — and that practical gains depend on addressing representation mismatch, optimization dynamics, and task or domain shifts. This synthesis summarizes prevailing methods, empirical patterns, and recurring trade-offs relevant for practitioners aiming to deploy efficient models in resource- or data-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Explaining Knowledge Distillation by Quantifying the Knowledge
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a method to interpret the success of knowledge distillation by quantifying and analyzing task-relevant and task-irrelevant visual concepts that are encoded in intermediate layers of a deep neural network (DNN). More specifically, three hypotheses are proposed as follows. 1. Knowledge distillation makes the DNN learn more visual concepts than learning from raw data. 2. Knowledge distillation ensures that the DNN is prone to learning various visual concepts simultaneously. Whereas, in the scenario of learning from raw data, the DNN learns visual concepts sequentially. 3. Knowledge distillation yields more stable optimization directions than learning from raw data. Accordingly, we design three types of mathematical metrics to evaluate feature representations of the DNN. In experiments, we diagnosed various DNNs, and above hypotheses were verified.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation for Deep Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in model compression have provided procedures for compressing large neural networks to a fraction of their original size while retaining most if not all of their accuracy. However, all of these approaches rely on access to the original training set, which might not always be possible if the network to be compressed was trained on a very large dataset, or on a dataset whose release poses privacy or safety concerns as may be the case for biometrics tasks. We present a method for data-free knowledge distillation, which is able to compress deep neural networks trained on large-scale datasets to a fraction of their size leveraging only some extra metadata to be provided with a pretrained model release. We also explore different kinds of metadata that can be used with our method, and discuss tradeoffs involved in using each of them.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation describes a method for training a student network to perform better by learning from a stronger teacher network. Translating a sentence with an Neural Machine Translation (NMT) engine is time expensive and having a smaller model speeds up this process. We demonstrate how to transfer the translation quality of an ensemble and an oracle BLEU teacher network into a single NMT system. Further, we present translation improvements from a teacher network that has the same architecture and dimensions of the student network. As the training of the student model is still expensive, we introduce a data filtering method based on the knowledge of the teacher model that not only speeds up the training, but also leads to better translation quality. Our techniques need no code change and can be easily reproduced with any NMT architecture to speed up the decoding process.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical and Flexible Path to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large models into smaller, faster ones while retaining much of their performance. Beyond simple teacher-student logit matching, effective KD approaches exploit feature-level mimicking, task-aware layer selection, meta-learned teachers, online distillation for large-scale training, and task-adaptive model search. When applied thoughtfully — choosing the right supervision signal (logits vs. features), shaping teacher behavior to be student-friendly, and matching distillation to deployment constraints — KD can deliver strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across vision and language tasks, improve robustness, and enable practical deployment of pretrained models in resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Walter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation from A Stronger Teacher
papers_seen.abstract: Unlike existing knowledge distillation methods focus on the baseline settings, where the teacher models and training strategies are not that strong and competing as state-of-the-art approaches, this paper presents a method dubbed DIST to distill better from a stronger teacher. We empirically find that the discrepancy of predictions between the student and a stronger teacher may tend to be fairly severer. As a result, the exact match of predictions in KL divergence would disturb the training and make existing methods perform poorly. In this paper, we show that simply preserving the relations between the predictions of teacher and student would suffice, and propose a correlation-based loss to capture the intrinsic inter-class relations from the teacher explicitly. Besides, considering that different instances have different semantic similarities to each class, we also extend this relational match to the intra-class level. Our method is simple yet practical, and extensive experiments demonstrate that it adapts well to various architectures, model sizes and training strategies, and can achieve state-of-the-art performance consistently on image classification, object detection, and semantic segmentation tasks. Code is available at: https://github.com/hunto/DIST_KD .

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical and Versatile Tool for Compression in NLP: Promise, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, faster students that retain much of the teacher's performance. In natural language processing, KD can operate at multiple granularities — from logits to intermediate representations or entire modules — and can be combined with pre-training, pruning, and low-precision inference to meet real-world deployment constraints. However, distillation is not a turnkey solution: optimization difficulties, mismatches in internal representations, and task-specific redundancies can limit benefits unless methods are adapted to the model size, pre-training regimen, and downstream objectives. When applied thoughtfully (e.g., pre-training compact students, selectively transferring internal features, and using task-aware layer-wise matching), KD yields efficient models that generalize well across tasks and settings.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques have matured into a diverse set of approaches that trade off capacity, latency, and privacy to deploy high-performing deep models in constrained settings. Methods operate at different places in the training pipeline: compressing via soft-targets, transferring intermediate representations, searching or adapting compact architectures, or avoiding access to original data. Work across modalities (vision, language, graphs, generative models, and medical imaging) shows that careful choice of what to transfer (logits, relations, feature directions, layer mappings) and how to transfer it (attention, contrastive alignment, adversarial generators, or task-aware filters) determines final student performance. Practical concerns such as domain adaptation, federated and heterogeneous-device settings, and data augmentation interact strongly with distillation design choices. The literature suggests a clear pattern: representation-level and layer-aware transfers often outperform naive logits-only approaches for structured or pre-trained models, while teacher-free, data-free, and communication-efficient variants enable distillation under realistic deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers behavior from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce latency, memory, and computation while retaining much of the teacher's performance. Across vision, language, and graph domains, KD has been applied as logit matching, intermediate-feature alignment, adversarial transfer, and data- or task-aware synthesis. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD often acts both as a source of extra task signal and as a regularizer; practical systems combine KD with pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, and data strategies to meet deployment constraints. Important open issues include data heterogeneity, teacher–student capacity mismatch, privacy-preserving releases, and closing remaining gaps in robustness and domain generalization.

papers_seen.author: West
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically proven toolkit for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across vision and NLP. KD preserves much of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and communication costs, and it integrates naturally with feature-level matching, data-free synthesis, online and federated protocols, and teacher-design strategies. However, its effectiveness depends on what is distilled (logits, features, attention), data availability and domain match, teacher–student capacity alignment, and objectives like robustness, privacy, and fairness. Real-world deployment requires matching distillation techniques to constraints and explicitly addressing robustness, bias, and data-privacy tradeoffs.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Unified Visual Transformer Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Vision transformers (ViTs) have gained popularity recently. Even without customized image operators such as convolutions, ViTs can yield competitive performance when properly trained on massive data. However, the computational overhead of ViTs remains prohibitive, due to stacking multi-head self-attention modules and else. Compared to the vast literature and prevailing success in compressing convolutional neural networks, the study of Vision Transformer compression has also just emerged, and existing works focused on one or two aspects of compression. This paper proposes a unified ViT compression framework that seamlessly assembles three effective techniques: pruning, layer skipping, and knowledge distillation. We formulate a budget-constrained, end-to-end optimization framework, targeting jointly learning model weights, layer-wise pruning ratios/masks, and skip configurations, under a distillation loss. The optimization problem is then solved using the primal-dual algorithm. Experiments are conducted with several ViT variants, e.g. DeiT and T2T-ViT backbones on the ImageNet dataset, and our approach consistently outperforms recent competitors. For example, DeiT-Tiny can be trimmed down to 50\% of the original FLOPs almost without losing accuracy. Codes are available online:~\url{https://github.com/VITA-Group/UVC}.
