papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Rejuvenating Low-Frequency Words: Making the Most of Parallel Data in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is commonly used to construct synthetic data for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models. However, there exists a discrepancy on low-frequency words between the distilled and the original data, leading to more errors on predicting low-frequency words. To alleviate the problem, we directly expose the raw data into NAT by leveraging pretraining. By analyzing directed alignments, we found that KD makes low-frequency source words aligned with targets more deterministically but fails to align sufficient low-frequency words from target to source. Accordingly, we propose reverse KD to rejuvenate more alignments for low-frequency target words. To make the most of authentic and synthetic data, we combine these complementary approaches as a new training strategy for further boosting NAT performance. We conduct experiments on five translation benchmarks over two advanced architectures. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach can significantly and universally improve translation quality by reducing translation errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach achieves 28.2 and 33.9 BLEU points on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets, respectively. Our code, data, and trained models are available at \url{https://github.com/alphadl/RLFW-NAT}.

papers_seen.author: Parsons
papers_seen.title: Curriculum Learning for Dense Retrieval Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent work has shown that more effective dense retrieval models can be obtained by distilling ranking knowledge from an existing base re-ranking model. In this paper, we propose a generic curriculum learning based optimization framework called CL-DRD that controls the difficulty level of training data produced by the re-ranking (teacher) model. CL-DRD iteratively optimizes the dense retrieval (student) model by increasing the difficulty of the knowledge distillation data made available to it. In more detail, we initially provide the student model coarse-grained preference pairs between documents in the teacher's ranking and progressively move towards finer-grained pairwise document ordering requirements. In our experiments, we apply a simple implementation of the CL-DRD framework to enhance two state-of-the-art dense retrieval models. Experiments on three public passage retrieval datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed framework.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation in Practical Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a niche training trick into a broad, practically necessary toolkit for compressing large deep models for deployment in resource-constrained settings. KD variants enable compressing Transformer-based and convolutional architectures, transferring useful inductive biases, operating with limited or no access to original training data, and even addressing downstream concerns such as fairness. At the same time, KD has limitations in certain distributed or heterogeneous-data settings that require complementary methods or careful protocol design. A targeted combination of task-aware layer-wise methods, feature-level mimicking, adversarial/data-free generation, and attention to distributional heterogeneity yields the best practical results for NLP and other deep learning applications.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: Model Compression with Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation for Web Question Answering System
papers_seen.abstract: Deep pre-training and fine-tuning models (such as BERT and OpenAI GPT) have demonstrated excellent results in question answering areas. However, due to the sheer amount of model parameters, the inference speed of these models is very slow. How to apply these complex models to real business scenarios becomes a challenging but practical problem. Previous model compression methods usually suffer from information loss during the model compression procedure, leading to inferior models compared with the original one. To tackle this challenge, we propose a Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (TMKD for short) method for web Question Answering system. We first develop a general Q\&A distillation task for student model pre-training, and further fine-tune this pre-trained student model with multi-teacher knowledge distillation on downstream tasks (like Web Q\&A task, MNLI, SNLI, RTE tasks from GLUE), which effectively reduces the overfitting bias in individual teacher models, and transfers more general knowledge to the student model. The experiment results show that our method can significantly outperform the baseline methods and even achieve comparable results with the original teacher models, along with substantial speedup of model inference.

papers_seen.author: Mckay
papers_seen.title: MixKD: Towards Efficient Distillation of Large-scale Language Models
papers_seen.abstract: Large-scale language models have recently demonstrated impressive empirical performance. Nevertheless, the improved results are attained at the price of bigger models, more power consumption, and slower inference, which hinder their applicability to low-resource (both memory and computation) platforms. Knowledge distillation (KD) has been demonstrated as an effective framework for compressing such big models. However, large-scale neural network systems are prone to memorize training instances, and thus tend to make inconsistent predictions when the data distribution is altered slightly. Moreover, the student model has few opportunities to request useful information from the teacher model when there is limited task-specific data available. To address these issues, we propose MixKD, a data-agnostic distillation framework that leverages mixup, a simple yet efficient data augmentation approach, to endow the resulting model with stronger generalization ability. Concretely, in addition to the original training examples, the student model is encouraged to mimic the teacher's behavior on the linear interpolation of example pairs as well. We prove from a theoretical perspective that under reasonable conditions MixKD gives rise to a smaller gap between the generalization error and the empirical error. To verify its effectiveness, we conduct experiments on the GLUE benchmark, where MixKD consistently leads to significant gains over the standard KD training, and outperforms several competitive baselines. Experiments under a limited-data setting and ablation studies further demonstrate the advantages of the proposed approach.

papers_seen.author: Roman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Tool for Practical Model Compression in NLP and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-purpose strategy for compressing large deep models while preserving performance. KD can be adapted to constraints common in NLP deployment—limited compute, privacy restrictions, low-latency requirements, and robustness demands—by pairing standard teacher-student training with techniques such as feature-level matching, data augmentation, multi-teacher supervision, and teacher adaptation. Across domains (transformers for NLP, speech embeddings, graph models, generative models), KD consistently enables large reductions in model size or latency with modest accuracy loss, making it a primary method for productionization of deep models.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: AlphaNet: Improved Training of Supernets with Alpha-Divergence
papers_seen.abstract: Weight-sharing neural architecture search (NAS) is an effective technique for automating efficient neural architecture design. Weight-sharing NAS builds a supernet that assembles all the architectures as its sub-networks and jointly trains the supernet with the sub-networks. The success of weight-sharing NAS heavily relies on distilling the knowledge of the supernet to the sub-networks. However, we find that the widely used distillation divergence, i.e., KL divergence, may lead to student sub-networks that over-estimate or under-estimate the uncertainty of the teacher supernet, leading to inferior performance of the sub-networks. In this work, we propose to improve the supernet training with a more generalized alpha-divergence. By adaptively selecting the alpha-divergence, we simultaneously prevent the over-estimation or under-estimation of the uncertainty of the teacher model. We apply the proposed alpha-divergence based supernets training to both slimmable neural networks and weight-sharing NAS, and demonstrate significant improvements. Specifically, our discovered model family, AlphaNet, outperforms prior-art models on a wide range of FLOPs regimes, including BigNAS, Once-for-All networks, and AttentiveNAS. We achieve ImageNet top-1 accuracy of 80.0% with only 444M FLOPs. Our code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/facebookresearch/AlphaNet.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Extract the Knowledge of Graph Neural Networks and Go Beyond it: An Effective Knowledge Distillation Framework
papers_seen.abstract: Semi-supervised learning on graphs is an important problem in the machine learning area. In recent years, state-of-the-art classification methods based on graph neural networks (GNNs) have shown their superiority over traditional ones such as label propagation. However, the sophisticated architectures of these neural models will lead to a complex prediction mechanism, which could not make full use of valuable prior knowledge lying in the data, e.g., structurally correlated nodes tend to have the same class. In this paper, we propose a framework based on knowledge distillation to address the above issues. Our framework extracts the knowledge of an arbitrary learned GNN model (teacher model), and injects it into a well-designed student model. The student model is built with two simple prediction mechanisms, i.e., label propagation and feature transformation, which naturally preserves structure-based and feature-based prior knowledge, respectively. In specific, we design the student model as a trainable combination of parameterized label propagation and feature transformation modules. As a result, the learned student can benefit from both prior knowledge and the knowledge in GNN teachers for more effective predictions. Moreover, the learned student model has a more interpretable prediction process than GNNs. We conduct experiments on five public benchmark datasets and employ seven GNN models including GCN, GAT, APPNP, SAGE, SGC, GCNII and GLP as the teacher models. Experimental results show that the learned student model can consistently outperform its corresponding teacher model by 1.4% - 4.7% on average. Code and data are available at https://github.com/BUPT-GAMMA/CPF

papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical, Task-aware Path for Efficient NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical route to deploy large deep models in resource- and privacy-constrained environments. When applied thoughtfully—matching the distilled signal to the student’s capacity and the target task, incorporating representation-level objectives, and combining KD with complementary compression strategies—distillation yields compact models that preserve much of the teacher’s utility. However, KD is not a silver bullet: optimization difficulties, teacher imperfections, domain shift, and fidelity losses on rare tokens or protected subgroups can degrade student performance unless addressed by task-aware design choices, domain adaptation, or multi-teacher/online schemes. This essay argues that KD should be treated as a core, adaptable toolkit for compression whose effectiveness depends on principled choices about what to transfer, how to train students, and how to combine distillation with orthogonal techniques.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical and Flexible Path to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large models into smaller, faster ones while retaining much of their performance. Beyond simple teacher-student logit matching, effective KD approaches exploit feature-level mimicking, task-aware layer selection, meta-learned teachers, online distillation for large-scale training, and task-adaptive model search. When applied thoughtfully — choosing the right supervision signal (logits vs. features), shaping teacher behavior to be student-friendly, and matching distillation to deployment constraints — KD can deliver strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across vision and language tasks, improve robustness, and enable practical deployment of pretrained models in resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Kidd
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable approach for compressing large deep learning models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students. Modern KD goes beyond matching logits: it includes feature- and representation-level transfers, multi-teacher and self-distillation strategies, and workflows that integrate augmentation, data-free synthesis, pruning, and quantization to meet latency, memory, and privacy requirements. Practical success depends on matching distillation technique to deployment objectives, careful design of layer mappings and loss terms, attention to teacher quality and data availability, and combinations with other compression tools to preserve robustness and generalization.

papers_seen.author: Murillo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Pragmatic Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students across modalities and tasks. KD reliably reduces inference cost and memory while preserving much of teacher performance, but it is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on design choices about what to transfer, how to handle data limitations, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression and fairness-preserving techniques. I argue that KD should be treated as a central component of a model-compression pipeline — one that is combined with architecture-aware methods, data and curriculum strategies, and explicit checks for robustness, privacy, and bias — to achieve deployable, efficient, and responsible models in practice.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical, flexible approach for producing compact neural models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. Across vision and language applications KD has been extended from simple soft-label matching to a wide set of techniques—intermediate-representation transfer, layer-aware alignment, multi-teacher and self-distillation, data-free variants, and adversarial or projector-based feature matching—that enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD both preserves predictive performance and can improve generalization in many settings, while also raising practical challenges such as teacher–student mismatch and degraded modeling of low-frequency phenomena that require targeted mitigations.

papers_seen.author: Gaines
papers_seen.title: AdaBERT: Task-Adaptive BERT Compression with Differentiable Neural Architecture Search
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained language models such as BERT have shown their effectiveness in various natural language processing tasks. However, the huge parameter size makes them difficult to be deployed in real-time applications that require quick inference with limited resources. Existing methods compress BERT into small models while such compression is task-independent, i.e., the same compressed BERT for all different downstream tasks. Motivated by the necessity and benefits of task-oriented BERT compression, we propose a novel compression method, AdaBERT, that leverages differentiable Neural Architecture Search to automatically compress BERT into task-adaptive small models for specific tasks. We incorporate a task-oriented knowledge distillation loss to provide search hints and an efficiency-aware loss as search constraints, which enables a good trade-off between efficiency and effectiveness for task-adaptive BERT compression. We evaluate AdaBERT on several NLP tasks, and the results demonstrate that those task-adaptive compressed models are 12.7x to 29.3x faster than BERT in inference time and 11.5x to 17.0x smaller in terms of parameter size, while comparable performance is maintained.

papers_seen.author: Galloway
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Context-Sensitive Path to Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly effective toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster students for deployment in resource-constrained settings. KD methods span matching output distributions, aligning internal representations, synthesizing surrogate data when originals are unavailable, and co-designing compact architectures for target tasks. While KD often preserves much of a teacher’s performance and enables trade-offs among accuracy, latency, and memory, success depends on the distillation signal, data regime, robustness and privacy needs, and architecture alignment between teacher and student.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: A Deep Hierarchical Approach to Lifelong Learning in Minecraft
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a lifelong learning system that has the ability to reuse and transfer knowledge from one task to another while efficiently retaining the previously learned knowledge-base. Knowledge is transferred by learning reusable skills to solve tasks in Minecraft, a popular video game which is an unsolved and high-dimensional lifelong learning problem. These reusable skills, which we refer to as Deep Skill Networks, are then incorporated into our novel Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning Network (H-DRLN) architecture using two techniques: (1) a deep skill array and (2) skill distillation, our novel variation of policy distillation (Rusu et. al. 2015) for learning skills. Skill distillation enables the HDRLN to efficiently retain knowledge and therefore scale in lifelong learning, by accumulating knowledge and encapsulating multiple reusable skills into a single distilled network. The H-DRLN exhibits superior performance and lower learning sample complexity compared to the regular Deep Q Network (Mnih et. al. 2015) in sub-domains of Minecraft.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques transfer information from large teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost and enable deployment in resource-constrained settings. A diverse set of KD variants—matching soft logits, aligning intermediate representations, synthesizing or reusing data, or adapting student architectures—has been developed. These methods are applied across modalities and combine effectively with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to achieve favorable size/accuracy trade-offs. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to generate or select training data, and how to align teacher and student architectures; open challenges include robust transfer under domain shift, privacy constraints, and heterogeneous deployment environments.

papers_seen.author: Allison
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable ones by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from teacher models to students. The field has diversified from logits-only matching to richer targets (intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals), multiple training regimes (data-free, online, federated, multi-teacher), and task-aware techniques that address capacity mismatch and deployment constraints. KD is widely applicable across modalities (vision, speech, multimodal, graphs, NLP) and is most effective when combined with data- and architecture-aware practices, but practical limits remain around representation alignment, rare-token behavior, privacy, and domain transfer.

papers_seen.author: Mason
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression strategies have become core methods for deploying large deep models in resource-constrained settings. Across vision, speech, and language tasks, practitioners compress models by transferring teacher behavior to smaller students, by architectural replacement, or by searching for task-specific compact architectures. Techniques differ in what is transferred (logits, intermediate representations, inter-class relations), how training data are used (original data, distilled targets, or synthetic data), and how robustness and task-specificity are preserved. Empirical work shows strong trade-offs between model size, runtime, and task performance; recent advances focus on task-adaptive compression, improved layer-mapping, data-free approaches, and preserving robustness under adversarial or distributional shifts. Important open challenges remain in handling domain shift, low-frequency phenomena, heterogeneous teacher ensembles, and reliable data-free distillation.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Linkless Link Prediction via Relational Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have shown exceptional performance in the task of link prediction. Despite their effectiveness, the high latency brought by non-trivial neighborhood data dependency limits GNNs in practical deployments. Conversely, the known efficient MLPs are much less effective than GNNs due to the lack of relational knowledge. In this work, to combine the advantages of GNNs and MLPs, we start with exploring direct knowledge distillation (KD) methods for link prediction, i.e., predicted logit-based matching and node representation-based matching. Upon observing direct KD analogs do not perform well for link prediction, we propose a relational KD framework, Linkless Link Prediction (LLP), to distill knowledge for link prediction with MLPs. Unlike simple KD methods that match independent link logits or node representations, LLP distills relational knowledge that is centered around each (anchor) node to the student MLP. Specifically, we propose rank-based matching and distribution-based matching strategies that complement each other. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LLP boosts the link prediction performance of MLPs with significant margins, and even outperforms the teacher GNNs on 7 out of 8 benchmarks. LLP also achieves a 70.68x speedup in link prediction inference compared to GNNs on the large-scale OGB dataset.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central technique for compressing large deep learning models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teachers' performance. Across vision, language, speech, and recommendation tasks, researchers combine KD with architectural compression, pre-training, privacy mechanisms, and data-free approaches to address inference cost, dataset availability, and domain-specific challenges. Empirical work shows that careful choices about what to transfer (logits, features, layers), how to train teachers and students, and how to incorporate task or data constraints strongly determine final student quality.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Design-Sensitive Path to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly useful family of techniques for transferring behavior from large teacher models to smaller students to reduce inference cost and enable deployment. KD has been instantiated as matching soft targets, aligning intermediate representations, progressive module replacement, and selective or multi-teacher schemes. While KD often yields strong empirical gains and enables domain- and task-specific compression, its success depends on optimization dynamics, the choice of distilled signal, data quality and selection, and teacher–student alignment. Careful method choices make KD a reliable, production-ready compression strategy, but it is not a universal shortcut: practitioners must tailor KD objectives and protocols to their constraints and goals.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high‑capacity models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or structural inductive biases from teachers. A spectrum of methods—logit/soft‑label matching, feature- and layer-wise imitation, attention and relation transfer, ensemble-to-singleton distillation, self-distillation, and data‑free synthesis—has been developed to meet deployment goals such as latency reduction, privacy, domain adaptation, and robustness. Empirical and applied work in NLP, vision, speech, and graph domains shows that carefully chosen distilled signals, teacher designs, and training protocols allow compact models to approach teacher performance, though challenges remain around domain shift, low-frequency phenomena, and preserving fairness and privacy in compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: What Makes a "Good" Data Augmentation in Knowledge Distillation -- A Statistical Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a general neural network training approach that uses a teacher model to guide the student model. Existing works mainly study KD from the network output side (e.g., trying to design a better KD loss function), while few have attempted to understand it from the input side. Especially, its interplay with data augmentation (DA) has not been well understood. In this paper, we ask: Why do some DA schemes (e.g., CutMix) inherently perform much better than others in KD? What makes a "good" DA in KD? Our investigation from a statistical perspective suggests that a good DA scheme should reduce the covariance of the teacher-student cross-entropy. A practical metric, the stddev of teacher's mean probability (T. stddev), is further presented and well justified empirically. Besides the theoretical understanding, we also introduce a new entropy-based data-mixing DA scheme, CutMixPick, to further enhance CutMix. Extensive empirical studies support our claims and demonstrate how we can harvest considerable performance gains simply by using a better DA scheme in knowledge distillation.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Compressing and Adapting NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a principled way to produce small, fast models that retain much of the performance of larger networks. In natural language processing, where modern pretrained models are large and domain shifts are common, KD enables domain adaptation, latency- and memory-constrained deployment, continual learning, and improved robustness when applied with the right strategies. Practical success relies on combining methods — e.g., multi-stage distillation, selective or curriculum-driven example selection, leveraging soft targets as regularizers, and using adversarial or synthetic data when original data are unavailable. When applied thoughtfully, KD is not merely an implementation detail of model compression but a versatile lever for engineering efficient, accurate, and robust NLP systems.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Channel Distillation: Channel-Wise Attention for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is to transfer the knowledge from the data learned by the teacher network to the student network, so that the student has the advantage of less parameters and less calculations, and the accuracy is close to the teacher. In this paper, we propose a new distillation method, which contains two transfer distillation strategies and a loss decay strategy. The first transfer strategy is based on channel-wise attention, called Channel Distillation (CD). CD transfers the channel information from the teacher to the student. The second is Guided Knowledge Distillation (GKD). Unlike Knowledge Distillation (KD), which allows the student to mimic each sample's prediction distribution of the teacher, GKD only enables the student to mimic the correct output of the teacher. The last part is Early Decay Teacher (EDT). During the training process, we gradually decay the weight of the distillation loss. The purpose is to enable the student to gradually control the optimization rather than the teacher. Our proposed method is evaluated on ImageNet and CIFAR100. On ImageNet, we achieve 27.68% of top-1 error with ResNet18, which outperforms state-of-the-art methods. On CIFAR100, we achieve surprising result that the student outperforms the teacher. Code is available at https://github.com/zhouzaida/channel-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Bass
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach to producing small, fast models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. When combined with complementary techniques (e.g., layer mapping, multi-stage curricula, data augmentation, and hardware-aware compression), KD enables deployable NLP and deep-learning systems across constrained environments while admitting clear failure modes that demand targeted remedies.

papers_seen.author: Cameron
papers_seen.title: Well-Read Students Learn Better: On the Importance of Pre-training Compact Models
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in natural language representations have been accompanied by large and expensive models that leverage vast amounts of general-domain text through self-supervised pre-training. Due to the cost of applying such models to down-stream tasks, several model compression techniques on pre-trained language representations have been proposed (Sun et al., 2019; Sanh, 2019). However, surprisingly, the simple baseline of just pre-training and fine-tuning compact models has been overlooked. In this paper, we first show that pre-training remains important in the context of smaller architectures, and fine-tuning pre-trained compact models can be competitive to more elaborate methods proposed in concurrent work. Starting with pre-trained compact models, we then explore transferring task knowledge from large fine-tuned models through standard knowledge distillation. The resulting simple, yet effective and general algorithm, Pre-trained Distillation, brings further improvements. Through extensive experiments, we more generally explore the interaction between pre-training and distillation under two variables that have been under-studied: model size and properties of unlabeled task data. One surprising observation is that they have a compound effect even when sequentially applied on the same data. To accelerate future research, we will make our 24 pre-trained miniature BERT models publicly available.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Powerful, Flexible, but Context-Sensitive for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques are practical, widely applicable tools for shrinking large models and transferring capability to smaller models. KD can preserve performance while reducing inference cost, enable cross-modal and cross-task transfer, and be adapted to constrained settings (few-shot, edge devices). However, KD is not a plug-and-play cure: its benefits depend on what is distilled (logits vs. features vs. internal structure), teacher-student design, data regime, and optimization choices. Careful method design — including feature-based objectives, intermediate-layer alignment, self-distillation or meta-learned teachers, and task-aware curricula — is required to realize robust gains without amplifying teacher errors.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a flexible, high-impact way to compress large models into smaller, efficient ones while retaining most task performance. Modern KD methods extend beyond matching final logits to include layer- and feature-level imitation, task-aware selection of distilled information, data-free or few-shot regimes, and multi-teacher or self-distillation strategies. When combined with architecture-aware compression or search, KD enables task-adaptive, privacy-conscious, and efficient deployment of deep models in real-world NLP and vision applications.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Multifaceted Tool: Beyond Compression to Fairness, Robustness, and Adaptation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is commonly used to compress large models into smaller, faster students, but its potential extends much further. When applied thoughtfully—via feature-level mimicking, progressive module replacement, teacher selection and confidence-weighting, and by combining with automated search or divergence choices—KD can improve fairness, domain adaptation, generative model compression, and student robustness while preserving or even improving task performance. This essay argues that KD is not a single recipe but a family of techniques that should be matched to specific goals (efficiency, fairness, transferability, or generation), and gives concrete methodological recommendations informed by empirical and theoretical work.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Unifying Heterogeneous Classifiers with Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we study the problem of unifying knowledge from a set of classifiers with different architectures and target classes into a single classifier, given only a generic set of unlabelled data. We call this problem Unifying Heterogeneous Classifiers (UHC). This problem is motivated by scenarios where data is collected from multiple sources, but the sources cannot share their data, e.g., due to privacy concerns, and only privately trained models can be shared. In addition, each source may not be able to gather data to train all classes due to data availability at each source, and may not be able to train the same classification model due to different computational resources. To tackle this problem, we propose a generalisation of knowledge distillation to merge HCs. We derive a probabilistic relation between the outputs of HCs and the probability over all classes. Based on this relation, we propose two classes of methods based on cross-entropy minimisation and matrix factorisation, which allow us to estimate soft labels over all classes from unlabelled samples and use them in lieu of ground truth labels to train a unified classifier. Our extensive experiments on ImageNet, LSUN, and Places365 datasets show that our approaches significantly outperform a naive extension of distillation and can achieve almost the same accuracy as classifiers that are trained in a centralised, supervised manner.

papers_seen.author: Gardner
papers_seen.title: Adversarially Robust Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is effective for producing small, high-performance neural networks for classification, but these small networks are vulnerable to adversarial attacks. This paper studies how adversarial robustness transfers from teacher to student during knowledge distillation. We find that a large amount of robustness may be inherited by the student even when distilled on only clean images. Second, we introduce Adversarially Robust Distillation (ARD) for distilling robustness onto student networks. In addition to producing small models with high test accuracy like conventional distillation, ARD also passes the superior robustness of large networks onto the student. In our experiments, we find that ARD student models decisively outperform adversarially trained networks of identical architecture in terms of robust accuracy, surpassing state-of-the-art methods on standard robustness benchmarks. Finally, we adapt recent fast adversarial training methods to ARD for accelerated robust distillation.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Improving the Interpretability of Deep Neural Networks with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep Neural Networks have achieved huge success at a wide spectrum of applications from language modeling, computer vision to speech recognition. However, nowadays, good performance alone is not sufficient to satisfy the needs of practical deployment where interpretability is demanded for cases involving ethics and mission critical applications. The complex models of Deep Neural Networks make it hard to understand and reason the predictions, which hinders its further progress. To tackle this problem, we apply the Knowledge Distillation technique to distill Deep Neural Networks into decision trees in order to attain good performance and interpretability simultaneously. We formulate the problem at hand as a multi-output regression problem and the experiments demonstrate that the student model achieves significantly better accuracy performance (about 1\% to 5\%) than vanilla decision trees at the same level of tree depth. The experiments are implemented on the TensorFlow platform to make it scalable to big datasets. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to distill Deep Neural Networks into vanilla decision trees on multi-class datasets.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Path to Deployable NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained models deliver state-of-the-art results in many NLP tasks but are often too large or too costly for real-world deployment. Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques enable retaining much of the teacher's performance while reducing model size and inference cost. Advances in task-aware, layer-wise, data-free, and adversarially-informed distillation methods demonstrate that KD can address capacity mismatch, data scarcity, robustness, and heterogeneity in deployment environments, making it a central tool for practical NLP systems.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers behavior from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce latency, memory, and computation while retaining much of the teacher's performance. Across vision, language, and graph domains, KD has been applied as logit matching, intermediate-feature alignment, adversarial transfer, and data- or task-aware synthesis. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD often acts both as a source of extra task signal and as a regularizer; practical systems combine KD with pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, and data strategies to meet deployment constraints. Important open issues include data heterogeneity, teacher–student capacity mismatch, privacy-preserving releases, and closing remaining gaps in robustness and domain generalization.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, and Composable Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly practical approach for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, efficient models suitable for deployment. Across vision and language tasks, KD enables substantial reductions in parameter count and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. Its strengths come from flexibility in what to transfer (logits, intermediate features, optimization signals), its compatibility with architecture search and other compression primitives, and its ability to operate under constrained or private-data scenarios. KD is not a one-size-fits-all remedy: practitioners should select KD variants and complementary techniques guided by task requirements, data availability, and deployment constraints to balance fidelity, robustness, and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Humphrey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Versatile Path to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) offers a pragmatic route to compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. Across modalities and tasks, KD can transfer predictive behavior, representations, or task-specific inductive biases; when combined with pre-training, architecture search, or careful data handling, it enables compact models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its effectiveness depends on the choice of what is distilled (logits vs. features), how teachers and students are chosen or trained, the availability and quality of data (including synthetic or unlabeled public data), and auxiliary techniques such as projectors, multi-teacher weighting, or meta-learning to adapt the teaching process. I argue that with these design choices attended to, KD is a broadly applicable and cost-effective strategy for model compression in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, broadly applicable route to compressing large models into smaller, faster ones for deployment in resource- and privacy-constrained settings. When combined with complementary techniques (e.g., architecture-aware design, data augmentation, and privacy mechanisms), KD consistently yields strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across modalities. However, realizing those gains requires careful choices about what to transfer (logits, features, attention), how to select or synthesize data, and how to mitigate transferred harms (bias, privacy leakage). This paper argues that KD should be treated as a central, flexible tool for model compression while emphasizing practical design principles and known failure modes that practitioners must address.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Practical NLP Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical, flexible pathway to deploy high-performing deep learning and NLP models under real-world constraints. By transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or inductive biases from large or multi-modal teachers to smaller students, distillation enables task- and domain-specific compression, faster inference, privacy-preserving distributed training, and architectural simplification. Effective distillation requires methods that match the target deployment needs—task-awareness, layer alignment, careful use of data augmentation and teacher ensembles, and scaling strategies for large datasets and distributed settings. When designed deliberately, distillation yields compressed models that retain much of the teacher's capability while meeting latency, size, and privacy requirements.

papers_seen.author: Peters
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or other forms of learned structure so students retain much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost. KD has evolved from simple soft-target matching to a broad toolkit that includes feature- and representation-level objectives, multi-teacher schemes, data- and privacy-aware variants, and combinations with pruning or quantization. Practical application requires task- and deployment-aware choices that balance accuracy, latency, data availability, and social/robustness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Walton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential, Practical Strategy for Compressing Deep Models in NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques are indispensable for deploying high-capacity deep and language models in resource-constrained settings. By transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teachers to smaller students, practitioners can achieve large reductions in model size and latency while retaining most task performance. However, realizing these gains reliably requires attention to what is transferred (logits, features, relations), how teachers and data are chosen, and hardware- or deployment-aware compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: A Deep Hierarchical Approach to Lifelong Learning in Minecraft
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a lifelong learning system that has the ability to reuse and transfer knowledge from one task to another while efficiently retaining the previously learned knowledge-base. Knowledge is transferred by learning reusable skills to solve tasks in Minecraft, a popular video game which is an unsolved and high-dimensional lifelong learning problem. These reusable skills, which we refer to as Deep Skill Networks, are then incorporated into our novel Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning Network (H-DRLN) architecture using two techniques: (1) a deep skill array and (2) skill distillation, our novel variation of policy distillation (Rusu et. al. 2015) for learning skills. Skill distillation enables the HDRLN to efficiently retain knowledge and therefore scale in lifelong learning, by accumulating knowledge and encapsulating multiple reusable skills into a single distilled network. The H-DRLN exhibits superior performance and lower learning sample complexity compared to the regular Deep Q Network (Mnih et. al. 2015) in sub-domains of Minecraft.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Compressing and Adapting NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a principled way to produce small, fast models that retain much of the performance of larger networks. In natural language processing, where modern pretrained models are large and domain shifts are common, KD enables domain adaptation, latency- and memory-constrained deployment, continual learning, and improved robustness when applied with the right strategies. Practical success relies on combining methods — e.g., multi-stage distillation, selective or curriculum-driven example selection, leveraging soft targets as regularizers, and using adversarial or synthetic data when original data are unavailable. When applied thoughtfully, KD is not merely an implementation detail of model compression but a versatile lever for engineering efficient, accurate, and robust NLP systems.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Show, Attend and Distill:Knowledge Distillation via Attention-based Feature Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation extracts general knowledge from a pre-trained teacher network and provides guidance to a target student network. Most studies manually tie intermediate features of the teacher and student, and transfer knowledge through pre-defined links. However, manual selection often constructs ineffective links that limit the improvement from the distillation. There has been an attempt to address the problem, but it is still challenging to identify effective links under practical scenarios. In this paper, we introduce an effective and efficient feature distillation method utilizing all the feature levels of the teacher without manually selecting the links. Specifically, our method utilizes an attention-based meta-network that learns relative similarities between features, and applies identified similarities to control distillation intensities of all possible pairs. As a result, our method determines competent links more efficiently than the previous approach and provides better performance on model compression and transfer learning tasks. Further qualitative analyses and ablative studies describe how our method contributes to better distillation. The implementation code is available at github.com/clovaai/attention-feature-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a flexible, empirically effective route to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of the teacher's performance. KD can be adapted across modalities and constraints—by matching soft logits, intermediate representations, or attention maps; by using ensembles or teacher optimization; and by operating with or without original training data—making it well suited to real-world deployment needs. Because its effectiveness depends on representation alignment, teacher–student design, and data regime, KD is best applied as a component in broader compression pipelines (combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware choices) and selected to fit the target task and constraints.

papers_seen.author: Larson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from larger teacher models to smaller students to reduce inference cost, memory, and latency while preserving performance. Methods extend beyond matching soft output logits to include intermediate feature/representation matching, layer-wise alignment, adversarial or curriculum-driven sample selection, and data-free or privacy-aware synthesis. Distillation is widely applicable across modalities (vision, speech, language, multimodal) and use cases (on-device deployment, federated learning, low-precision inference), but success depends on careful choices about which signals to transfer, how to handle data availability or heterogeneity, and how to align teacher and student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Variants, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, faster ones by transferring information from a teacher to a student. Research has explored diverse transfer signals (soft outputs, internal representations, layer mappings), different training regimes (data-driven, data-free, adversarial, federated), and task- or resource-aware designs that trade accuracy for latency and memory. Methods have been applied across vision, language, multimodal, and distributed settings, producing widely varying compression ratios and runtime improvements while raising challenges in alignment, stability, and privacy. The field continues to diversify through architecture-aware searches, self-distillation, and mechanisms that adapt teachers to be more student-friendly.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad family of techniques for transferring information from large, often expensive teacher models to smaller, cheaper student models so they retain much of the teacher's performance while reducing inference cost. KD methods operate at different levels (logits, intermediate features, modules or entire architectures) and are applied across domains including vision, speech, NLP and federated settings. Contemporary work has advanced new losses, layer-alignment strategies, module-replacement schemes, robustness-aware procedures, and analyses that clarify when and why distillation helps. Important practical challenges remain around heterogeneous data, strong teachers, and preserving properties such as robustness, generalization across distributions, and multimodal capability.

papers_seen.author: House
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Principled, Practical, and Context-Sensitive Toolbox for NLP Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an essential approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable systems. When treated as a flexible framework rather than a single recipe, KD can preserve much of teacher performance while meeting constraints of latency, memory, privacy, and domain heterogeneity. However, its success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to adapt to new domains or architectures, and how to select or synthesize training signals for the student.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Is Label Smoothing Truly Incompatible with Knowledge Distillation: An Empirical Study
papers_seen.abstract: This work aims to empirically clarify a recently discovered perspective that label smoothing is incompatible with knowledge distillation. We begin by introducing the motivation behind on how this incompatibility is raised, i.e., label smoothing erases relative information between teacher logits. We provide a novel connection on how label smoothing affects distributions of semantically similar and dissimilar classes. Then we propose a metric to quantitatively measure the degree of erased information in sample's representation. After that, we study its one-sidedness and imperfection of the incompatibility view through massive analyses, visualizations and comprehensive experiments on Image Classification, Binary Networks, and Neural Machine Translation. Finally, we broadly discuss several circumstances wherein label smoothing will indeed lose its effectiveness. Project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/LS_and_KD/index.html.

papers_seen.author: Gaines
papers_seen.title: AdaBERT: Task-Adaptive BERT Compression with Differentiable Neural Architecture Search
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained language models such as BERT have shown their effectiveness in various natural language processing tasks. However, the huge parameter size makes them difficult to be deployed in real-time applications that require quick inference with limited resources. Existing methods compress BERT into small models while such compression is task-independent, i.e., the same compressed BERT for all different downstream tasks. Motivated by the necessity and benefits of task-oriented BERT compression, we propose a novel compression method, AdaBERT, that leverages differentiable Neural Architecture Search to automatically compress BERT into task-adaptive small models for specific tasks. We incorporate a task-oriented knowledge distillation loss to provide search hints and an efficiency-aware loss as search constraints, which enables a good trade-off between efficiency and effectiveness for task-adaptive BERT compression. We evaluate AdaBERT on several NLP tasks, and the results demonstrate that those task-adaptive compressed models are 12.7x to 29.3x faster than BERT in inference time and 11.5x to 17.0x smaller in terms of parameter size, while comparable performance is maintained.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Confidence-Aware Multi-Teacher Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is initially introduced to utilize additional supervision from a single teacher model for the student model training. To boost the student performance, some recent variants attempt to exploit diverse knowledge sources from multiple teachers. However, existing studies mainly integrate knowledge from diverse sources by averaging over multiple teacher predictions or combining them using other various label-free strategies, which may mislead student in the presence of low-quality teacher predictions. To tackle this problem, we propose Confidence-Aware Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (CA-MKD), which adaptively assigns sample-wise reliability for each teacher prediction with the help of ground-truth labels, with those teacher predictions close to one-hot labels assigned large weights. Besides, CA-MKD incorporates intermediate layers to stable the knowledge transfer process. Extensive experiments show that our CA-MKD consistently outperforms all compared state-of-the-art methods across various teacher-student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students while retaining much of the teacher's behavior. A growing literature shows KD can act via soft-target matching, intermediate representation transfer, attention- or relation-based losses, self-distillation, online and data-free variants, and can be combined with pruning, layer-skipping, quantization, or architecture search. KD delivers strong empirical gains across modalities (vision, language, recommendation, and graphs) when its signal, data strategy, and optimization schedule are chosen to match the deployment constraints. Important open issues remain — handling rare or low-frequency behaviors, adapting across domains and heterogeneous architectures, and operating under strict privacy or data-availability constraints — but pragmatic pipelines that mix KD with complementary compression tools offer the most reliable path to deployable compact models.

papers_seen.author: Munoz
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression methods form a broad set of techniques for transferring information from large or ensemble models into smaller, faster, or more interpretable models. These techniques are applied across modalities (vision, language, multimodal), deployment scenarios (edge devices, federated learning), and objectives (accuracy preservation, efficiency, interpretability, fairness). Advances include theoretical reframings that connect KD to regularization, a range of strategies for aligning outputs and internal representations, methods that restructure or progressively replace model components, and practical systems that enable heterogeneous and privacy-sensitive deployments. Despite clear empirical gains, open problems remain in understanding when and why different distillation targets (soft outputs, internal features, attention maps, module behavior) are most effective, and how to balance compression with robustness and interpretability.

papers_seen.author: Roman
papers_seen.title: Fair Feature Distillation for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: Fairness is becoming an increasingly crucial issue for computer vision, especially in the human-related decision systems. However, achieving algorithmic fairness, which makes a model produce indiscriminative outcomes against protected groups, is still an unresolved problem. In this paper, we devise a systematic approach which reduces algorithmic biases via feature distillation for visual recognition tasks, dubbed as MMD-based Fair Distillation (MFD). While the distillation technique has been widely used in general to improve the prediction accuracy, to the best of our knowledge, there has been no explicit work that also tries to improve fairness via distillation. Furthermore, We give a theoretical justification of our MFD on the effect of knowledge distillation and fairness. Throughout the extensive experiments, we show our MFD significantly mitigates the bias against specific minorities without any loss of the accuracy on both synthetic and real-world face datasets.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Apprentice: Using Knowledge Distillation Techniques To Improve Low-Precision Network Accuracy
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning networks have achieved state-of-the-art accuracies on computer vision workloads like image classification and object detection. The performant systems, however, typically involve big models with numerous parameters. Once trained, a challenging aspect for such top performing models is deployment on resource constrained inference systems - the models (often deep networks or wide networks or both) are compute and memory intensive. Low-precision numerics and model compression using knowledge distillation are popular techniques to lower both the compute requirements and memory footprint of these deployed models. In this paper, we study the combination of these two techniques and show that the performance of low-precision networks can be significantly improved by using knowledge distillation techniques. Our approach, Apprentice, achieves state-of-the-art accuracies using ternary precision and 4-bit precision for variants of ResNet architecture on ImageNet dataset. We present three schemes using which one can apply knowledge distillation techniques to various stages of the train-and-deploy pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. Across vision and language tasks KD supports deployment to resource-constrained devices, data-scarce regimes, and domain adaptation. Effective distillation combines teacher-to-student signal design (soft outputs, features, attention or relational cues), data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or online generation), and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture modification). While KD often produces strong size–performance tradeoffs, practical success depends on addressing capacity mismatch, domain shift, and signal selection so the student can absorb the teacher’s knowledge.

papers_seen.author: Riley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is not merely a model-compression trick but a central, practical paradigm for deploying high-performance deep and NLP models under real-world constraints. KD can compress large pre-trained models into lightweight students, transfer inductive biases, improve robustness and generalization, enable low-precision and privacy-aware deployments, and adapt to data- or compute-limited settings. Effective distillation couples soft-label transfer with representation-level alignment, task-aware architecture choices, and complementary techniques (quantization, pruning, augmentation). However, KD must be applied carefully: teacher–student mismatches, bias transfer, domain shift, and limited-data regimes require method choices such as feature mimicking, teacher ensembles, teacher-free objectives, or fairness-aware augmentations. The result is a flexible toolkit that—when combined with architectural and data strategies—makes high-quality, efficient models feasible for production NLP and deep-learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Imperative for Deploying Large NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained models have driven major NLP advances but are often impractical for real-world deployment because of size, latency, privacy, and data-distribution constraints. Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression strategies enable retaining most of a large model's performance while producing models that meet latency, memory, and regulatory requirements. Effective KD encompasses diverse techniques — task-adaptive compression, feature mimicking, data-free distillation, teacher meta-learning, privacy-aware distillation, and distributed/continual distillation — which together form a practical toolkit for making state-of-the-art NLP useful at scale.
