papers_seen.author: Heath
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and flexible approach for producing smaller, faster models from larger teachers across vision, language, speech, and multimodal settings. Methods range from matching teacher logits to aligning intermediate representations, ensembling or self-teaching, and combining distillation with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of a teacher's performance while enabling deployment under compute, memory, privacy, and latency constraints, but effectiveness depends on choices of distilled signals, data and augmentations, teacher–student alignment, and task-aware pipeline design.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Design-Sensitive Path to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly useful family of techniques for transferring behavior from large teacher models to smaller students to reduce inference cost and enable deployment. KD has been instantiated as matching soft targets, aligning intermediate representations, progressive module replacement, and selective or multi-teacher schemes. While KD often yields strong empirical gains and enables domain- and task-specific compression, its success depends on optimization dynamics, the choice of distilled signal, data quality and selection, and teacher–student alignment. Careful method choices make KD a reliable, production-ready compression strategy, but it is not a universal shortcut: practitioners must tailor KD objectives and protocols to their constraints and goals.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: A Closer Look at Deep Learning Heuristics: Learning rate restarts, Warmup and Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The convergence rate and final performance of common deep learning models have significantly benefited from heuristics such as learning rate schedules, knowledge distillation, skip connections, and normalization layers. In the absence of theoretical underpinnings, controlled experiments aimed at explaining these strategies can aid our understanding of deep learning landscapes and the training dynamics. Existing approaches for empirical analysis rely on tools of linear interpolation and visualizations with dimensionality reduction, each with their limitations. Instead, we revisit such analysis of heuristics through the lens of recently proposed methods for loss surface and representation analysis, viz., mode connectivity and canonical correlation analysis (CCA), and hypothesize reasons for the success of the heuristics. In particular, we explore knowledge distillation and learning rate heuristics of (cosine) restarts and warmup using mode connectivity and CCA. Our empirical analysis suggests that: (a) the reasons often quoted for the success of cosine annealing are not evidenced in practice; (b) that the effect of learning rate warmup is to prevent the deeper layers from creating training instability; and (c) that the latent knowledge shared by the teacher is primarily disbursed to the deeper layers.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Unifying Heterogeneous Classifiers with Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we study the problem of unifying knowledge from a set of classifiers with different architectures and target classes into a single classifier, given only a generic set of unlabelled data. We call this problem Unifying Heterogeneous Classifiers (UHC). This problem is motivated by scenarios where data is collected from multiple sources, but the sources cannot share their data, e.g., due to privacy concerns, and only privately trained models can be shared. In addition, each source may not be able to gather data to train all classes due to data availability at each source, and may not be able to train the same classification model due to different computational resources. To tackle this problem, we propose a generalisation of knowledge distillation to merge HCs. We derive a probabilistic relation between the outputs of HCs and the probability over all classes. Based on this relation, we propose two classes of methods based on cross-entropy minimisation and matrix factorisation, which allow us to estimate soft labels over all classes from unlabelled samples and use them in lieu of ground truth labels to train a unified classifier. Our extensive experiments on ImageNet, LSUN, and Places365 datasets show that our approaches significantly outperform a naive extension of distillation and can achieve almost the same accuracy as classifiers that are trained in a centralised, supervised manner.

papers_seen.author: Allen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practical Principles, and Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques transfer knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models so that compact systems approach teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. Work across vision and NLP shows that effective compression combines multiple strategies — soft-label matching, intermediate representation alignment, architecture-aware design, data- and privacy-aware workflows, and adversarial or ensemble consolidation — and that practical gains depend on addressing representation mismatch, optimization dynamics, and task or domain shifts. This synthesis summarizes prevailing methods, empirical patterns, and recurring trade-offs relevant for practitioners aiming to deploy efficient models in resource- or data-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques provide practical routes to deploy large, high-performance neural models in resource- constrained or latency-sensitive settings. Methods vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, relational structure), how training data is used or synthesized, and whether compression is task-agnostic or task-adaptive. In natural language tasks, KD has enabled dramatic size and speed gains for large pretrained models (e.g., BERT) as well as the feasibility of simple architectures that retain most of the original performance. Despite empirical success, challenges remain: choosing what to transfer for maximal utility, constructing or selecting suitable training examples, handling heterogeneous or private data (federated or data-free settings), and designing teacher-student curricula or architectures that improve transfer. Emerging directions include task-adaptive compression, many-to-many layer alignment, multi-teacher and teacher-aware training, and principled approaches to data selection or generation during distillation.

papers_seen.author: Bowman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger, expensive models (teachers) to smaller, efficient models (students). KD has been applied across vision, language, generative modeling, and privacy-sensitive settings to reduce storage, latency, and energy while attempting to preserve accuracy and desirable properties. Practical approaches range from soft-label matching and feature imitation to many-to-many layer mappings and self-distillation; theoretical work links KD to regularization effects and label smoothing. Despite clear empirical successes in compressing large pretrained language models and vision networks, important challenges remain: students often fail to replicate teachers' internal representations, robustness and fairness do not automatically transfer, and privacy or heterogeneous-data settings impose additional constraints. Ongoing advances focus on richer targets (internal features, layer mappings), alternate training regimes (self- and teacher-free distillation), and task-aware strategies for robust and private compression.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Preserving Privacy in Federated Learning with Ensemble Cross-Domain Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is a machine learning paradigm where local nodes collaboratively train a central model while the training data remains decentralized. Existing FL methods typically share model parameters or employ co-distillation to address the issue of unbalanced data distribution. However, they suffer from communication bottlenecks. More importantly, they risk privacy leakage. In this work, we develop a privacy preserving and communication efficient method in a FL framework with one-shot offline knowledge distillation using unlabeled, cross-domain public data. We propose a quantized and noisy ensemble of local predictions from completely trained local models for stronger privacy guarantees without sacrificing accuracy. Based on extensive experiments on image classification and text classification tasks, we show that our privacy-preserving method outperforms baseline FL algorithms with superior performance in both accuracy and communication efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Cameron
papers_seen.title: Well-Read Students Learn Better: On the Importance of Pre-training Compact Models
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in natural language representations have been accompanied by large and expensive models that leverage vast amounts of general-domain text through self-supervised pre-training. Due to the cost of applying such models to down-stream tasks, several model compression techniques on pre-trained language representations have been proposed (Sun et al., 2019; Sanh, 2019). However, surprisingly, the simple baseline of just pre-training and fine-tuning compact models has been overlooked. In this paper, we first show that pre-training remains important in the context of smaller architectures, and fine-tuning pre-trained compact models can be competitive to more elaborate methods proposed in concurrent work. Starting with pre-trained compact models, we then explore transferring task knowledge from large fine-tuned models through standard knowledge distillation. The resulting simple, yet effective and general algorithm, Pre-trained Distillation, brings further improvements. Through extensive experiments, we more generally explore the interaction between pre-training and distillation under two variables that have been under-studied: model size and properties of unlabeled task data. One surprising observation is that they have a compound effect even when sequentially applied on the same data. To accelerate future research, we will make our 24 pre-trained miniature BERT models publicly available.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation for Deep Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in model compression have provided procedures for compressing large neural networks to a fraction of their original size while retaining most if not all of their accuracy. However, all of these approaches rely on access to the original training set, which might not always be possible if the network to be compressed was trained on a very large dataset, or on a dataset whose release poses privacy or safety concerns as may be the case for biometrics tasks. We present a method for data-free knowledge distillation, which is able to compress deep neural networks trained on large-scale datasets to a fraction of their size leveraging only some extra metadata to be provided with a pretrained model release. We also explore different kinds of metadata that can be used with our method, and discuss tradeoffs involved in using each of them.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Versatile Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable ones while retaining much of their effectiveness. When combined with task-specific adaptations (layer mapping, data-free synthesis, federated protocols, quantization, or self-supervision), KD enables deployment in low-resource, privacy-sensitive, and domain-specific settings. Success depends on designing appropriate alignment mechanisms, data strategies, and fairness safeguards.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large models by transferring information from a high-capacity teacher to a smaller student, using signals beyond hard labels to preserve generalization while reducing compute and memory. Modern work expands KD beyond soft logits to intermediate features, layer mappings, adversarial and attention-based objectives, and data- or resource-constrained settings. Empirical results across vision, speech and NLP show that tailored distillation strategies can recover much of a teacher's performance in compact models, though challenges remain in data-free scenarios, handling imperfect teachers, and preserving rare-token fidelity in sequence tasks.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: BERT Learns to Teach: Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning
papers_seen.abstract: We present Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning (MetaDistil), a simple yet effective alternative to traditional knowledge distillation (KD) methods where the teacher model is fixed during training. We show the teacher network can learn to better transfer knowledge to the student network (i.e., learning to teach) with the feedback from the performance of the distilled student network in a meta learning framework. Moreover, we introduce a pilot update mechanism to improve the alignment between the inner-learner and meta-learner in meta learning algorithms that focus on an improved inner-learner. Experiments on various benchmarks show that MetaDistil can yield significant improvements compared with traditional KD algorithms and is less sensitive to the choice of different student capacity and hyperparameters, facilitating the use of KD on different tasks and models.

papers_seen.author: Mcclain
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multi-Modal Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an essential and versatile approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable models across NLP and vision domains. When adapted to task and deployment constraints—via multi-teacher schedules, feature-level objectives, data-free synthesis, online protocols, or privacy-aware ensembles—KD both preserves quality and addresses communication, privacy, and compute bottlenecks. However, KD is not a panacea: dataset heterogeneity and optimization mismatches can limit its effectiveness, so careful method selection and engineering are required for robust compression in real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Path to Deployable Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical framework for producing compact, faster models that retain much of the capability of larger teachers. Beyond simple logit matching, modern KD leverages internal representation transfer, selective data strategies, and integration with pruning, architecture search, or federated protocols to meet latency, privacy, and device-heterogeneity constraints. When applied thoughtfully, KD enables efficient deployment across modalities while posing clear methodological trade-offs and open challenges that guide future research.

papers_seen.author: Parsons
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Compressing NLP and Deep Learning Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a practical and flexible route to compress large neural models for real-world deployment. When applied carefully — via multi-stage pipelines, layer-aware mappings, internal-representation transfer, self-distillation, or even without original data — KD can preserve much of the teacher performance while reducing latency and memory. KD also composes effectively with orthogonal compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet diverse resource constraints. These properties make KD a central technique for bringing large pretrained models into production in NLP and other domains.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression strategies enable smaller, faster models to inherit performance from larger teachers by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or ensemble knowledge. Techniques range from logit-based soft-target distillation to feature- and attention-level mimicry, multi-teacher and task-adaptive pipelines, and methods that relax the need for original training data or strong teachers. Across computer vision and natural language processing tasks, distilled students can approach teacher accuracy while drastically reducing parameters and latency; complementary strategies such as careful pre-training of compact models and architecture search further improve trade-offs between efficiency and effectiveness. Key challenges remain in preserving rare-token behavior, aligning heterogeneous teacher–student inputs, and ensuring privacy and robustness during compression.

papers_seen.author: Whitehead
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce computation, memory, and latency while retaining much of the original performance. KD encompasses a family of techniques — matching soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, using multi-stage or curriculum schemes, and combining distillation with other compression methods — and is widely used for deploying models in resource-constrained or privacy-sensitive settings. Success depends on matching distillation objectives and data strategies to deployment goals and student capacity.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Efficient Transformer-based Large Scale Language Representations using Hardware-friendly Block Structured Pruning
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained large-scale language models have increasingly demonstrated high accuracy on many natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, the limited weight storage and computational speed on hardware platforms have impeded the popularity of pre-trained models, especially in the era of edge computing. In this work, we propose an efficient transformer-based large-scale language representation using hardware-friendly block structure pruning. We incorporate the reweighted group Lasso into block-structured pruning for optimization. Besides the significantly reduced weight storage and computation, the proposed approach achieves high compression rates. Experimental results on different models (BERT, RoBERTa, and DistilBERT) on the General Language Understanding Evaluation (GLUE) benchmark tasks show that we achieve up to 5.0x with zero or minor accuracy degradation on certain task(s). Our proposed method is also orthogonal to existing compact pre-trained language models such as DistilBERT using knowledge distillation, since a further 1.79x average compression rate can be achieved on top of DistilBERT with zero or minor accuracy degradation. It is suitable to deploy the final compressed model on resource-constrained edge devices.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: FedZKT: Zero-Shot Knowledge Transfer towards Resource-Constrained Federated Learning with Heterogeneous On-Device Models
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning enables multiple distributed devices to collaboratively learn a shared prediction model without centralizing their on-device data. Most of the current algorithms require comparable individual efforts for local training with the same structure and size of on-device models, which, however, impedes participation from resource-constrained devices. Given the widespread yet heterogeneous devices nowadays, in this paper, we propose an innovative federated learning framework with heterogeneous on-device models through Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer, named by FedZKT. Specifically, FedZKT allows devices to independently determine the on-device models upon their local resources. To achieve knowledge transfer across these heterogeneous on-device models, a zero-shot distillation approach is designed without any prerequisites for private on-device data, which is contrary to certain prior research based on a public dataset or a pre-trained data generator. Moreover, this compute-intensive distillation task is assigned to the server to allow the participation of resource-constrained devices, where a generator is adversarially learned with the ensemble of collected on-device models. The distilled central knowledge is then sent back in the form of the corresponding on-device model parameters, which can be easily absorbed on the device side. Extensive experimental studies demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of FedZKT towards on-device knowledge agnostic, on-device model heterogeneity, and other challenging federated learning scenarios, such as heterogeneous on-device data and straggler effects.

papers_seen.author: Shaffer
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become central to deploying large deep models in resource-constrained settings. Research spans a range of goals — shrinking model size and latency, preserving privacy, enabling distributed learning, and retaining task- or robustness-related properties — and a correspondingly diverse set of techniques including logit and feature matching, layer-wise and many-to-many mapping, adversarial generation of training examples, and architecture-aware pruning and replacement. Empirical work shows effective trade-offs across vision, multimodal, and language tasks, while recent methods also tackle practical constraints such as lack of original data, privacy requirements, and distributed communication budgets.

papers_seen.author: Hurst
papers_seen.title: Contemporary Approaches and Applications of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques transfer information from larger, more costly models to smaller, deployable models. Modern work expands beyond simple soft-label matching to include distillation of internal representations, feature-level imitation, privacy-preserving and data-free strategies, task-adaptive compression, and adaptations to specialized architectures (e.g., GANs, detectors, and transformers). These methods aim to preserve accuracy, robustness, and efficiency (compute, memory, or communication) while enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices or in privacy-sensitive and distributed settings.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Effective Knowledge Distillation: Representation, Selection, and Practical Constraints
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach to compress and adapt large deep models for deployment in resource- or privacy-constrained settings. Effective distillation goes beyond matching teacher logits: transferring internal representations, choosing which teacher signals to trust, and accommodating deployment constraints (limited data, communication, low-precision hardware) are all decisive. I argue that the most reliable distillation pipelines combine representation-level objectives, selective/sample-aware strategies, and engineering choices that address privacy and efficiency, yielding compact students that retain teacher strengths across NLP, vision, and graph domains.

papers_seen.author: Zamora
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, cheaper students by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. The family of KD methods includes soft-target (logit) matching, feature- and layer-wise alignment, relational and module-level transfer, data-free or zero-shot synthesis, and integration with architecture search or federated training. Practical deployments balance what is transferred with student capacity, data availability, privacy constraints, and device heterogeneity; empirical work shows KD often preserves much of teacher performance while enabling lower latency, smaller models, and domain specialization, but open challenges remain around robustness, domain shift, and principled selection of distilled signals.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation transfers information from large teacher models to smaller students to reduce inference cost and memory while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. Modern distillation expands beyond matching teacher logits to include intermediate representation matching, self-supervised and contrastive objectives, data-free and synthetic-data schemes, curriculum and augmentation strategies, and privacy- and deployment-aware protocols. These variants enable application across vision, speech, graph-structured data, and NLP, but practical deployment requires care about data availability, optimization dynamics, robustness, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Federated Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Distributed learning frameworks often rely on exchanging model parameters across workers, instead of revealing their raw data. A prime example is federated learning that exchanges the gradients or weights of each neural network model. Under limited communication resources, however, such a method becomes extremely costly particularly for modern deep neural networks having a huge number of model parameters. In this regard, federated distillation (FD) is a compelling distributed learning solution that only exchanges the model outputs whose dimensions are commonly much smaller than the model sizes (e.g., 10 labels in the MNIST dataset). The goal of this chapter is to provide a deep understanding of FD while demonstrating its communication efficiency and applicability to a variety of tasks. To this end, towards demystifying the operational principle of FD, the first part of this chapter provides a novel asymptotic analysis for two foundational algorithms of FD, namely knowledge distillation (KD) and co-distillation (CD), by exploiting the theory of neural tangent kernel (NTK). Next, the second part elaborates on a baseline implementation of FD for a classification task, and illustrates its performance in terms of accuracy and communication efficiency compared to FL. Lastly, to demonstrate the applicability of FD to various distributed learning tasks and environments, the third part presents two selected applications, namely FD over asymmetric uplink-and-downlink wireless channels and FD for reinforcement learning.

papers_seen.author: Jordan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models by transferring information from a high-capacity teacher to a smaller student, enabling deployment under computation, memory, and latency constraints. A range of techniques—matching soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, multi-stage pipelines, and data synthesis—have been developed to address diverse practical needs such as on-device inference, privacy-sensitive releases, federated settings, and domain shifts. Combining KD with orthogonal compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and adapting distillation signals to task and deployment constraints yields the best real-world outcomes, while open challenges remain around handling distribution shift, data scarcity, and student–teacher capacity mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Gaines
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques enable smaller or more efficient models to approach the performance of larger teacher models by transferring information through supervisory signals beyond standard hard labels. Across computer vision, speech, and NLP, practitioners apply soft-label distillation, feature- and layer-level imitation, self- and online-distillation, data-free methods, and structural transformations (e.g., pruning or cheap-convolution replacements) to trade off accuracy, latency, and memory for deployability. Empirical work shows strong task-specific gains (often recovering much of the teacher’s quality) while recent methodological and theoretical studies clarify when and why different forms of distillation help. Open challenges remain in data scarcity or privacy, matching features across heterogeneous architectures, and designing distillation schedules that manage regularization versus bias. The literature suggests combined approaches—mixing logits, intermediate features, architectural compression, and distributed or data-free strategies—are effective practical pathways for producing compact, high-performing models for real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Osborne
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge from Deep Networks with Applications to Healthcare Domain
papers_seen.abstract: Exponential growth in Electronic Healthcare Records (EHR) has resulted in new opportunities and urgent needs for discovery of meaningful data-driven representations and patterns of diseases in Computational Phenotyping research. Deep Learning models have shown superior performance for robust prediction in computational phenotyping tasks, but suffer from the issue of model interpretability which is crucial for clinicians involved in decision-making. In this paper, we introduce a novel knowledge-distillation approach called Interpretable Mimic Learning, to learn interpretable phenotype features for making robust prediction while mimicking the performance of deep learning models. Our framework uses Gradient Boosting Trees to learn interpretable features from deep learning models such as Stacked Denoising Autoencoder and Long Short-Term Memory. Exhaustive experiments on a real-world clinical time-series dataset show that our method obtains similar or better performance than the deep learning models, and it provides interpretable phenotypes for clinical decision making.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression in NLP and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable ones while retaining much of their performance. Across NLP, speech, vision-language, and multimodal tasks, distillation techniques—including self-distillation, layer-wise/task-aware distillation, and teacher adaptation—enable substantial reductions in model size and compute with limited accuracy loss. KD is complementary to other compression strategies (e.g., pruning and architecture search) and benefits from careful choices in intermediate-target selection, data augmentation, and teacher-student alignment. When combined thoughtfully with task adaptation and hardware-aware techniques, KD unlocks feasible deployment of advanced models in resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Compression: Effective but Context-Sensitive
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful and practical approach to compress large neural models into smaller, faster, or more hardware-friendly students while retaining much of teacher performance. Its effectiveness spans supervised, self-supervised, and cross-modal settings, but the choice of what to transfer (logits, features, intermediate representations, attention), how to measure discrepancy, and how to combine KD with pruning or quantization critically determines success. I argue that KD should be treated as a toolbox of complementary techniques whose components must be matched to task, teacher quality, and deployment constraints to obtain reliable and robust compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Efficient and Responsible NLP and Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical, versatile approach for compressing large models and enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments. Beyond raw compression, KD supports domain adaptation, data-free scenarios, improved inference speed, and novel training regimes for specialized tasks. However, distillation is not a panacea: it can amplify teacher biases, interact with regularization techniques in subtle ways, and benefits most when combined with complementary methods such as architecture-aware training, generator-based sample synthesis, or instance-aware losses.

papers_seen.author: Walls
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large or ensemble teacher models into smaller student models. Across vision, language, graphs, and multimodal problems, KD is used alone or combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data-centric strategies to produce compact models that preserve much of teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. Empirical and analytical work highlights mechanisms behind KD’s success, practical recipes for improving student fidelity, and persistent challenges (data mismatch, rare-token behavior, robustness, and optimization). This synthesis summarizes methods, applications, practical recommendations, and key open problems reported in recent literature.

papers_seen.author: Warner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression and Adaptation in NLP and Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as a central, practical technique for compressing and adapting large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD is versatile: it transfers predictive behavior, intermediate representations, and ensemble knowledge; supports data-free or privacy-sensitive settings; and can improve robustness and calibration when combined with complementary methods. Realizing KD’s full potential requires matching the distillation recipe to deployment goals and addressing failure modes such as optimization mismatches, bias transfer, and poor handling of low-frequency phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Rocha
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Trends
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques aim to transfer predictive power from large teacher models into smaller, faster, or more private student models while retaining most of the original performance. Work across vision and language has expanded KD beyond simple logit matching into data-centric methods (augmentation and mixup), layer- and representation-level transfers, task-adaptive architecture search, data-free and privacy-aware distillation, and unified pipelines that combine pruning or structural compression with distillation. The field blends empirical engineering (speed/size trade-offs) with emerging theoretical analyses that help explain when and why distillation helps.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Towards Understanding Ensemble, Knowledge Distillation and Self-Distillation in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: We formally study how ensemble of deep learning models can improve test accuracy, and how the superior performance of ensemble can be distilled into a single model using knowledge distillation. We consider the challenging case where the ensemble is simply an average of the outputs of a few independently trained neural networks with the SAME architecture, trained using the SAME algorithm on the SAME data set, and they only differ by the random seeds used in the initialization.   We show that ensemble/knowledge distillation in Deep Learning works very differently from traditional learning theory (such as boosting or NTKs, neural tangent kernels). To properly understand them, we develop a theory showing that when data has a structure we refer to as ``multi-view'', then ensemble of independently trained neural networks can provably improve test accuracy, and such superior test accuracy can also be provably distilled into a single model by training a single model to match the output of the ensemble instead of the true label. Our result sheds light on how ensemble works in deep learning in a way that is completely different from traditional theorems, and how the ``dark knowledge'' is hidden in the outputs of the ensemble and can be used in distillation. In the end, we prove that self-distillation can also be viewed as implicitly combining ensemble and knowledge distillation to improve test accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Why and How Knowledge Distillation Enables Practical Compression for Deep NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained and ensemble models deliver state-of-the-art accuracy in NLP and other deep learning domains but are often too large or slow for real-world deployment. Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques provide principled ways to transfer predictive behaviour and internal representations from expensive teachers into compact students. When combined with careful pre-training, feature-level matching, layer-mapping strategies, data augmentation, and curriculum design, distillation yields models that approach teacher accuracy while reducing inference cost by an order of magnitude or more. This paper argues that KD is both necessary and practical for deploying high-quality compact models and outlines concrete, evidence-backed strategies to maximize its effectiveness.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: On Representation Knowledge Distillation for Graph Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a learning paradigm for boosting resource-efficient graph neural networks (GNNs) using more expressive yet cumbersome teacher models. Past work on distillation for GNNs proposed the Local Structure Preserving loss (LSP), which matches local structural relationships defined over edges across the student and teacher's node embeddings. This paper studies whether preserving the global topology of how the teacher embeds graph data can be a more effective distillation objective for GNNs, as real-world graphs often contain latent interactions and noisy edges. We propose Graph Contrastive Representation Distillation (G-CRD), which uses contrastive learning to implicitly preserve global topology by aligning the student node embeddings to those of the teacher in a shared representation space. Additionally, we introduce an expanded set of benchmarks on large-scale real-world datasets where the performance gap between teacher and student GNNs is non-negligible. Experiments across 4 datasets and 14 heterogeneous GNN architectures show that G-CRD consistently boosts the performance and robustness of lightweight GNNs, outperforming LSP (and a global structure preserving variant of LSP) as well as baselines from 2D computer vision. An analysis of the representational similarity among teacher and student embedding spaces reveals that G-CRD balances preserving local and global relationships, while structure preserving approaches are best at preserving one or the other. Our code is available at https://github.com/chaitjo/efficient-gnns

papers_seen.author: Rhodes
papers_seen.title: Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: It is challenging to perform lifelong language learning (LLL) on a stream of different tasks without any performance degradation comparing to the multi-task counterparts. To address this issue, we present Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation (L2KD), a simple but efficient method that can be easily applied to existing LLL architectures in order to mitigate the degradation. Specifically, when the LLL model is trained on a new task, we assign a teacher model to first learn the new task, and pass the knowledge to the LLL model via knowledge distillation. Therefore, the LLL model can better adapt to the new task while keeping the previously learned knowledge. Experiments show that the proposed L2KD consistently improves previous state-of-the-art models, and the degradation comparing to multi-task models in LLL tasks is well mitigated for both sequence generation and text classification tasks.

papers_seen.author: Montgomery
papers_seen.title: Object DGCNN: 3D Object Detection using Dynamic Graphs
papers_seen.abstract: 3D object detection often involves complicated training and testing pipelines, which require substantial domain knowledge about individual datasets. Inspired by recent non-maximum suppression-free 2D object detection models, we propose a 3D object detection architecture on point clouds. Our method models 3D object detection as message passing on a dynamic graph, generalizing the DGCNN framework to predict a set of objects. In our construction, we remove the necessity of post-processing via object confidence aggregation or non-maximum suppression. To facilitate object detection from sparse point clouds, we also propose a set-to-set distillation approach customized to 3D detection. This approach aligns the outputs of the teacher model and the student model in a permutation-invariant fashion, significantly simplifying knowledge distillation for the 3D detection task. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on autonomous driving benchmarks. We also provide abundant analysis of the detection model and distillation framework.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: FedZKT: Zero-Shot Knowledge Transfer towards Resource-Constrained Federated Learning with Heterogeneous On-Device Models
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning enables multiple distributed devices to collaboratively learn a shared prediction model without centralizing their on-device data. Most of the current algorithms require comparable individual efforts for local training with the same structure and size of on-device models, which, however, impedes participation from resource-constrained devices. Given the widespread yet heterogeneous devices nowadays, in this paper, we propose an innovative federated learning framework with heterogeneous on-device models through Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer, named by FedZKT. Specifically, FedZKT allows devices to independently determine the on-device models upon their local resources. To achieve knowledge transfer across these heterogeneous on-device models, a zero-shot distillation approach is designed without any prerequisites for private on-device data, which is contrary to certain prior research based on a public dataset or a pre-trained data generator. Moreover, this compute-intensive distillation task is assigned to the server to allow the participation of resource-constrained devices, where a generator is adversarially learned with the ensemble of collected on-device models. The distilled central knowledge is then sent back in the form of the corresponding on-device model parameters, which can be easily absorbed on the device side. Extensive experimental studies demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of FedZKT towards on-device knowledge agnostic, on-device model heterogeneity, and other challenging federated learning scenarios, such as heterogeneous on-device data and straggler effects.

papers_seen.author: Cohen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Strategy for Model Compression and Adaptation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach to produce compact models that retain much of the performance of larger models. Beyond simple compression, KD can transfer inductive biases, enable domain adaptation and vocabulary specialization, support privacy-preserving and federated scenarios, work without access to original data, and improve robustness and feature quality when carefully applied. When combined with targeted techniques — feature mimicking, weighted soft labels, projector layers, or adversarial robustness objectives — KD becomes a unifying toolkit to meet latency, capacity, and privacy constraints in real-world NLP and deep learning deployments.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Insights, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large models into smaller, faster ones by transferring information from a teacher to a student. It has been applied across supervised, self-supervised, multimodal and domain-adaptation settings to reduce inference cost while retaining much of the teacher's performance. Progress includes direct soft-target matching, feature- and relation-based imitation, self- and progressive-distillation strategies, and task- or domain-aware adaptations. Empirical work highlights both the power of KD to produce efficient models for deployment and important practical considerations—such as the value of pre-training, the role of data augmentation and sample selection, and computational bottlenecks—that shape effective distillation regimes. Despite advances, optimization mismatches, teacher–student capacity differences, and data-domain shift remain active challenges guiding current research and practice.

papers_seen.author: Maldonado
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques reduce model size or communication cost by transferring knowledge from larger or multiple models (teachers) to smaller or otherwise constrained models (students). Methods vary from matching soft outputs to transferring intermediate features, training teachers to be student-friendly, coordinating multiple teachers, and combining distillation with pruning or federated/online schemes. Empirical and theoretical work highlights how distilled "dark knowledge" improves student generalization, how architectural components (e.g., projectors) shape transfer, and how distillation can be adapted for privacy, heterogeneity, and large-scale or multi-task NLP applications.

papers_seen.author: Hicks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Adaptation: Teaching to Adapt
papers_seen.abstract: Domain adaptation is crucial in many real-world applications where the distribution of the training data differs from the distribution of the test data. Previous Deep Learning-based approaches to domain adaptation need to be trained jointly on source and target domain data and are therefore unappealing in scenarios where models need to be adapted to a large number of domains or where a domain is evolving, e.g. spam detection where attackers continuously change their tactics.   To fill this gap, we propose Knowledge Adaptation, an extension of Knowledge Distillation (Bucilua et al., 2006; Hinton et al., 2015) to the domain adaptation scenario. We show how a student model achieves state-of-the-art results on unsupervised domain adaptation from multiple sources on a standard sentiment analysis benchmark by taking into account the domain-specific expertise of multiple teachers and the similarities between their domains.   When learning from a single teacher, using domain similarity to gauge trustworthiness is inadequate. To this end, we propose a simple metric that correlates well with the teacher's accuracy in the target domain. We demonstrate that incorporating high-confidence examples selected by this metric enables the student model to achieve state-of-the-art performance in the single-source scenario.

papers_seen.author: Osborne
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, more efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal knowledge. Across vision and language tasks, KD is used to reduce inference cost, enable deployment on resource-constrained devices, and retain performance through techniques that go beyond matching final outputs—including intermediate representation imitation, data-aware training, multi-teacher strategies, and teacher-free or data-free approaches. Empirical work demonstrates both consistent gains and important failure modes (e.g., loss of low-frequency lexical information or sensitivity to domain shift), motivating refinements such as internal representation distillation, curriculum or sample selection, data augmentation choices, and dynamic teacher weighting. Open challenges remain in understanding what components of teacher knowledge most benefit students, how to handle heterogeneity between teacher and student architectures, and how to distill effectively without access to original training data.

papers_seen.author: Dudley
papers_seen.title: Attention-Guided Answer Distillation for Machine Reading Comprehension
papers_seen.abstract: Despite that current reading comprehension systems have achieved significant advancements, their promising performances are often obtained at the cost of making an ensemble of numerous models. Besides, existing approaches are also vulnerable to adversarial attacks. This paper tackles these problems by leveraging knowledge distillation, which aims to transfer knowledge from an ensemble model to a single model. We first demonstrate that vanilla knowledge distillation applied to answer span prediction is effective for reading comprehension systems. We then propose two novel approaches that not only penalize the prediction on confusing answers but also guide the training with alignment information distilled from the ensemble. Experiments show that our best student model has only a slight drop of 0.4% F1 on the SQuAD test set compared to the ensemble teacher, while running 12x faster during inference. It even outperforms the teacher on adversarial SQuAD datasets and NarrativeQA benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Powerful, Flexible, but Context-Sensitive for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques are practical, widely applicable tools for shrinking large models and transferring capability to smaller models. KD can preserve performance while reducing inference cost, enable cross-modal and cross-task transfer, and be adapted to constrained settings (few-shot, edge devices). However, KD is not a plug-and-play cure: its benefits depend on what is distilled (logits vs. features vs. internal structure), teacher-student design, data regime, and optimization choices. Careful method design — including feature-based objectives, intermediate-layer alignment, self-distillation or meta-learned teachers, and task-aware curricula — is required to realize robust gains without amplifying teacher errors.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Explaining Knowledge Distillation by Quantifying the Knowledge
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a method to interpret the success of knowledge distillation by quantifying and analyzing task-relevant and task-irrelevant visual concepts that are encoded in intermediate layers of a deep neural network (DNN). More specifically, three hypotheses are proposed as follows. 1. Knowledge distillation makes the DNN learn more visual concepts than learning from raw data. 2. Knowledge distillation ensures that the DNN is prone to learning various visual concepts simultaneously. Whereas, in the scenario of learning from raw data, the DNN learns visual concepts sequentially. 3. Knowledge distillation yields more stable optimization directions than learning from raw data. Accordingly, we design three types of mathematical metrics to evaluate feature representations of the DNN. In experiments, we diagnosed various DNNs, and above hypotheses were verified.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across vision, speech, and language tasks, KD has expanded from simple logit matching to a rich toolbox including feature- and layer-level imitation, self- and progressive-distillation, ensemble compression, data-free or zero-shot approaches, and federated protocols. Empirical work shows KD can yield compact models that retain much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost, but practical success depends on design choices about what to transfer, how to supply or synthesize data, and how to handle teacher–student mismatches and optimization challenges.

papers_seen.author: Donovan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Practical Compression: Essential, Effective, but Context-Sensitive
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students that retain much of teacher performance. KD can yield large speed, storage, and deployment gains across vision, speech, and language when combined with careful choices about what to transfer and how to train. However, success is not automatic: data regime, teacher-student mismatch, optimization dynamics, and downstream robustness or fairness constraints shape outcomes. I argue that KD should be treated as a core tool in model compression pipelines but one that must be adapted to the task, data availability, and deployment constraints through a set of best practices.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Federated Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Distributed learning frameworks often rely on exchanging model parameters across workers, instead of revealing their raw data. A prime example is federated learning that exchanges the gradients or weights of each neural network model. Under limited communication resources, however, such a method becomes extremely costly particularly for modern deep neural networks having a huge number of model parameters. In this regard, federated distillation (FD) is a compelling distributed learning solution that only exchanges the model outputs whose dimensions are commonly much smaller than the model sizes (e.g., 10 labels in the MNIST dataset). The goal of this chapter is to provide a deep understanding of FD while demonstrating its communication efficiency and applicability to a variety of tasks. To this end, towards demystifying the operational principle of FD, the first part of this chapter provides a novel asymptotic analysis for two foundational algorithms of FD, namely knowledge distillation (KD) and co-distillation (CD), by exploiting the theory of neural tangent kernel (NTK). Next, the second part elaborates on a baseline implementation of FD for a classification task, and illustrates its performance in terms of accuracy and communication efficiency compared to FL. Lastly, to demonstrate the applicability of FD to various distributed learning tasks and environments, the third part presents two selected applications, namely FD over asymmetric uplink-and-downlink wireless channels and FD for reinforcement learning.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Strategy for NLP Model Compression: Promise, Proofs, and Precautions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable approach for compressing large NLP and deep learning models into smaller, deployable students. When combined with complementary techniques—such as architecture-aware compression, data augmentation, and data-free synthesis—KD can deliver much of a teacher model’s performance while greatly reducing inference cost and memory. However, distillation is not without limits: it can propagate teacher biases, depends on careful choice of what and how to transfer, and requires task- and data-aware engineering to be robust in low-data or privacy-sensitive settings. A pragmatic pipeline therefore treats KD as the central tool but couples it with targeted strategies for representation alignment, sample selection, and evaluation under deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Blair
papers_seen.title: Distilling Policy Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The transfer of knowledge from one policy to another is an important tool in Deep Reinforcement Learning. This process, referred to as distillation, has been used to great success, for example, by enhancing the optimisation of agents, leading to stronger performance faster, on harder domains [26, 32, 5, 8]. Despite the widespread use and conceptual simplicity of distillation, many different formulations are used in practice, and the subtle variations between them can often drastically change the performance and the resulting objective that is being optimised. In this work, we rigorously explore the entire landscape of policy distillation, comparing the motivations and strengths of each variant through theoretical and empirical analysis. Our results point to three distillation techniques, that are preferred depending on specifics of the task. Specifically a newly proposed expected entropy regularised distillation allows for quicker learning in a wide range of situations, while still guaranteeing convergence.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical approach for compressing large neural networks by training smaller student models to reproduce useful behavior of larger teacher models. Across vision, language, speech and graph settings, KD variants—matching softened teacher logits, aligning intermediate features, adversarial and contrastive objectives, multi-stage or multi-teacher pipelines, and data- or privacy-aware synthesis—enable large reductions in model size and latency while retaining much of teacher performance. Realizing these gains requires task-aware choices about what to transfer, how to map layers between architectures, how to select or synthesize training data, and how to balance regularization from soft targets with student capacity and robustness considerations.

papers_seen.author: Kennedy
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques transfer information from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost while preserving performance. The literature identifies several methodological families — soft-label/logit matching, intermediate representation or feature mimicking, layer-wise and many-to-many layer alignment, multi-teacher and online protocols, and data-free/synthetic-data strategies — and shows that KD often works best when combined with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when adapted to the task and deployment constraints. Empirical work demonstrates strong gains across vision, language, graph, and multimodal domains, while practical deployment raises challenges in data availability, teacher-student architecture mismatch, robustness, and privacy in federated or distributed settings.

papers_seen.author: Montgomery
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical, Versatile Path to Model Compression and Responsible Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature and flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, and often more deployable models. Beyond raw compression, KD can be adapted to meet constraints of privacy, heterogeneous devices, low-precision hardware, and domain or modality shifts. When combined with complementary techniques such as pre-training, layer-level supervision, or ensemble teachers, distillation can retain much of the teacher’s effectiveness while enabling production usage that would otherwise be impractical. This essay argues that KD should be a primary tool in the model-compression toolbox for both research and engineering deployments, and that best results come from tailoring distillation objectives and pipelines to application needs.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Task-Aware Path to Model Compression in NLP and Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a flexible and practical framework for compressing large models and transferring capabilities to smaller ones. When applied thoughtfully — using layer-aware alignment, attention-guided feature matching, dynamic multi-teacher strategies, and privacy- or deployment-aware protocols — distillation enables substantial speedups, reduced footprint, and cross-modal or cross-device applicability with small drops (or even gains) in task performance. Distillation is not a plug-and-play cure: optimization challenges, teacher-student mismatch, and task-specific redundancy mean methods must be adapted to the target architecture and data regime to realize consistent benefits.

papers_seen.author: Bass
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach to producing small, fast models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. When combined with complementary techniques (e.g., layer mapping, multi-stage curricula, data augmentation, and hardware-aware compression), KD enables deployable NLP and deep-learning systems across constrained environments while admitting clear failure modes that demand targeted remedies.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer predictive behavior and internal structure from larger, often pre-trained teacher models into smaller, efficient student models in order to reduce latency, memory, and deployment cost while retaining task performance. Methods span matching soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, attention- or relation-based feature matching, curriculum strategies for progressively harder supervision, and task- or data-aware architecture search. Practical success depends on student capacity, availability and quality of data, whether the student itself is pre-trained, and choices about what to transfer; open challenges include preserving fairness and robustness, aligning heterogeneous architectures, and operating under privacy or data-limited conditions.
