papers_seen.author: Humphrey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Versatile Path to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) offers a pragmatic route to compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. Across modalities and tasks, KD can transfer predictive behavior, representations, or task-specific inductive biases; when combined with pre-training, architecture search, or careful data handling, it enables compact models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its effectiveness depends on the choice of what is distilled (logits vs. features), how teachers and students are chosen or trained, the availability and quality of data (including synthetic or unlabeled public data), and auxiliary techniques such as projectors, multi-teacher weighting, or meta-learning to adapt the teaching process. I argue that with these design choices attended to, KD is a broadly applicable and cost-effective strategy for model compression in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Cohen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Strategy for Model Compression and Adaptation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach to produce compact models that retain much of the performance of larger models. Beyond simple compression, KD can transfer inductive biases, enable domain adaptation and vocabulary specialization, support privacy-preserving and federated scenarios, work without access to original data, and improve robustness and feature quality when carefully applied. When combined with targeted techniques — feature mimicking, weighted soft labels, projector layers, or adversarial robustness objectives — KD becomes a unifying toolkit to meet latency, capacity, and privacy constraints in real-world NLP and deep learning deployments.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Flexible Path to Compact and Robust NLP and Deep Learning Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical and versatile set of techniques for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster ones while retaining most of their performance. Distillation methods can be adapted to structural compression, domain adaptation, low-data or no-data scenarios, and different model families (transformers, convolutional nets, graph models). A pragmatic compression strategy combines well-chosen distillation objectives with complementary methods (pruning, architecture transformations, multi-teacher supervision, or data-generation) to meet deployment constraints without sacrificing reliability.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models by transferring information from a high-capacity teacher to a smaller student so the student retains much of the teacher’s predictive power while using less compute, memory, or latency. The literature has expanded KD beyond matching teacher soft-labels to include intermediate-feature and layer-wise matching, online/self-distillation, data-free and privacy-aware methods, and combinations with architectural compression (pruning, quantization, and architecture search). Empirical results across vision, NLP, speech, graphs, and ranking show that distilled students often recover a large fraction of teacher performance, but practical success depends on choices like teacher design, student capacity, layer alignment, data availability, and training schedules. Remaining challenges include handling low-frequency or fine-grained behaviors, optimization and capacity mismatch, matching heterogeneous architectures, and distilling under privacy or data-scarce constraints.

papers_seen.author: Huff
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression methods transfer information from larger teacher models to smaller students to reduce computation, memory, and latency while retaining predictive performance. Methods vary from matching soft outputs to aligning intermediate representations, using teacher ensembles or meta-learned teachers, and operating under constraints such as missing data, privacy, or heterogeneous devices. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD improves student generalization relative to training from scratch in many settings but interacts with optimization, data availability, and teacher imperfection; practical deployments benefit from task-aware choices of distillation targets, architectural adapters, and data strategies.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, broadly applicable route to compressing large models into smaller, faster ones for deployment in resource- and privacy-constrained settings. When combined with complementary techniques (e.g., architecture-aware design, data augmentation, and privacy mechanisms), KD consistently yields strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across modalities. However, realizing those gains requires careful choices about what to transfer (logits, features, attention), how to select or synthesize data, and how to mitigate transferred harms (bias, privacy leakage). This paper argues that KD should be treated as a central, flexible tool for model compression while emphasizing practical design principles and known failure modes that practitioners must address.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation transfers information from large teacher models to smaller students to reduce inference cost and memory while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. Modern distillation expands beyond matching teacher logits to include intermediate representation matching, self-supervised and contrastive objectives, data-free and synthetic-data schemes, curriculum and augmentation strategies, and privacy- and deployment-aware protocols. These variants enable application across vision, speech, graph-structured data, and NLP, but practical deployment requires care about data availability, optimization dynamics, robustness, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce compute, memory, and latency while preserving task performance. Across vision, speech, and language tasks, KD has been adapted into many forms—soft-target matching, intermediate representation alignment, attention and relational transfers, multi-teacher ensembles, online distillation, and task-adaptive pipelines—and combined with orthogonal compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to enable deployment in resource-constrained or privacy-sensitive settings. Empirical work shows KD often recovers most of a teacher's utility in a much smaller footprint, but success depends on teacher quality, the choice of distilled signals, data availability and domain shift, and robustness and privacy constraints. The field continues to refine objectives, layer-mapping strategies, and workflows that make distillation effective across modalities and large pretrained models in practical deployments.

papers_seen.author: Peters
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or other forms of learned structure so students retain much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost. KD has evolved from simple soft-target matching to a broad toolkit that includes feature- and representation-level objectives, multi-teacher schemes, data- and privacy-aware variants, and combinations with pruning or quantization. Practical application requires task- and deployment-aware choices that balance accuracy, latency, data availability, and social/robustness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Nguyen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Small-footprint Highway Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning has significantly advanced state-of-the-art of speech recognition in the past few years. However, compared to conventional Gaussian mixture acoustic models, neural network models are usually much larger, and are therefore not very deployable in embedded devices. Previously, we investigated a compact highway deep neural network (HDNN) for acoustic modelling, which is a type of depth-gated feedforward neural network. We have shown that HDNN-based acoustic models can achieve comparable recognition accuracy with much smaller number of model parameters compared to plain deep neural network (DNN) acoustic models. In this paper, we push the boundary further by leveraging on the knowledge distillation technique that is also known as {\it teacher-student} training, i.e., we train the compact HDNN model with the supervision of a high accuracy cumbersome model. Furthermore, we also investigate sequence training and adaptation in the context of teacher-student training. Our experiments were performed on the AMI meeting speech recognition corpus. With this technique, we significantly improved the recognition accuracy of the HDNN acoustic model with less than 0.8 million parameters, and narrowed the gap between this model and the plain DNN with 30 million parameters.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression seek to transfer performance and desirable properties from large, expensive models to smaller, efficient ones. The literature spans techniques that match outputs (soft labels), intermediate representations, or training dynamics; methods that operate with or without access to original data; and approaches that adapt compression to tasks, modalities, or deployment constraints. Empirical results show that discriminative matching of representations, careful layer mappings, adversarial data synthesis, and task-aware architecture search all improve the trade-offs between size, speed, and accuracy in both vision and language settings. Practical developments also emphasize teacher design, robustness transfer, and strategies for low-data or privacy-constrained scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Bush
papers_seen.title: Practical and Principled Knowledge Distillation for NLP: Task-aware, Teacher-aware, and System-level Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical pillar for compressing large deep and language models into deployable, efficient students. When applied thoughtfully—aligning distilled information to the downstream task, designing or adapting teachers with student constraints in mind, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques—KD can recover much of the teacher's capability while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a panacea: optimization difficulties, dataset mismatch, and distributional issues can limit gains unless addressed explicitly. A principled KD pipeline therefore includes task-aware selection of distilled signals, teacher-student co-design, and system-level techniques (pruning/quantization or data-free synthesis) to achieve robust, efficient models for production NLP settings.

papers_seen.author: Roman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Tool for Practical Model Compression in NLP and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-purpose strategy for compressing large deep models while preserving performance. KD can be adapted to constraints common in NLP deployment—limited compute, privacy restrictions, low-latency requirements, and robustness demands—by pairing standard teacher-student training with techniques such as feature-level matching, data augmentation, multi-teacher supervision, and teacher adaptation. Across domains (transformers for NLP, speech embeddings, graph models, generative models), KD consistently enables large reductions in model size or latency with modest accuracy loss, making it a primary method for productionization of deep models.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile method for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. It is applied across modalities and deployment constraints and is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques, careful data and teacher design, and methods that address representation mismatch and optimization. This synthesis summarizes practical techniques, common challenges, and recommended practices for using KD in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: What We Know
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical suite of techniques that transfers information from large teacher models to smaller students to enable efficient deployment. In practice KD spans matching teacher outputs (soft logits), aligning intermediate representations, specialized layer- and channel-level transfers, and workflows that combine distillation with pruning, quantization, or synthetic-data strategies. KD delivers substantial reductions in compute, memory, and latency while often improving student generalization, but its success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity, and how to handle data or domain shifts. Open issues include robustness under distributional heterogeneity, preserving rare-token or fine-grained behavior in sequence models, and distillation without original training data.

papers_seen.author: Ibarra
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Composable Path for Compressing Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, versatile technique for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce latency, memory, and power requirements while retaining much of the teacher's performance. KD works across modalities and tasks, but its practical success depends on choices about what signal to transfer, how to supply or synthesize training data, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression methods. When applied thoughtfully within a wider compression pipeline, KD enables deployable models for resource-constrained and privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Rios
papers_seen.title: Improving Neural Topic Models using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Topic models are often used to identify human-interpretable topics to help make sense of large document collections. We use knowledge distillation to combine the best attributes of probabilistic topic models and pretrained transformers. Our modular method can be straightforwardly applied with any neural topic model to improve topic quality, which we demonstrate using two models having disparate architectures, obtaining state-of-the-art topic coherence. We show that our adaptable framework not only improves performance in the aggregate over all estimated topics, as is commonly reported, but also in head-to-head comparisons of aligned topics.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Solution for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach to compressing large neural models for deployment and domain-specialization. Beyond simple teacher-to-student label matching, modern KD techniques transfer intermediate representations, exploit synthetic or augmented data, operate without original training data, and incorporate privacy or distributed-training constraints. These variants enable retaining much of the teacher performance while reducing inference cost, supporting domain adaptation, improving generalization under limited-data regimes, and meeting privacy or latency requirements for real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Kennedy
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques transfer information from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost while preserving performance. The literature identifies several methodological families — soft-label/logit matching, intermediate representation or feature mimicking, layer-wise and many-to-many layer alignment, multi-teacher and online protocols, and data-free/synthetic-data strategies — and shows that KD often works best when combined with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when adapted to the task and deployment constraints. Empirical work demonstrates strong gains across vision, language, graph, and multimodal domains, while practical deployment raises challenges in data availability, teacher-student architecture mismatch, robustness, and privacy in federated or distributed settings.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central technique for compressing large deep learning models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teachers' performance. Across vision, language, speech, and recommendation tasks, researchers combine KD with architectural compression, pre-training, privacy mechanisms, and data-free approaches to address inference cost, dataset availability, and domain-specific challenges. Empirical work shows that careful choices about what to transfer (logits, features, layers), how to train teachers and students, and how to incorporate task or data constraints strongly determine final student quality.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Revisiting Knowledge Distillation via Label Smoothing Regularization
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to distill the knowledge of a cumbersome teacher model into a lightweight student model. Its success is generally attributed to the privileged information on similarities among categories provided by the teacher model, and in this sense, only strong teacher models are deployed to teach weaker students in practice. In this work, we challenge this common belief by following experimental observations: 1) beyond the acknowledgment that the teacher can improve the student, the student can also enhance the teacher significantly by reversing the KD procedure; 2) a poorly-trained teacher with much lower accuracy than the student can still improve the latter significantly. To explain these observations, we provide a theoretical analysis of the relationships between KD and label smoothing regularization. We prove that 1) KD is a type of learned label smoothing regularization and 2) label smoothing regularization provides a virtual teacher model for KD. From these results, we argue that the success of KD is not fully due to the similarity information between categories from teachers, but also to the regularization of soft targets, which is equally or even more important.   Based on these analyses, we further propose a novel Teacher-free Knowledge Distillation (Tf-KD) framework, where a student model learns from itself or manuallydesigned regularization distribution. The Tf-KD achieves comparable performance with normal KD from a superior teacher, which is well applied when a stronger teacher model is unavailable. Meanwhile, Tf-KD is generic and can be directly deployed for training deep neural networks. Without any extra computation cost, Tf-KD achieves up to 0.65\% improvement on ImageNet over well-established baseline models, which is superior to label smoothing regularization.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques have become central tools for deploying large deep models in resource-constrained settings. Research across computer vision, graph learning, and natural language processing has explored why distillation helps, when it fails, and how to improve it via soft labels, representation alignment, data augmentation, multi-teacher schemes, and teacher training strategies. Work also studies fairness, privacy, and domain-specific adaptations, showing that distillation is a flexible framework but one whose benefits depend strongly on optimization, data, and the design of teacher-student interactions.

papers_seen.author: Walls
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large or ensemble teacher models into smaller student models. Across vision, language, graphs, and multimodal problems, KD is used alone or combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data-centric strategies to produce compact models that preserve much of teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. Empirical and analytical work highlights mechanisms behind KD’s success, practical recipes for improving student fidelity, and persistent challenges (data mismatch, rare-token behavior, robustness, and optimization). This synthesis summarizes methods, applications, practical recommendations, and key open problems reported in recent literature.

papers_seen.author: Galloway
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Context-Sensitive Path to Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly effective toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster students for deployment in resource-constrained settings. KD methods span matching output distributions, aligning internal representations, synthesizing surrogate data when originals are unavailable, and co-designing compact architectures for target tasks. While KD often preserves much of a teacher’s performance and enables trade-offs among accuracy, latency, and memory, success depends on the distillation signal, data regime, robustness and privacy needs, and architecture alignment between teacher and student.

papers_seen.author: Maldonado
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge by Mimicking Features
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a popular method to train efficient networks ("student") with the help of high-capacity networks ("teacher"). Traditional methods use the teacher's soft logits as extra supervision to train the student network. In this paper, we argue that it is more advantageous to make the student mimic the teacher's features in the penultimate layer. Not only the student can directly learn more effective information from the teacher feature, feature mimicking can also be applied for teachers trained without a softmax layer. Experiments show that it can achieve higher accuracy than traditional KD. To further facilitate feature mimicking, we decompose a feature vector into the magnitude and the direction. We argue that the teacher should give more freedom to the student feature's magnitude, and let the student pay more attention on mimicking the feature direction. To meet this requirement, we propose a loss term based on locality-sensitive hashing (LSH). With the help of this new loss, our method indeed mimics feature directions more accurately, relaxes constraints on feature magnitudes, and achieves state-of-the-art distillation accuracy. We provide theoretical analyses of how LSH facilitates feature direction mimicking, and further extend feature mimicking to multi-label recognition and object detection.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Effective Knowledge Distillation: Representation, Selection, and Practical Constraints
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach to compress and adapt large deep models for deployment in resource- or privacy-constrained settings. Effective distillation goes beyond matching teacher logits: transferring internal representations, choosing which teacher signals to trust, and accommodating deployment constraints (limited data, communication, low-precision hardware) are all decisive. I argue that the most reliable distillation pipelines combine representation-level objectives, selective/sample-aware strategies, and engineering choices that address privacy and efficiency, yielding compact students that retain teacher strengths across NLP, vision, and graph domains.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: A Closer Look at Deep Learning Heuristics: Learning rate restarts, Warmup and Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The convergence rate and final performance of common deep learning models have significantly benefited from heuristics such as learning rate schedules, knowledge distillation, skip connections, and normalization layers. In the absence of theoretical underpinnings, controlled experiments aimed at explaining these strategies can aid our understanding of deep learning landscapes and the training dynamics. Existing approaches for empirical analysis rely on tools of linear interpolation and visualizations with dimensionality reduction, each with their limitations. Instead, we revisit such analysis of heuristics through the lens of recently proposed methods for loss surface and representation analysis, viz., mode connectivity and canonical correlation analysis (CCA), and hypothesize reasons for the success of the heuristics. In particular, we explore knowledge distillation and learning rate heuristics of (cosine) restarts and warmup using mode connectivity and CCA. Our empirical analysis suggests that: (a) the reasons often quoted for the success of cosine annealing are not evidenced in practice; (b) that the effect of learning rate warmup is to prevent the deeper layers from creating training instability; and (c) that the latent knowledge shared by the teacher is primarily disbursed to the deeper layers.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Rejuvenating Low-Frequency Words: Making the Most of Parallel Data in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is commonly used to construct synthetic data for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models. However, there exists a discrepancy on low-frequency words between the distilled and the original data, leading to more errors on predicting low-frequency words. To alleviate the problem, we directly expose the raw data into NAT by leveraging pretraining. By analyzing directed alignments, we found that KD makes low-frequency source words aligned with targets more deterministically but fails to align sufficient low-frequency words from target to source. Accordingly, we propose reverse KD to rejuvenate more alignments for low-frequency target words. To make the most of authentic and synthetic data, we combine these complementary approaches as a new training strategy for further boosting NAT performance. We conduct experiments on five translation benchmarks over two advanced architectures. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach can significantly and universally improve translation quality by reducing translation errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach achieves 28.2 and 33.9 BLEU points on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets, respectively. Our code, data, and trained models are available at \url{https://github.com/alphadl/RLFW-NAT}.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Variants, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses or transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller students by providing richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. Across vision, speech, graph, and language tasks, KD appears to work through a mix of mechanisms — soft targets acting as regularizers, matching intermediate representations, and reducing effective data complexity — and can be combined with data augmentation, privacy-preserving noise, and architecture-aware projectors. Practical research highlights trade-offs related to teacher quality, which samples to transfer, robustness, and device heterogeneity; current methods address these by selective sample transfer, contrastive or feature-level alignment, adversarial objectives, and pre-training compact students before distillation. Key open directions include principled selection of distilled samples, theoretical characterization of when distilled soft targets help versus hurt, and integrating KD with pruning and other compression approaches for deployment on constrained devices.

papers_seen.author: Mckay
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques have become central to deploying high-performance deep models in resource-constrained settings. Research has produced diverse approaches that transfer information from larger "teacher" models to smaller "student" models via softened outputs, intermediate feature supervision, layer-wise alignment, module replacement, data augmentation, and data-free synthesis. These methods have been applied across modalities (vision, speech, language, multi-modal), combined with quantization and architecture search, and adapted for settings with limited or private data. Empirical and theoretical work highlights why distillation can improve generalization, how inductive biases or teacher strength influence transfer, and practical strategies to make students more robust and efficient. Challenges remain in aligning heterogeneous architectures, preserving task-relevant representations, and designing principled distillation objectives for varied downstream tasks.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: Model Compression with Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation for Web Question Answering System
papers_seen.abstract: Deep pre-training and fine-tuning models (such as BERT and OpenAI GPT) have demonstrated excellent results in question answering areas. However, due to the sheer amount of model parameters, the inference speed of these models is very slow. How to apply these complex models to real business scenarios becomes a challenging but practical problem. Previous model compression methods usually suffer from information loss during the model compression procedure, leading to inferior models compared with the original one. To tackle this challenge, we propose a Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (TMKD for short) method for web Question Answering system. We first develop a general Q\&A distillation task for student model pre-training, and further fine-tune this pre-trained student model with multi-teacher knowledge distillation on downstream tasks (like Web Q\&A task, MNLI, SNLI, RTE tasks from GLUE), which effectively reduces the overfitting bias in individual teacher models, and transfers more general knowledge to the student model. The experiment results show that our method can significantly outperform the baseline methods and even achieve comparable results with the original teacher models, along with substantial speedup of model inference.

papers_seen.author: Dudley
papers_seen.title: Attention-Guided Answer Distillation for Machine Reading Comprehension
papers_seen.abstract: Despite that current reading comprehension systems have achieved significant advancements, their promising performances are often obtained at the cost of making an ensemble of numerous models. Besides, existing approaches are also vulnerable to adversarial attacks. This paper tackles these problems by leveraging knowledge distillation, which aims to transfer knowledge from an ensemble model to a single model. We first demonstrate that vanilla knowledge distillation applied to answer span prediction is effective for reading comprehension systems. We then propose two novel approaches that not only penalize the prediction on confusing answers but also guide the training with alignment information distilled from the ensemble. Experiments show that our best student model has only a slight drop of 0.4% F1 on the SQuAD test set compared to the ensemble teacher, while running 12x faster during inference. It even outperforms the teacher on adversarial SQuAD datasets and NarrativeQA benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Variants, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses or transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller students by providing richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. Across vision, speech, graph, and language tasks, KD appears to work through a mix of mechanisms — soft targets acting as regularizers, matching intermediate representations, and reducing effective data complexity — and can be combined with data augmentation, privacy-preserving noise, and architecture-aware projectors. Practical research highlights trade-offs related to teacher quality, which samples to transfer, robustness, and device heterogeneity; current methods address these by selective sample transfer, contrastive or feature-level alignment, adversarial objectives, and pre-training compact students before distillation. Key open directions include principled selection of distilled samples, theoretical characterization of when distilled soft targets help versus hurt, and integrating KD with pruning and other compression approaches for deployment on constrained devices.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Is Label Smoothing Truly Incompatible with Knowledge Distillation: An Empirical Study
papers_seen.abstract: This work aims to empirically clarify a recently discovered perspective that label smoothing is incompatible with knowledge distillation. We begin by introducing the motivation behind on how this incompatibility is raised, i.e., label smoothing erases relative information between teacher logits. We provide a novel connection on how label smoothing affects distributions of semantically similar and dissimilar classes. Then we propose a metric to quantitatively measure the degree of erased information in sample's representation. After that, we study its one-sidedness and imperfection of the incompatibility view through massive analyses, visualizations and comprehensive experiments on Image Classification, Binary Networks, and Neural Machine Translation. Finally, we broadly discuss several circumstances wherein label smoothing will indeed lose its effectiveness. Project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/LS_and_KD/index.html.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques transfer predictive behavior and internal structure from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce computation, memory, and latency while preserving performance. The literature documents a spectrum of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or channel maps, and relational signals), a variety of optimization and architectural practices (layer mapping, projectors, multi-stage training, and student-friendly teacher design), and deployment workflows for constrained settings (data-free, federated, and domain-adaptive distillation). Empirical and theoretical work highlights multiple mechanisms that make KD effective (regularization via soft targets, representation alignment, and optimization/inductive-bias transfer), while also identifying persistent challenges such as aligning heterogeneous architectures, preserving low-frequency behavior, and selecting what and when to transfer. Practical recommendations center on matching distillation signals to student capacity, using feature- or layer-aware objectives when internal alignment matters, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques for robust deployment.

papers_seen.author: Harrell
papers_seen.title: No One Left Behind: Inclusive Federated Learning over Heterogeneous Devices
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning (FL) is an important paradigm for training global models from decentralized data in a privacy-preserving way. Existing FL methods usually assume the global model can be trained on any participating client. However, in real applications, the devices of clients are usually heterogeneous, and have different computing power. Although big models like BERT have achieved huge success in AI, it is difficult to apply them to heterogeneous FL with weak clients. The straightforward solutions like removing the weak clients or using a small model to fit all clients will lead to some problems, such as under-representation of dropped clients and inferior accuracy due to data loss or limited model representation ability. In this work, we propose InclusiveFL, a client-inclusive federated learning method to handle this problem. The core idea of InclusiveFL is to assign models of different sizes to clients with different computing capabilities, bigger models for powerful clients and smaller ones for weak clients. We also propose an effective method to share the knowledge among multiple local models with different sizes. In this way, all the clients can participate in the model learning in FL, and the final model can be big and powerful enough. Besides, we propose a momentum knowledge distillation method to better transfer knowledge in big models on powerful clients to the small models on weak clients. Extensive experiments on many real-world benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in learning accurate models from clients with heterogeneous devices under the FL framework.

papers_seen.author: Koch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques aim to transfer useful knowledge from larger, expensive models to smaller, more efficient ones so that deployed systems retain high performance under resource constraints. Approaches span logit-level supervision, feature- and layer-level matching, progressive module replacement, and data-augmentation or data-free strategies. Applications include compressing large language models, accelerating inference on edge devices, enabling multi-task and federated learning, and improving robustness or generalization. Practical deployments often combine KD with quantization, architecture design, or task-aware selection of teacher signals to balance fidelity and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Linkless Link Prediction via Relational Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have shown exceptional performance in the task of link prediction. Despite their effectiveness, the high latency brought by non-trivial neighborhood data dependency limits GNNs in practical deployments. Conversely, the known efficient MLPs are much less effective than GNNs due to the lack of relational knowledge. In this work, to combine the advantages of GNNs and MLPs, we start with exploring direct knowledge distillation (KD) methods for link prediction, i.e., predicted logit-based matching and node representation-based matching. Upon observing direct KD analogs do not perform well for link prediction, we propose a relational KD framework, Linkless Link Prediction (LLP), to distill knowledge for link prediction with MLPs. Unlike simple KD methods that match independent link logits or node representations, LLP distills relational knowledge that is centered around each (anchor) node to the student MLP. Specifically, we propose rank-based matching and distribution-based matching strategies that complement each other. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LLP boosts the link prediction performance of MLPs with significant margins, and even outperforms the teacher GNNs on 7 out of 8 benchmarks. LLP also achieves a 70.68x speedup in link prediction inference compared to GNNs on the large-scale OGB dataset.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Path to Efficient Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation provides a pragmatic and versatile set of techniques to compress large neural models into compact, faster students while retaining much of their performance. Across NLP and vision, modern distillation variants — including multi-teacher pipelines, self-distillation, teacher optimization, and task-aware layer alignment — address core challenges such as capacity gaps and task-specific redundancy. When combined with complementary compression strategies (pruning, low-precision arithmetic, architecture search), distillation enables deployment of high-performing models under tight resource or latency constraints.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high‑capacity models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or structural inductive biases from teachers. A spectrum of methods—logit/soft‑label matching, feature- and layer-wise imitation, attention and relation transfer, ensemble-to-singleton distillation, self-distillation, and data‑free synthesis—has been developed to meet deployment goals such as latency reduction, privacy, domain adaptation, and robustness. Empirical and applied work in NLP, vision, speech, and graph domains shows that carefully chosen distilled signals, teacher designs, and training protocols allow compact models to approach teacher performance, though challenges remain around domain shift, low-frequency phenomena, and preserving fairness and privacy in compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques transfer information from large teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost and enable deployment in resource-constrained settings. A diverse set of KD variants—matching soft logits, aligning intermediate representations, synthesizing or reusing data, or adapting student architectures—has been developed. These methods are applied across modalities and combine effectively with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to achieve favorable size/accuracy trade-offs. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to generate or select training data, and how to align teacher and student architectures; open challenges include robust transfer under domain shift, privacy constraints, and heterogeneous deployment environments.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Backbone for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical framework for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, and multimodal tasks. When combined with careful pre-training, selective sample use, multi-teacher strategies, or data-free and privacy-aware protocols, KD preserves much of the teacher's utility while enabling efficiency and wider deployment. Success depends on matching distillation technique to the task and data regime, and on addressing issues such as corrupted information from smoothing, misaligned layer mappings, and synthetic-data drift.

papers_seen.author: Gibson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression methods transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from larger or more informed teacher models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained students. These methods are applied to reduce latency and memory, enable deployment on heterogeneous or private devices, and to retain teacher performance through tailored losses, intermediate-feature matching, multi-stage pipelines, and combinations with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Empirical work shows KD succeeds across modalities (language, vision, multimodal, and generative models) when design choices — what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and which data to use — are matched to the task and constraints. Ongoing challenges include distilling rare-token behaviors, handling severe data heterogeneity, ensuring privacy and fairness, and automating student architecture design.

papers_seen.author: Callahan
papers_seen.title: A Practical Position on Knowledge Distillation: Go Beyond Soft Labels
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a necessary tool for compressing large deep and NLP models into efficient students suitable for deployment. However, naive KD that only matches teacher soft-labels is often insufficient. Effective distillation combines richer knowledge targets (internal features, attention, and layerwise signals), data-aware augmentations, selective sample strategies, and privacy- or domain-aware procedures. The best practical pipelines treat KD as a toolbox: choose which knowledge to transfer based on student capacity and task needs, use augmentation or self-distillation to improve generalization when data are scarce, and apply selective or privacy-preserving queries where constraints require it.

papers_seen.author: Duncan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practically essential approach for compressing large neural models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. By transferring learned behavior from teachers to students, KD enables many deployment trade-offs while remaining compatible with complementary techniques (e.g., quantization, pruning, architecture search). However, to be robust and broadly useful in real systems, distillation must go beyond naive soft-label matching: effective pipelines combine logits with internal representation transfer, task- and layer-aware selection of signals, appropriate data strategies, and attention to distributional heterogeneity and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Rice
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Methods, Theory, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. Across modalities and deployment settings KD techniques leverage soft targets, intermediate-feature matching, attention, generative synthesis, and architecture search to balance accuracy, size, privacy, and communication cost. Practical systems extend KD to settings with no original data, heterogeneous or private devices, multi-teacher ensembles, and task-adaptive compression. Key challenges remain in distribution shift of synthetic data, aligning teacher and student inputs/representations, preserving privacy under queries, and choosing effective distillation signals for downstream tasks.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation: Versatile Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and powerful approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, more efficient ones. Beyond simple size reduction, KD enables transfer of capabilities across modalities, supports domain adaptation, improves deployment in resource-constrained or privacy-sensitive settings, and can be adapted to distributed training. However, benefits are not automatic: careful design of teacher-student alignment, training data, and distillation objectives is required to preserve task performance and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical, flexible approach for producing compact neural models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. Across vision and language applications KD has been extended from simple soft-label matching to a wide set of techniques—intermediate-representation transfer, layer-aware alignment, multi-teacher and self-distillation, data-free variants, and adversarial or projector-based feature matching—that enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD both preserves predictive performance and can improve generalization in many settings, while also raising practical challenges such as teacher–student mismatch and degraded modeling of low-frequency phenomena that require targeted mitigations.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Design-Sensitive Path to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly useful family of techniques for transferring behavior from large teacher models to smaller students to reduce inference cost and enable deployment. KD has been instantiated as matching soft targets, aligning intermediate representations, progressive module replacement, and selective or multi-teacher schemes. While KD often yields strong empirical gains and enables domain- and task-specific compression, its success depends on optimization dynamics, the choice of distilled signal, data quality and selection, and teacher–student alignment. Careful method choices make KD a reliable, production-ready compression strategy, but it is not a universal shortcut: practitioners must tailor KD objectives and protocols to their constraints and goals.

papers_seen.author: Harvey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical, and Composable Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students that remain useful for deployment in resource-constrained or data-limited settings. KD works across modalities and deployment scenarios when combined with complementary compression techniques and careful design choices. To realize its benefits practitioners should treat KD as a component of a compression pipeline: design student-friendly teachers, choose what to transfer (logits, features, layers) based on task needs, address data constraints with augmentation or data-free methods, and pair distillation with pruning, quantization, or architecture search to meet latency and memory goals.

papers_seen.author: Harrell
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques have become central tools to deploy high-capacity deep models in latency-, memory-, privacy-, and compute-constrained settings. Across vision, language, graph, and multimodal domains, practitioners use teacher-student training, feature-level transfer, data-free distillation, and hybrid pipelines that combine pruning or architecture search with distillation. Work in this area balances fidelity to teacher models, robustness, and efficiency, and explores trade-offs such as reliance on original training data, communication overhead in federated settings, and the benefits of designing students or student-friendly teachers. The literature shows repeated success of KD when tailored to the task and constraints, while also revealing limitations under severe data heterogeneity or adversarial settings.

papers_seen.author: Nguyen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical and Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students. Across vision, speech, graph, and language tasks, KD enables substantial reductions in memory and inference cost while retaining much of the teacher's performance. However, KD is not a silver bullet: its effectiveness depends on choices of teacher/student architecture, what is distilled (logits, layers, attention, representations), the optimization and data used for distillation, and constraints such as privacy or fairness. Carefully combining KD with techniques like multi-teacher schedules, layer-mapping strategies, task-adaptive compression, and privacy-preserving perturbations yields the best trade-offs for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Valdez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Pragmatic Tool for Compressing Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is not merely one technique among many for model compression: when applied thoughtfully it is a central, practical lever for producing small, fast models that retain much of the performance, robustness, and task-specific behavior of large teachers. Best practice couples KD with representation-level supervision, teacher-student co-design, data and privacy strategies, and complementary compression methods so that compact models meet real-world latency, memory and heterogeneity constraints.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and/or internal structure. Across vision and NLP, practitioners use KD to reduce latency and memory, adapt models to new domains, enable privacy- or data-constrained deployments, and condense ensembles into single deployable models. Effective distillation blends choices about what to transfer (soft targets, features, layers), how to pretrain or adapt compact architectures, and how to handle limited or sensitive data. While KD often preserves much of a teacher’s performance, achieving robust, fair, and domain-appropriate students requires careful design of teachers, student architectures, and distillation signals.

papers_seen.author: Mason
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression strategies have become core methods for deploying large deep models in resource-constrained settings. Across vision, speech, and language tasks, practitioners compress models by transferring teacher behavior to smaller students, by architectural replacement, or by searching for task-specific compact architectures. Techniques differ in what is transferred (logits, intermediate representations, inter-class relations), how training data are used (original data, distilled targets, or synthetic data), and how robustness and task-specificity are preserved. Empirical work shows strong trade-offs between model size, runtime, and task performance; recent advances focus on task-adaptive compression, improved layer-mapping, data-free approaches, and preserving robustness under adversarial or distributional shifts. Important open challenges remain in handling domain shift, low-frequency phenomena, heterogeneous teacher ensembles, and reliable data-free distillation.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: Towards Practical Lipreading with Distilled and Efficient Models
papers_seen.abstract: Lipreading has witnessed a lot of progress due to the resurgence of neural networks. Recent works have placed emphasis on aspects such as improving performance by finding the optimal architecture or improving generalization. However, there is still a significant gap between the current methodologies and the requirements for an effective deployment of lipreading in practical scenarios. In this work, we propose a series of innovations that significantly bridge that gap: first, we raise the state-of-the-art performance by a wide margin on LRW and LRW-1000 to 88.5% and 46.6%, respectively using self-distillation. Secondly, we propose a series of architectural changes, including a novel Depthwise Separable Temporal Convolutional Network (DS-TCN) head, that slashes the computational cost to a fraction of the (already quite efficient) original model. Thirdly, we show that knowledge distillation is a very effective tool for recovering performance of the lightweight models. This results in a range of models with different accuracy-efficiency trade-offs. However, our most promising lightweight models are on par with the current state-of-the-art while showing a reduction of 8.2x and 3.9x in terms of computational cost and number of parameters, respectively, which we hope will enable the deployment of lipreading models in practical applications.

papers_seen.author: Rocha
papers_seen.title: Few Shot Network Compression via Cross Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Model compression has been widely adopted to obtain light-weighted deep neural networks. Most prevalent methods, however, require fine-tuning with sufficient training data to ensure accuracy, which could be challenged by privacy and security issues. As a compromise between privacy and performance, in this paper we investigate few shot network compression: given few samples per class, how can we effectively compress the network with negligible performance drop? The core challenge of few shot network compression lies in high estimation errors from the original network during inference, since the compressed network can easily over-fits on the few training instances. The estimation errors could propagate and accumulate layer-wisely and finally deteriorate the network output. To address the problem, we propose cross distillation, a novel layer-wise knowledge distillation approach. By interweaving hidden layers of teacher and student network, layer-wisely accumulated estimation errors can be effectively reduced.The proposed method offers a general framework compatible with prevalent network compression techniques such as pruning. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that cross distillation can significantly improve the student network's accuracy when only a few training instances are available.

papers_seen.author: Whitehead
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce computation, memory, and latency while retaining much of the original performance. KD encompasses a family of techniques — matching soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, using multi-stage or curriculum schemes, and combining distillation with other compression methods — and is widely used for deploying models in resource-constrained or privacy-sensitive settings. Success depends on matching distillation objectives and data strategies to deployment goals and student capacity.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Private Model Compression via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The soaring demand for intelligent mobile applications calls for deploying powerful deep neural networks (DNNs) on mobile devices. However, the outstanding performance of DNNs notoriously relies on increasingly complex models, which in turn is associated with an increase in computational expense far surpassing mobile devices' capacity. What is worse, app service providers need to collect and utilize a large volume of users' data, which contain sensitive information, to build the sophisticated DNN models. Directly deploying these models on public mobile devices presents prohibitive privacy risk. To benefit from the on-device deep learning without the capacity and privacy concerns, we design a private model compression framework RONA. Following the knowledge distillation paradigm, we jointly use hint learning, distillation learning, and self learning to train a compact and fast neural network. The knowledge distilled from the cumbersome model is adaptively bounded and carefully perturbed to enforce differential privacy. We further propose an elegant query sample selection method to reduce the number of queries and control the privacy loss. A series of empirical evaluations as well as the implementation on an Android mobile device show that RONA can not only compress cumbersome models efficiently but also provide a strong privacy guarantee. For example, on SVHN, when a meaningful $(9.83,10^{-6})$-differential privacy is guaranteed, the compact model trained by RONA can obtain 20$\times$ compression ratio and 19$\times$ speed-up with merely 0.97% accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Kim
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When paired with representation-aware objectives, careful pre-training of compact models, and safeguards for robustness and privacy, KD enables production-ready reductions in latency, memory, and energy while retaining much of a teacher's performance. I argue that KD should be treated as a central tool in model-compression pipelines, not as a single recipe but as a family of methods to be combined with task-aware design choices for reliable deployment.
