papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Compressing GANs using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been used in several machine learning tasks such as domain transfer, super resolution, and synthetic data generation. State-of-the-art GANs often use tens of millions of parameters, making them expensive to deploy for applications in low SWAP (size, weight, and power) hardware, such as mobile devices, and for applications with real time capabilities. There has been no work found to reduce the number of parameters used in GANs. Therefore, we propose a method to compress GANs using knowledge distillation techniques, in which a smaller "student" GAN learns to mimic a larger "teacher" GAN. We show that the distillation methods used on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and Celeb-A datasets can compress teacher GANs at ratios of 1669:1, 58:1, and 87:1, respectively, while retaining the quality of the generated image. From our experiments, we observe a qualitative limit for GAN's compression. Moreover, we observe that, with a fixed parameter budget, compressed GANs outperform GANs trained using standard training methods. We conjecture that this is partially owing to the optimization landscape of over-parameterized GANs which allows efficient training using alternating gradient descent. Thus, training an over-parameterized GAN followed by our proposed compression scheme provides a high quality generative model with a small number of parameters.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers behavior from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce latency, memory, and computation while retaining much of the teacher's performance. Across vision, language, and graph domains, KD has been applied as logit matching, intermediate-feature alignment, adversarial transfer, and data- or task-aware synthesis. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD often acts both as a source of extra task signal and as a regularizer; practical systems combine KD with pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, and data strategies to meet deployment constraints. Important open issues include data heterogeneity, teacher–student capacity mismatch, privacy-preserving releases, and closing remaining gaps in robustness and domain generalization.

papers_seen.author: Huff
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression methods transfer information from larger teacher models to smaller students to reduce computation, memory, and latency while retaining predictive performance. Methods vary from matching soft outputs to aligning intermediate representations, using teacher ensembles or meta-learned teachers, and operating under constraints such as missing data, privacy, or heterogeneous devices. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD improves student generalization relative to training from scratch in many settings but interacts with optimization, data availability, and teacher imperfection; practical deployments benefit from task-aware choices of distillation targets, architectural adapters, and data strategies.

papers_seen.author: Ibarra
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Composable Path for Compressing Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, versatile technique for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce latency, memory, and power requirements while retaining much of the teacher's performance. KD works across modalities and tasks, but its practical success depends on choices about what signal to transfer, how to supply or synthesize training data, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression methods. When applied thoughtfully within a wider compression pipeline, KD enables deployable models for resource-constrained and privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Warner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression and Adaptation in NLP and Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as a central, practical technique for compressing and adapting large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD is versatile: it transfers predictive behavior, intermediate representations, and ensemble knowledge; supports data-free or privacy-sensitive settings; and can improve robustness and calibration when combined with complementary methods. Realizing KD’s full potential requires matching the distillation recipe to deployment goals and addressing failure modes such as optimization mismatches, bias transfer, and poor handling of low-frequency phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Riley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is not merely a model-compression trick but a central, practical paradigm for deploying high-performance deep and NLP models under real-world constraints. KD can compress large pre-trained models into lightweight students, transfer inductive biases, improve robustness and generalization, enable low-precision and privacy-aware deployments, and adapt to data- or compute-limited settings. Effective distillation couples soft-label transfer with representation-level alignment, task-aware architecture choices, and complementary techniques (quantization, pruning, augmentation). However, KD must be applied carefully: teacher–student mismatches, bias transfer, domain shift, and limited-data regimes require method choices such as feature mimicking, teacher ensembles, teacher-free objectives, or fairness-aware augmentations. The result is a flexible toolkit that—when combined with architectural and data strategies—makes high-quality, efficient models feasible for production NLP and deep-learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Graph-less Neural Networks: Teaching Old MLPs New Tricks via Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are popular for graph machine learning and have shown great results on wide node classification tasks. Yet, they are less popular for practical deployments in the industry owing to their scalability challenges incurred by data dependency. Namely, GNN inference depends on neighbor nodes multiple hops away from the target, and fetching them burdens latency-constrained applications. Existing inference acceleration methods like pruning and quantization can speed up GNNs by reducing Multiplication-and-ACcumulation (MAC) operations, but the improvements are limited given the data dependency is not resolved. Conversely, multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) have no graph dependency and infer much faster than GNNs, even though they are less accurate than GNNs for node classification in general. Motivated by these complementary strengths and weaknesses, we bring GNNs and MLPs together via knowledge distillation (KD). Our work shows that the performance of MLPs can be improved by large margins with GNN KD. We call the distilled MLPs Graph-less Neural Networks (GLNNs) as they have no inference graph dependency. We show that GLNNs with competitive accuracy infer faster than GNNs by 146X-273X and faster than other acceleration methods by 14X-27X. Under a production setting involving both transductive and inductive predictions across 7 datasets, GLNN accuracies improve over stand-alone MLPs by 12.36% on average and match GNNs on 6/7 datasets. Comprehensive analysis shows when and why GLNNs can achieve competitive accuracies to GNNs and suggests GLNN as a handy choice for latency-constrained applications.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Does Knowledge Distillation Really Work?
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular technique for training a small student network to emulate a larger teacher model, such as an ensemble of networks. We show that while knowledge distillation can improve student generalization, it does not typically work as it is commonly understood: there often remains a surprisingly large discrepancy between the predictive distributions of the teacher and the student, even in cases when the student has the capacity to perfectly match the teacher. We identify difficulties in optimization as a key reason for why the student is unable to match the teacher. We also show how the details of the dataset used for distillation play a role in how closely the student matches the teacher -- and that more closely matching the teacher paradoxically does not always lead to better student generalization.

papers_seen.author: Gibson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression methods transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from larger or more informed teacher models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained students. These methods are applied to reduce latency and memory, enable deployment on heterogeneous or private devices, and to retain teacher performance through tailored losses, intermediate-feature matching, multi-stage pipelines, and combinations with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Empirical work shows KD succeeds across modalities (language, vision, multimodal, and generative models) when design choices — what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and which data to use — are matched to the task and constraints. Ongoing challenges include distilling rare-token behaviors, handling severe data heterogeneity, ensuring privacy and fairness, and automating student architecture design.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Private Model Compression via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The soaring demand for intelligent mobile applications calls for deploying powerful deep neural networks (DNNs) on mobile devices. However, the outstanding performance of DNNs notoriously relies on increasingly complex models, which in turn is associated with an increase in computational expense far surpassing mobile devices' capacity. What is worse, app service providers need to collect and utilize a large volume of users' data, which contain sensitive information, to build the sophisticated DNN models. Directly deploying these models on public mobile devices presents prohibitive privacy risk. To benefit from the on-device deep learning without the capacity and privacy concerns, we design a private model compression framework RONA. Following the knowledge distillation paradigm, we jointly use hint learning, distillation learning, and self learning to train a compact and fast neural network. The knowledge distilled from the cumbersome model is adaptively bounded and carefully perturbed to enforce differential privacy. We further propose an elegant query sample selection method to reduce the number of queries and control the privacy loss. A series of empirical evaluations as well as the implementation on an Android mobile device show that RONA can not only compress cumbersome models efficiently but also provide a strong privacy guarantee. For example, on SVHN, when a meaningful $(9.83,10^{-6})$-differential privacy is guaranteed, the compact model trained by RONA can obtain 20$\times$ compression ratio and 19$\times$ speed-up with merely 0.97% accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical and Versatile Tool for Compression in NLP: Promise, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, faster students that retain much of the teacher's performance. In natural language processing, KD can operate at multiple granularities — from logits to intermediate representations or entire modules — and can be combined with pre-training, pruning, and low-precision inference to meet real-world deployment constraints. However, distillation is not a turnkey solution: optimization difficulties, mismatches in internal representations, and task-specific redundancies can limit benefits unless methods are adapted to the model size, pre-training regimen, and downstream objectives. When applied thoughtfully (e.g., pre-training compact students, selectively transferring internal features, and using task-aware layer-wise matching), KD yields efficient models that generalize well across tasks and settings.

papers_seen.author: House
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Principled, Practical, and Context-Sensitive Toolbox for NLP Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an essential approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable systems. When treated as a flexible framework rather than a single recipe, KD can preserve much of teacher performance while meeting constraints of latency, memory, privacy, and domain heterogeneity. However, its success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to adapt to new domains or architectures, and how to select or synthesize training signals for the student.

papers_seen.author: Osborne
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge from Deep Networks with Applications to Healthcare Domain
papers_seen.abstract: Exponential growth in Electronic Healthcare Records (EHR) has resulted in new opportunities and urgent needs for discovery of meaningful data-driven representations and patterns of diseases in Computational Phenotyping research. Deep Learning models have shown superior performance for robust prediction in computational phenotyping tasks, but suffer from the issue of model interpretability which is crucial for clinicians involved in decision-making. In this paper, we introduce a novel knowledge-distillation approach called Interpretable Mimic Learning, to learn interpretable phenotype features for making robust prediction while mimicking the performance of deep learning models. Our framework uses Gradient Boosting Trees to learn interpretable features from deep learning models such as Stacked Denoising Autoencoder and Long Short-Term Memory. Exhaustive experiments on a real-world clinical time-series dataset show that our method obtains similar or better performance than the deep learning models, and it provides interpretable phenotypes for clinical decision making.

papers_seen.author: Mueller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central, pragmatic approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD delivers strong empirical gains across domains by transferring soft outputs, intermediate representations, or task-specific behaviors from teachers to students. Its strengths are practical: it supports deployment on constrained hardware, enables multi-teacher and cross-model transfer, and integrates with other compression tools. At the same time, KD is not a plug-and-play solution: theoretical and empirical work shows limits under data heterogeneity, imperfect teachers, and mismatched architectures, so KD must be applied with task-aware choices (signal type, layer alignment, teacher selection, and curricula) and often combined with complementary methods to realize reliable, high-fidelity compression.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Beyond Soft Labels: A Practical Position on Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a crucial technique for shrinking large deep models to meet real-world latency, memory and privacy constraints while retaining much of their performance. However, naive distillation that only matches teacher soft-labels is often insufficient. A more reliable strategy combines distillation of internal representations and features, task- or domain-adaptive compression, and architecture-aware search or adaptation. When applied with care — addressing optimization issues, data or privacy limits, and mismatch between teacher and student capacities — distillation enables compact, fast models that approach teacher performance across speech, NLP and vision tasks.

papers_seen.author: Maldonado
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge by Mimicking Features
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a popular method to train efficient networks ("student") with the help of high-capacity networks ("teacher"). Traditional methods use the teacher's soft logits as extra supervision to train the student network. In this paper, we argue that it is more advantageous to make the student mimic the teacher's features in the penultimate layer. Not only the student can directly learn more effective information from the teacher feature, feature mimicking can also be applied for teachers trained without a softmax layer. Experiments show that it can achieve higher accuracy than traditional KD. To further facilitate feature mimicking, we decompose a feature vector into the magnitude and the direction. We argue that the teacher should give more freedom to the student feature's magnitude, and let the student pay more attention on mimicking the feature direction. To meet this requirement, we propose a loss term based on locality-sensitive hashing (LSH). With the help of this new loss, our method indeed mimics feature directions more accurately, relaxes constraints on feature magnitudes, and achieves state-of-the-art distillation accuracy. We provide theoretical analyses of how LSH facilitates feature direction mimicking, and further extend feature mimicking to multi-label recognition and object detection.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Central Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable method for compressing large models into smaller, deployable ones across NLP and other deep learning domains. KD preserves much of teacher performance while enabling faster inference, smaller footprints, and flexible deployment; however, it has failure modes related to data dependence, teacher quality, and rare-token fidelity. Effective use of KD therefore treats it as a toolbox—combining multi-teacher schedules, data-aware augmentation, representation-level objectives, and privacy-aware protocols—to produce robust, task-appropriate compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Wide Neural Networks: Risk Bound, Data Efficiency and Imperfect Teacher
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a strategy of training a student network with guide of the soft output from a teacher network. It has been a successful method of model compression and knowledge transfer. However, currently knowledge distillation lacks a convincing theoretical understanding. On the other hand, recent finding on neural tangent kernel enables us to approximate a wide neural network with a linear model of the network's random features. In this paper, we theoretically analyze the knowledge distillation of a wide neural network. First we provide a transfer risk bound for the linearized model of the network. Then we propose a metric of the task's training difficulty, called data inefficiency. Based on this metric, we show that for a perfect teacher, a high ratio of teacher's soft labels can be beneficial. Finally, for the case of imperfect teacher, we find that hard labels can correct teacher's wrong prediction, which explains the practice of mixing hard and soft labels.

papers_seen.author: Alvarado
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques compress large neural networks into smaller, faster models for practical deployment. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD succeeds through multiple mechanisms — not solely by copying a stronger teacher — enabling many practical variants (logit-based soft targets, feature- and layer-level matching, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-free and privacy-preserving protocols). Effective application depends on choosing what and how to transfer, handling data or device constraints, and combining distillation with other compression tools. Key limitations include optimization dynamics, distribution shift for synthetic data, and heterogeneity in federated or privacy-sensitive settings; current research points toward deeper study of representation transfer, optimization effects, and task-aware distillation pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Owens
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses capability from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. It encompasses methods that transfer final outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure, or training curricula, and it is applied across modalities (vision, language, scene synthesis, and optimization tasks). KD delivers practical gains in inference speed, memory footprint, and often generalization or robustness when paired with complementary techniques (data augmentation, architecture design, and adversarial training), but its success depends on choices about what is transferred, how data are used or synthesized, and how teacher and student capacities are aligned.

papers_seen.author: Farrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Versatile Tool for Model Compression and Adaptation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable strategy for producing compact models that retain much of the accuracy, inductive bias, and robustness of larger teachers. Beyond simple logit-matching, KD encompasses feature- and layer-level alignment, self-distillation, many-to-many layer mapping, and data-aware or data-free workflows that together enable deployment under latency, memory, privacy, and domain-shift constraints. When combined with careful objectives, curriculum strategies, and task-aware layer mapping, KD can serve both as a primary compression mechanism and as a general-purpose training paradigm for regularization and adaptation. However, realizing its full value requires attention to teacher quality, data heterogeneity, and the choice of distilled signals to preserve robustness and generalization.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression methods aim to transfer performance and representational properties from large, expensive models to smaller, efficient ones. Across tasks in vision, language, graph learning, and generative modeling, researchers have developed strategies that extend beyond matching final logits: layer-wise and representation matching, many-to-many layer alignment, data-free distillation, private/distilled deployment, multi-teacher and self-distillation schemes, and task-adaptive compression. These approaches trade off fidelity, privacy, and computational cost, and they have been shown to enable real-world deployment of pretrained language models and other deep systems while revealing open challenges in distribution shift, heterogeneous data, and preserving inductive biases.

papers_seen.author: Bass
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach to producing small, fast models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. When combined with complementary techniques (e.g., layer mapping, multi-stage curricula, data augmentation, and hardware-aware compression), KD enables deployable NLP and deep-learning systems across constrained environments while admitting clear failure modes that demand targeted remedies.

papers_seen.author: Callahan
papers_seen.title: A Practical Position on Knowledge Distillation: Go Beyond Soft Labels
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a necessary tool for compressing large deep and NLP models into efficient students suitable for deployment. However, naive KD that only matches teacher soft-labels is often insufficient. Effective distillation combines richer knowledge targets (internal features, attention, and layerwise signals), data-aware augmentations, selective sample strategies, and privacy- or domain-aware procedures. The best practical pipelines treat KD as a toolbox: choose which knowledge to transfer based on student capacity and task needs, use augmentation or self-distillation to improve generalization when data are scarce, and apply selective or privacy-preserving queries where constraints require it.

papers_seen.author: Humphrey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Versatile Path to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) offers a pragmatic route to compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. Across modalities and tasks, KD can transfer predictive behavior, representations, or task-specific inductive biases; when combined with pre-training, architecture search, or careful data handling, it enables compact models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its effectiveness depends on the choice of what is distilled (logits vs. features), how teachers and students are chosen or trained, the availability and quality of data (including synthetic or unlabeled public data), and auxiliary techniques such as projectors, multi-teacher weighting, or meta-learning to adapt the teaching process. I argue that with these design choices attended to, KD is a broadly applicable and cost-effective strategy for model compression in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Mitigating Gender Bias in Distilled Language Models via Counterfactual Role Reversal
papers_seen.abstract: Language models excel at generating coherent text, and model compression techniques such as knowledge distillation have enabled their use in resource-constrained settings. However, these models can be biased in multiple ways, including the unfounded association of male and female genders with gender-neutral professions. Therefore, knowledge distillation without any fairness constraints may preserve or exaggerate the teacher model's biases onto the distilled model. To this end, we present a novel approach to mitigate gender disparity in text generation by learning a fair model during knowledge distillation. We propose two modifications to the base knowledge distillation based on counterfactual role reversal$\unicode{x2014}$modifying teacher probabilities and augmenting the training set. We evaluate gender polarity across professions in open-ended text generated from the resulting distilled and finetuned GPT$\unicode{x2012}$2 models and demonstrate a substantial reduction in gender disparity with only a minor compromise in utility. Finally, we observe that language models that reduce gender polarity in language generation do not improve embedding fairness or downstream classification fairness.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques reduce computation, memory and latency of large deep models by transferring information from high-capacity "teacher" models to smaller "student" models. A range of approaches have been developed: soft-target (logit) distillation, feature- and layer-wise matching, data-augmentation and data-free synthesis, multi-teacher and curriculum strategies, and teacher-aware or teacher-training modifications. These methods are applied across modalities (NLP, vision, multimodal) and settings (limited data, federated or resource-constrained deployments), and combine naturally with quantization and low-precision inference. Empirical and theoretical work shows gains arise both from conveying inter-class similarities (dark knowledge) and from the regularization effect of softened targets; more recent work focuses on selecting or synthesizing the most useful knowledge for a given student and task.

papers_seen.author: Donovan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Practical Compression: Essential, Effective, but Context-Sensitive
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students that retain much of teacher performance. KD can yield large speed, storage, and deployment gains across vision, speech, and language when combined with careful choices about what to transfer and how to train. However, success is not automatic: data regime, teacher-student mismatch, optimization dynamics, and downstream robustness or fairness constraints shape outcomes. I argue that KD should be treated as a core tool in model compression pipelines but one that must be adapted to the task, data availability, and deployment constraints through a set of best practices.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Trade-offs, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or ensemble knowledge. The approach spans simple logit/soft-label matching to feature- and layer-level objectives, multi-teacher pipelines, teacher-free variants, and combinations with architecture search, pruning and data-synthesis. Empirical and theoretical work shows distillation yields substantial efficiency gains with careful design, but also exposes limits from optimization, data heterogeneity, and capacity mismatch. Practical deployment therefore balances what to transfer, how to adapt the student architecture, and whether data or privacy constraints require specialized protocols.

papers_seen.author: Abbott
papers_seen.title: Compressing Deep Graph Neural Networks via Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep graph neural networks (GNNs) have been shown to be expressive for modeling graph-structured data. Nevertheless, the over-stacked architecture of deep graph models makes it difficult to deploy and rapidly test on mobile or embedded systems. To compress over-stacked GNNs, knowledge distillation via a teacher-student architecture turns out to be an effective technique, where the key step is to measure the discrepancy between teacher and student networks with predefined distance functions. However, using the same distance for graphs of various structures may be unfit, and the optimal distance formulation is hard to determine. To tackle these problems, we propose a novel Adversarial Knowledge Distillation framework for graph models named GraphAKD, which adversarially trains a discriminator and a generator to adaptively detect and decrease the discrepancy. Specifically, noticing that the well-captured inter-node and inter-class correlations favor the success of deep GNNs, we propose to criticize the inherited knowledge from node-level and class-level views with a trainable discriminator. The discriminator distinguishes between teacher knowledge and what the student inherits, while the student GNN works as a generator and aims to fool the discriminator. To our best knowledge, GraphAKD is the first to introduce adversarial training to knowledge distillation in graph domains. Experiments on node-level and graph-level classification benchmarks demonstrate that GraphAKD improves the student performance by a large margin. The results imply that GraphAKD can precisely transfer knowledge from a complicated teacher GNN to a compact student GNN.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: The Case for Versatile Knowledge Distillation: Compression, Adaptation, and Robustness in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical and flexible paradigm for transferring information from large, high-capacity models into smaller, more efficient ones. Beyond simple logit matching, distillation techniques can be adapted to operate without original training data, guide architecture search, improve generalization under limited data, support cross-modal and multi-task transfer, and preserve or even enhance downstream performance on specialized tasks. When combined with task-aware search, feature-level imitation, and data augmentation strategies, distillation enables deployment of compact models that remain competitive with their teachers while meeting real-world constraints such as privacy, compute, and latency.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Unifying Paradigm for Compression, Adaptation, and Robust Training
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be considered not merely as a compression trick but as a general and practical training paradigm. Across modalities and tasks, KD transfers information about function, structure, and uncertainty from one model (or ensemble) to another, enabling smaller, faster, or more adaptable models while improving generalization, interpretability, and domain transfer. Success depends on how teacher knowledge is selected, represented, and combined with data-side techniques; thoughtful design choices (layer mapping, sample selection, augmentation, and teacher trust) determine whether KD yields compression, robustness, or better task-specific performance.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Beyond Soft Labels: A Practical Position on Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a crucial technique for shrinking large deep models to meet real-world latency, memory and privacy constraints while retaining much of their performance. However, naive distillation that only matches teacher soft-labels is often insufficient. A more reliable strategy combines distillation of internal representations and features, task- or domain-adaptive compression, and architecture-aware search or adaptation. When applied with care — addressing optimization issues, data or privacy limits, and mismatch between teacher and student capacities — distillation enables compact, fast models that approach teacher performance across speech, NLP and vision tasks.

papers_seen.author: Cameron
papers_seen.title: Well-Read Students Learn Better: On the Importance of Pre-training Compact Models
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in natural language representations have been accompanied by large and expensive models that leverage vast amounts of general-domain text through self-supervised pre-training. Due to the cost of applying such models to down-stream tasks, several model compression techniques on pre-trained language representations have been proposed (Sun et al., 2019; Sanh, 2019). However, surprisingly, the simple baseline of just pre-training and fine-tuning compact models has been overlooked. In this paper, we first show that pre-training remains important in the context of smaller architectures, and fine-tuning pre-trained compact models can be competitive to more elaborate methods proposed in concurrent work. Starting with pre-trained compact models, we then explore transferring task knowledge from large fine-tuned models through standard knowledge distillation. The resulting simple, yet effective and general algorithm, Pre-trained Distillation, brings further improvements. Through extensive experiments, we more generally explore the interaction between pre-training and distillation under two variables that have been under-studied: model size and properties of unlabeled task data. One surprising observation is that they have a compound effect even when sequentially applied on the same data. To accelerate future research, we will make our 24 pre-trained miniature BERT models publicly available.

papers_seen.author: Bass
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach to producing small, fast models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. When combined with complementary techniques (e.g., layer mapping, multi-stage curricula, data augmentation, and hardware-aware compression), KD enables deployable NLP and deep-learning systems across constrained environments while admitting clear failure modes that demand targeted remedies.

papers_seen.author: Duncan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practically essential approach for compressing large neural models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. By transferring learned behavior from teachers to students, KD enables many deployment trade-offs while remaining compatible with complementary techniques (e.g., quantization, pruning, architecture search). However, to be robust and broadly useful in real systems, distillation must go beyond naive soft-label matching: effective pipelines combine logits with internal representation transfer, task- and layer-aware selection of signals, appropriate data strategies, and attention to distributional heterogeneity and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity models into smaller, faster models by transferring learned behavior from a teacher to a student. Techniques range from matching soft outputs to mimicking internal representations, and they address goals including latency reduction, domain adaptation, privacy, and scalability. Recent work expands classical teacher-student pipelines with self-distillation, data-free approaches, ensemble-to-singleton transfer, and scalable online schemes, while theoretical analyses reframe distillation as a form of label smoothing and regularization. Practical deployments show that careful choice of distilled signal (logits, features, attention, or ensembles) and training protocols can yield compact models that approach or match teacher performance in many settings, but open issues remain around low-frequency token handling, domain shift, and privacy-aware data constraints.

papers_seen.author: Chapman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster students by transferring useful predictive behavior, representations, or inductive biases. A diverse set of distillation strategies—matching soft logits, aligning intermediate features or attention maps, self-distillation, multi-teacher schemes, data-free synthesis, and task-aware adaptations—has been developed to preserve performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Practice-oriented work emphasizes matching the distillation technique to the task, addressing data or privacy limits via synthetic examples or adversarial generation, and combining distillation with architecture and optimization adjustments to close remaining gaps. Empirical successes across language, vision, speech, graphs, and ranking systems show substantial speed and size improvements, though limits remain around distribution shift, teacher–student mismatch, and heterogeneous or federated data settings.

papers_seen.author: Rocha
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Trends
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques aim to transfer predictive power from large teacher models into smaller, faster, or more private student models while retaining most of the original performance. Work across vision and language has expanded KD beyond simple logit matching into data-centric methods (augmentation and mixup), layer- and representation-level transfers, task-adaptive architecture search, data-free and privacy-aware distillation, and unified pipelines that combine pruning or structural compression with distillation. The field blends empirical engineering (speed/size trade-offs) with emerging theoretical analyses that help explain when and why distillation helps.

papers_seen.author: Walls
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large or ensemble teacher models into smaller student models. Across vision, language, graphs, and multimodal problems, KD is used alone or combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data-centric strategies to produce compact models that preserve much of teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. Empirical and analytical work highlights mechanisms behind KD’s success, practical recipes for improving student fidelity, and persistent challenges (data mismatch, rare-token behavior, robustness, and optimization). This synthesis summarizes methods, applications, practical recommendations, and key open problems reported in recent literature.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Show, Attend and Distill:Knowledge Distillation via Attention-based Feature Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation extracts general knowledge from a pre-trained teacher network and provides guidance to a target student network. Most studies manually tie intermediate features of the teacher and student, and transfer knowledge through pre-defined links. However, manual selection often constructs ineffective links that limit the improvement from the distillation. There has been an attempt to address the problem, but it is still challenging to identify effective links under practical scenarios. In this paper, we introduce an effective and efficient feature distillation method utilizing all the feature levels of the teacher without manually selecting the links. Specifically, our method utilizes an attention-based meta-network that learns relative similarities between features, and applies identified similarities to control distillation intensities of all possible pairs. As a result, our method determines competent links more efficiently than the previous approach and provides better performance on model compression and transfer learning tasks. Further qualitative analyses and ablative studies describe how our method contributes to better distillation. The implementation code is available at github.com/clovaai/attention-feature-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Farmer
papers_seen.title: Towards Efficient 3D Object Detection with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite substantial progress in 3D object detection, advanced 3D detectors often suffer from heavy computation overheads. To this end, we explore the potential of knowledge distillation (KD) for developing efficient 3D object detectors, focusing on popular pillar- and voxel-based detectors.In the absence of well-developed teacher-student pairs, we first study how to obtain student models with good trade offs between accuracy and efficiency from the perspectives of model compression and input resolution reduction. Then, we build a benchmark to assess existing KD methods developed in the 2D domain for 3D object detection upon six well-constructed teacher-student pairs. Further, we propose an improved KD pipeline incorporating an enhanced logit KD method that performs KD on only a few pivotal positions determined by teacher classification response, and a teacher-guided student model initialization to facilitate transferring teacher model's feature extraction ability to students through weight inheritance. Finally, we conduct extensive experiments on the Waymo dataset. Our best performing model achieves $65.75\%$ LEVEL 2 mAPH, surpassing its teacher model and requiring only $44\%$ of teacher flops. Our most efficient model runs 51 FPS on an NVIDIA A100, which is $2.2\times$ faster than PointPillar with even higher accuracy. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/CVMI-Lab/SparseKD}.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Confidence-Aware Multi-Teacher Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is initially introduced to utilize additional supervision from a single teacher model for the student model training. To boost the student performance, some recent variants attempt to exploit diverse knowledge sources from multiple teachers. However, existing studies mainly integrate knowledge from diverse sources by averaging over multiple teacher predictions or combining them using other various label-free strategies, which may mislead student in the presence of low-quality teacher predictions. To tackle this problem, we propose Confidence-Aware Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (CA-MKD), which adaptively assigns sample-wise reliability for each teacher prediction with the help of ground-truth labels, with those teacher predictions close to one-hot labels assigned large weights. Besides, CA-MKD incorporates intermediate layers to stable the knowledge transfer process. Extensive experiments show that our CA-MKD consistently outperforms all compared state-of-the-art methods across various teacher-student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques have matured into a diverse set of approaches that trade off capacity, latency, and privacy to deploy high-performing deep models in constrained settings. Methods operate at different places in the training pipeline: compressing via soft-targets, transferring intermediate representations, searching or adapting compact architectures, or avoiding access to original data. Work across modalities (vision, language, graphs, generative models, and medical imaging) shows that careful choice of what to transfer (logits, relations, feature directions, layer mappings) and how to transfer it (attention, contrastive alignment, adversarial generators, or task-aware filters) determines final student performance. Practical concerns such as domain adaptation, federated and heterogeneous-device settings, and data augmentation interact strongly with distillation design choices. The literature suggests a clear pattern: representation-level and layer-aware transfers often outperform naive logits-only approaches for structured or pre-trained models, while teacher-free, data-free, and communication-efficient variants enable distillation under realistic deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Gaines
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques enable smaller or more efficient models to approach the performance of larger teacher models by transferring information through supervisory signals beyond standard hard labels. Across computer vision, speech, and NLP, practitioners apply soft-label distillation, feature- and layer-level imitation, self- and online-distillation, data-free methods, and structural transformations (e.g., pruning or cheap-convolution replacements) to trade off accuracy, latency, and memory for deployability. Empirical work shows strong task-specific gains (often recovering much of the teacher’s quality) while recent methodological and theoretical studies clarify when and why different forms of distillation help. Open challenges remain in data scarcity or privacy, matching features across heterogeneous architectures, and designing distillation schedules that manage regularization versus bias. The literature suggests combined approaches—mixing logits, intermediate features, architectural compression, and distributed or data-free strategies—are effective practical pathways for producing compact, high-performing models for real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Owens
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses capability from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. It encompasses methods that transfer final outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure, or training curricula, and it is applied across modalities (vision, language, scene synthesis, and optimization tasks). KD delivers practical gains in inference speed, memory footprint, and often generalization or robustness when paired with complementary techniques (data augmentation, architecture design, and adversarial training), but its success depends on choices about what is transferred, how data are used or synthesized, and how teacher and student capacities are aligned.

papers_seen.author: Decker
papers_seen.title: Practical and Principled Knowledge Distillation for Compressing NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature and versatile approach for compressing large deep learning and NLP models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of the teacher’s performance. Effective compression in practice requires matching the distillation technique to the deployment objective: using self-distillation or multi-teacher strategies to extract richer supervisory signals, combining KD with architecture search or pruning for task-specific efficiency, applying appropriate soft/hard label mixing informed by bias–variance tradeoffs, and controlling data and privacy considerations during distillation. When these elements are combined, KD can deliver substantial runtime and memory savings with minimal accuracy loss, making it central to deploying modern NLP systems under resource constraints.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Insights, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large models into smaller, faster ones by transferring information from a teacher to a student. It has been applied across supervised, self-supervised, multimodal and domain-adaptation settings to reduce inference cost while retaining much of the teacher's performance. Progress includes direct soft-target matching, feature- and relation-based imitation, self- and progressive-distillation strategies, and task- or domain-aware adaptations. Empirical work highlights both the power of KD to produce efficient models for deployment and important practical considerations—such as the value of pre-training, the role of data augmentation and sample selection, and computational bottlenecks—that shape effective distillation regimes. Despite advances, optimization mismatches, teacher–student capacity differences, and data-domain shift remain active challenges guiding current research and practice.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: A Deep Hierarchical Approach to Lifelong Learning in Minecraft
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a lifelong learning system that has the ability to reuse and transfer knowledge from one task to another while efficiently retaining the previously learned knowledge-base. Knowledge is transferred by learning reusable skills to solve tasks in Minecraft, a popular video game which is an unsolved and high-dimensional lifelong learning problem. These reusable skills, which we refer to as Deep Skill Networks, are then incorporated into our novel Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning Network (H-DRLN) architecture using two techniques: (1) a deep skill array and (2) skill distillation, our novel variation of policy distillation (Rusu et. al. 2015) for learning skills. Skill distillation enables the HDRLN to efficiently retain knowledge and therefore scale in lifelong learning, by accumulating knowledge and encapsulating multiple reusable skills into a single distilled network. The H-DRLN exhibits superior performance and lower learning sample complexity compared to the regular Deep Q Network (Mnih et. al. 2015) in sub-domains of Minecraft.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a heuristic for compressing large models into a broadly applicable set of techniques that enable smaller, faster, and in some cases fairer or more interpretable models. Its effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer (logits, features, structure), how to prepare training data, and how to reconcile teacher imperfections with student capacity. When these design choices are matched to the task and constraints, KD enables substantial compression with small performance loss and can address privacy and resource limitations.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Compressing GANs using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been used in several machine learning tasks such as domain transfer, super resolution, and synthetic data generation. State-of-the-art GANs often use tens of millions of parameters, making them expensive to deploy for applications in low SWAP (size, weight, and power) hardware, such as mobile devices, and for applications with real time capabilities. There has been no work found to reduce the number of parameters used in GANs. Therefore, we propose a method to compress GANs using knowledge distillation techniques, in which a smaller "student" GAN learns to mimic a larger "teacher" GAN. We show that the distillation methods used on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and Celeb-A datasets can compress teacher GANs at ratios of 1669:1, 58:1, and 87:1, respectively, while retaining the quality of the generated image. From our experiments, we observe a qualitative limit for GAN's compression. Moreover, we observe that, with a fixed parameter budget, compressed GANs outperform GANs trained using standard training methods. We conjecture that this is partially owing to the optimization landscape of over-parameterized GANs which allows efficient training using alternating gradient descent. Thus, training an over-parameterized GAN followed by our proposed compression scheme provides a high quality generative model with a small number of parameters.

papers_seen.author: Bowman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger, expensive models (teachers) to smaller, efficient models (students). KD has been applied across vision, language, generative modeling, and privacy-sensitive settings to reduce storage, latency, and energy while attempting to preserve accuracy and desirable properties. Practical approaches range from soft-label matching and feature imitation to many-to-many layer mappings and self-distillation; theoretical work links KD to regularization effects and label smoothing. Despite clear empirical successes in compressing large pretrained language models and vision networks, important challenges remain: students often fail to replicate teachers' internal representations, robustness and fairness do not automatically transfer, and privacy or heterogeneous-data settings impose additional constraints. Ongoing advances focus on richer targets (internal features, layer mappings), alternate training regimes (self- and teacher-free distillation), and task-aware strategies for robust and private compression.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Improving the Interpretability of Deep Neural Networks with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep Neural Networks have achieved huge success at a wide spectrum of applications from language modeling, computer vision to speech recognition. However, nowadays, good performance alone is not sufficient to satisfy the needs of practical deployment where interpretability is demanded for cases involving ethics and mission critical applications. The complex models of Deep Neural Networks make it hard to understand and reason the predictions, which hinders its further progress. To tackle this problem, we apply the Knowledge Distillation technique to distill Deep Neural Networks into decision trees in order to attain good performance and interpretability simultaneously. We formulate the problem at hand as a multi-output regression problem and the experiments demonstrate that the student model achieves significantly better accuracy performance (about 1\% to 5\%) than vanilla decision trees at the same level of tree depth. The experiments are implemented on the TensorFlow platform to make it scalable to big datasets. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to distill Deep Neural Networks into vanilla decision trees on multi-class datasets.

papers_seen.author: Allison
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable ones by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from teacher models to students. The field has diversified from logits-only matching to richer targets (intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals), multiple training regimes (data-free, online, federated, multi-teacher), and task-aware techniques that address capacity mismatch and deployment constraints. KD is widely applicable across modalities (vision, speech, multimodal, graphs, NLP) and is most effective when combined with data- and architecture-aware practices, but practical limits remain around representation alignment, rare-token behavior, privacy, and domain transfer.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Highlight Every Step: Knowledge Distillation via Collaborative Teaching
papers_seen.abstract: High storage and computational costs obstruct deep neural networks to be deployed on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation aims to train a compact student network by transferring knowledge from a larger pre-trained teacher model. However, most existing methods on knowledge distillation ignore the valuable information among training process associated with training results. In this paper, we provide a new Collaborative Teaching Knowledge Distillation (CTKD) strategy which employs two special teachers. Specifically, one teacher trained from scratch (i.e., scratch teacher) assists the student step by step using its temporary outputs. It forces the student to approach the optimal path towards the final logits with high accuracy. The other pre-trained teacher (i.e., expert teacher) guides the student to focus on a critical region which is more useful for the task. The combination of the knowledge from two special teachers can significantly improve the performance of the student network in knowledge distillation. The results of experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN and Tiny ImageNet datasets verify that the proposed knowledge distillation method is efficient and achieves state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge distillation from multi-modal to mono-modal segmentation networks
papers_seen.abstract: The joint use of multiple imaging modalities for medical image segmentation has been widely studied in recent years. The fusion of information from different modalities has demonstrated to improve the segmentation accuracy, with respect to mono-modal segmentations, in several applications. However, acquiring multiple modalities is usually not possible in a clinical setting due to a limited number of physicians and scanners, and to limit costs and scan time. Most of the time, only one modality is acquired. In this paper, we propose KD-Net, a framework to transfer knowledge from a trained multi-modal network (teacher) to a mono-modal one (student). The proposed method is an adaptation of the generalized distillation framework where the student network is trained on a subset (1 modality) of the teacher's inputs (n modalities). We illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in brain tumor segmentation with the BraTS 2018 dataset. Using different architectures, we show that the student network effectively learns from the teacher and always outperforms the baseline mono-modal network in terms of segmentation accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Montoya
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of methods for transferring behavior from large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster student models so they can be deployed under real-world constraints. Approaches vary in what is transferred (soft outputs, internal features, attention maps, module behavior), whether distillation is offline, online, or federated, and how it is combined with architecture search, pruning, or privacy mechanisms. Empirically, KD routinely improves compact models over training from scratch and enables deployments across on-device, distributed, and data-scarce settings; however, practical success depends on aligning distillation signals to student capacity, handling imperfect or heterogeneous teachers, and addressing data and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Harrell
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques have become central tools to deploy high-capacity deep models in latency-, memory-, privacy-, and compute-constrained settings. Across vision, language, graph, and multimodal domains, practitioners use teacher-student training, feature-level transfer, data-free distillation, and hybrid pipelines that combine pruning or architecture search with distillation. Work in this area balances fidelity to teacher models, robustness, and efficiency, and explores trade-offs such as reliance on original training data, communication overhead in federated settings, and the benefits of designing students or student-friendly teachers. The literature shows repeated success of KD when tailored to the task and constraints, while also revealing limitations under severe data heterogeneity or adversarial settings.

papers_seen.author: Bush
papers_seen.title: Multi-Label Image Classification via Knowledge Distillation from Weakly-Supervised Detection
papers_seen.abstract: Multi-label image classification is a fundamental but challenging task towards general visual understanding. Existing methods found the region-level cues (e.g., features from RoIs) can facilitate multi-label classification. Nevertheless, such methods usually require laborious object-level annotations (i.e., object labels and bounding boxes) for effective learning of the object-level visual features. In this paper, we propose a novel and efficient deep framework to boost multi-label classification by distilling knowledge from weakly-supervised detection task without bounding box annotations. Specifically, given the image-level annotations, (1) we first develop a weakly-supervised detection (WSD) model, and then (2) construct an end-to-end multi-label image classification framework augmented by a knowledge distillation module that guides the classification model by the WSD model according to the class-level predictions for the whole image and the object-level visual features for object RoIs. The WSD model is the teacher model and the classification model is the student model. After this cross-task knowledge distillation, the performance of the classification model is significantly improved and the efficiency is maintained since the WSD model can be safely discarded in the test phase. Extensive experiments on two large-scale datasets (MS-COCO and NUS-WIDE) show that our framework achieves superior performances over the state-of-the-art methods on both performance and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques have become central tools for reducing the computational and memory footprint of large neural networks while retaining much of their performance. Work in this area has diversified beyond the original teacher-to-student soft-label matching to include self-distillation, online and distributed distillation, feature- and representation-level transfer, multi-teacher selection, and data-augmentation-aware distillation. These methods are applied across modalities (vision, speech, NLP, and graphs) and contexts (domain adaptation, continual learning, large-scale training, and on-device deployment), yielding a range of practical trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and model size. Current advances emphasize richer forms of knowledge (internal representations, relational signals), adaptive teacher weighting, and training-time strategies that improve student generalization, but challenges remain in reliably transferring rare-word or low-frequency behavior, aligning heterogeneous architectures, and scaling distillation to extremely large datasets and models.
